policies.name: Hours of Work, Overtime & Timekeeping
policies.owner: Total Rewards (classification) and Global Payroll (timekeeping and overtime pay)
policies.review: Annual + each 1 January threshold change + on law change
policies.audience: All employees; mandatory for non-exempt (US), ESA-covered (Canada), 'worker'-category (India), LSA-covered (Taiwan) and all mainland China staff, and for managers who approve time
policies.purpose: Make sure every role is classified correctly for hours and overtime under the law of the place where the work is done, that all time worked is recorded and paid, and that working-time limits are respected. The highest-risk groups are lab technicians, test operators and support staff, and engineers in jurisdictions with no salary-based exemption (Taiwan, mainland China, India 'workers').
keyProvisions: Total Rewards sets the classification for each job code and work location and records it in Darwinbox: exempt or non-exempt (US), ESA-exempt or not (Canada), 'worker' or managerial (India), LSA-covered or Art. 84-1 (Taiwan), and standard, comprehensive or flexible hours (China). Title and salary alone never decide classification.

A US exemption requires both the duties test and the higher of the federal salary level ($684/week; HCE $107,432) or the state level. In California that is $70,304 (2026) or $72,384 (2027), or for computer professionals $58.85/hour ($122,573.13/year in 2026).

Non-exempt employees and all Taiwan and mainland China staff must record their actual start, end and break times in the timekeeping system every day (in Taiwan, to the minute). This includes remote work, after-hours calls with other time zones, required travel and training.
Off-the-clock work is prohibited. Managers may not request or allow unrecorded work. Only Payroll may edit a time record, and only with a documented reason that the employee can see.

Managers pre-approve overtime where practicable. All overtime actually worked is paid at the legally required premium even if it was not approved. Unauthorized overtime is handled as a conduct issue and never by withholding pay.

Overtime premiums follow local law: US FLSA 1.5x over 40 hours a week; California daily 1.5x and 2x; Ontario 1.5x after 44 hours a week; BC 1.5x after 8 hours a day or 40 a week and 2x after 12 hours a day; India 'workers' 2x; Taiwan +1/3 and +2/3 tiers plus rest-day and holiday rules; China 150%, 200% and 300%.

Working-time caps are hard limits. Taiwan: 12 hours a day and 46 overtime hours a month (54 a month and 138 per 3 months with labor-management-meeting consent). China: 36 overtime hours a month. India: OSH Code and state rules (Karnataka 24x7: 10 hours a day including overtime and 50 overtime hours a quarter). Company-wide: an RBA ceiling of 60 hours a week including overtime and one day off in seven, except in genuine emergencies.

Meal and rest breaks follow local law. Examples: California requires a 30-minute meal before the end of the 5th hour, 10 minutes' rest per 4 hours, and one hour of premium pay for each day a break is missed; Taiwan requires 30 minutes after 4 hours and 11 hours between shifts.
The regular rate includes non-discretionary bonuses, shift differentials and on-call pay where the law requires. Payroll must approve any new lab shift or on-call rota before it launches.

Alternative or special schedules are used only after the election, consent or government approval they require: California alternative workweek elections and DLSE filing, Taiwan flexible-hours schemes and Art. 84-1 agreements, China comprehensive or flexible hours approval.

Payroll reports the FLSA overtime premium separately in W-2 Box 12, code TT, from tax year 2026. Time records are kept for at least 3 years in the US (timecards 2), 5 years in Taiwan, and as local law requires elsewhere.
Canadian engineering staff code their time to projects to support SR&ED claims. This project coding does not change an exempt role to hourly.

Employees may raise pay or timekeeping concerns with their manager, HR or the Speak Up line without retaliation. Improper deductions from exempt salary are reimbursed under the 29 CFR 541.603 safe harbor.
policies.sampleLanguage: Recording and paying for all time worked. [Company] pays for all time worked. If your role is classified as non-exempt, or you work in Taiwan or mainland China, record your actual start and end times, meal breaks and any overtime in [Timekeeping System] each day. This includes calls with colleagues in other time zones, work done remotely, and required training or travel. Do not work 'off the clock', and do not ask anyone else to. Managers must approve overtime in advance whenever practicable. However, all overtime you actually work will be paid at the rate required by local law, even if it was not approved. Working unapproved overtime may lead to corrective action, but it will never result in unpaid time. Only Payroll may change a time record, and only with a documented reason that you can see. Total Rewards decides your classification based on your duties, pay and work location, not your job title. If you believe your time or pay is wrong, or you were asked to work without recording it, contact [Payroll/HR] or the Speak Up line. [Company] prohibits retaliation for raising these concerns.

roles.duties: Record accurate time every day, get approval for overtime where practicable, and report any request to work off the clock or any pay error.

Review and approve timesheets before payroll closes, plan work within the hours caps, and never discourage employees from recording time or contact them after hours without an approved overtime or on-call arrangement.
Classify every job code by country, review classifications whenever thresholds or duties change, and document the exemption analysis for Legal.
Calculate premiums and the regular rate, report W-2 code TT, audit time edits, and keep records for the statutory periods.
Approve exemption positions, alternative schedules and government filings (Taiwan Art. 84-1, China special hours, California AWS).
In Taiwan, the labor-management meeting (or union) consents to overtime above standard caps and to flexible schedules. In China, the union is consulted on overtime.

countryAddenda.us: FLSA plus state law: pay the highest applicable minimum wage for the work location, apply state daily overtime (e.g., AK, NV, CO) and the higher state exempt thresholds (e.g., NY, WA, CO; verify current figures). Track the FLSA overtime premium separately for W-2 code TT from 2026. Keep payroll records 3 years and timecards 2 years (29 CFR 516). Remote non-exempt staff follow their work state's meal and rest rules (e.g., WA, OR, CO, NY).
countryAddenda.us-ca: Add IWC Wage Order 4 terms: daily overtime (1.5x after 8 hours, 2x after 12, plus 7th-day rules); meal and rest periods with automatic premium pay (LC 226.7, 512); alternative workweeks only after a secret-ballot election and DLSE filing; and the local minimum wage of the actual work location (e.g., Sunnyvale $19.50, Mountain View $19.70 in 2026). The exempt floor is $70,304 (2026) and $72,384 (2027), and the computer-professional rate is $58.85/hr. Lab technicians and test or fab operators are presumed non-exempt.
countryAddenda.ca: Ontario: maximum 8 hours a day and 48 a week unless agreed in writing, and overtime at 1.5x after 44 hours a week. IT professionals are exempt from the hours and overtime rules (O. Reg. 285/01). BC: 1.5x after 8 hours a day or 40 a week and 2x after 12 hours a day. 'High technology professionals' are exempt under ESR s.37.8. Confirm every exemption role by role, because technicians, test operators and admin staff usually do not qualify.
countryAddenda.in: Identify 'workers': everyone except managerial or administrative staff and supervisors earning over INR 18,000/month. Workers are limited to 8 hours a day and 48 a week, with overtime only by consent at twice the ordinary rate (OSH Code s.27; Code on Wages s.14) and a central cap of 144 overtime hours a quarter. Karnataka offices on the 24x7 notification (valid to Sep 2027) are limited to 10 hours a day including overtime and 50 overtime hours a quarter, with a rotating weekly off and women's night-work consent and transport. Keep electronic attendance and overtime registers.
countryAddenda.tw: The LSA covers almost everyone: there is no salary-based exemption, and Art. 84-1 applies only to MOL-designated roles with an approved written agreement. Record attendance to the minute (LSA Art. 30; keep 5 years); under the Labor Incident Act, recorded time is presumed to be working time. Get labor-management-meeting consent for overtime above 46 hours a month (caps of 54 a month and 138 per 3 months) and file it with the authority if there are 30+ employees. Pay the premium or give comp time, whichever the employee chooses, and pay out unused comp time.
countryAddenda.cn: Standard hours are 8 a day and 40 a week. Overtime is allowed only after consulting the union and the employee, normally up to 1 hour a day (3 in special cases) and 36 hours a month, and is paid at 150% on workdays, 200% on rest days (or time off) and 300% on holidays (Labor Law Arts. 41, 44). Comprehensive or flexible hours for shift, FAE or senior roles need local HR bureau approval first. The overtime base is the contractual monthly wage divided by 21.75 (daily) or 174 (hourly), and in Shanghai it is defined by the wage payment measures effective 1 Aug 2026.

decisions: Classify US design and verification engineers under the learned-professional exemption or the computer-professional exemption? (Learned professional fits hardware design. Computer professional suits software, firmware and EDA roles, but in California it needs $58.85/hr. Mixed roles need a documented duties analysis.)

Pay lab technicians hourly or as salaried non-exempt? (Salaried non-exempt simplifies pay but still needs time records and regular-rate calculations. Hourly is cleaner for California daily overtime and meal/rest premiums.)

Make overtime pre-approval mandatory or advisory? (Mandatory approval controls cost but must never lead to unpaid time. Advisory approval is easier during tape-out crunches but weakens budget control.)
Use minute-level timekeeping for all APAC and Canadian engineers, or only where the law requires it? (Uniform tooling reduces errors and helps SR&ED evidence, but adds friction in India and Canada.)

Seek Taiwan Art. 84-1 or China comprehensive/flexible-hours approval for FAEs and senior engineers? (It reduces overtime exposure but needs regulator approval, written agreements and continuing health protections.)

Adopt a company-wide 60-hour weekly ceiling (RBA) with a documented exception process for tape-outs and customer escalations? (Ready for customer audits, but needs monitoring and VP-level exception approval.)
Pay for late-evening cross-time-zone calls as overtime, or redesign meeting windows? (Paying is compliant but costly. Rotating core meeting windows cuts both cost and burnout.)
pitfalls: Treating all engineers as exempt everywhere. Taiwan has no salary exemption, China needs government approval for special hours, Indian individual contributors may be 'workers', and California technicians often fail the salary or duties test.
Using the federal $684/week level as the US test when state thresholds (CA, NY, WA, CO) are much higher.
Leaving non-discretionary bonuses, shift differentials and on-call pay out of the regular rate, so overtime is underpaid.
Letting after-hours Slack or Teams work with US HQ go unrecorded. In Taiwan, recorded or provable time is presumed to be working time, and in California small daily tasks add up to PAGA exposure.
Informally 'banking' hours or docking pay instead of paying overtime or following the statutory comp-time rules.
Running 24x7 lab shifts in Bengaluru or Shanghai without meeting the Karnataka 24x7 conditions or getting China comprehensive-hours approval.
policies.training: Managers of non-exempt or hours-regulated staff: timekeeping and overtime training on appointment and every year. Employees: acknowledgment at hire and on material change. Payroll: annual refresher on the regular rate and W-2 reporting.

policies.name: Expense Reimbursement & Remote-Work Stipends
policies.audience: All employees; contractors only as their contract provides
policies.purpose: Reimburse necessary business expenses promptly and in a tax-compliant way. Set remote-work stipends that meet statutory reimbursement duties such as California Labor Code 2802 rather than replacing them. Stop expense channels from being used for bribery, sanctions or payroll leakage.
keyProvisions: [Company] reimburses reasonable and necessary expenses employees incur as a direct result of doing their job. This includes approved travel, required equipment and, for remote or hybrid staff, a reasonable share of personal phone and internet costs.

Claims are submitted in the expense tool within 60 days of the expense, with itemized receipts for lodging and for any item of US$75 or more (or the local equivalent). Excess advances are returned within 120 days (IRS accountable-plan standards applied globally).
The manager approves every claim. Claims over US$5,000, any exception to this policy and all executive-officer claims need second-level approval (VP, or the CFO for executive officers).
Approved claims are paid within 30 days. Outstanding reimbursements are settled with final pay.

Remote-work stipends are set by country band to cover typical phone, internet and home-office consumable costs. Where the law requires full reimbursement (e.g., California), the stipend is a floor: employees may claim documented costs above it.
Company-provided laptops and peripherals remain [Company] property and are returned at exit. A one-time home-office equipment allowance, if offered, is paid through payroll and taxed where required.
Stipends and allowances are taxable wages unless local law provides an exclusion. Reimbursements under an accountable plan, or supported by local tax invoices, are not wages.
Local tax documents are mandatory for reimbursement: India GST invoices, China fapiao, Taiwan uniform invoices and US receipts meeting IRS substantiation rules.

The following are not reimbursed: personal items, traffic and parking fines, spouse or family travel unless pre-approved (then taxable, and tracked as a perquisite for executive officers), or travel involving comprehensively sanctioned countries or regions.

Gifts, meals, travel or hospitality for government officials, employees of state-owned customers or foundries, or their relatives need Ethics & Compliance pre-approval and must be recorded in the gifts and hospitality register.
Corporate cards are for business use only. Personal charges must be repaid within 30 days and are recovered only in ways local wage law permits.

[Company] does not deduct unreturned equipment, advances or disallowed expenses from wages without written authorization that complies with local law. It never makes such deductions from California final pay.
Finance audits a risk-based sample every quarter. Falsified or inflated claims are serious misconduct and may be referred under the Code of Conduct.
policies.sampleLanguage: Business expenses and remote-work support. [Company] will reimburse you for reasonable and necessary expenses you incur in doing your job, including approved travel, required equipment and, if you work remotely or hybrid, a reasonable share of your personal mobile phone and internet costs. Submit claims in [Expense Tool] within 60 days with itemized receipts; your manager will review them, and approved amounts are paid within 30 days. If you receive the monthly remote-work stipend for your country, it is intended to cover typical costs. If your actual necessary costs are higher and you work in a location where the law requires full reimbursement, you may submit documentation for the difference. Stipends are generally taxable; reimbursements supported by receipts generally are not. Expenses involving government officials or employees of state-owned companies require prior approval from Ethics & Compliance. [Company] will never make deductions from your pay for equipment, advances or disallowed claims unless you have authorized it in writing and the deduction is permitted by law.

roles.duties: Submit accurate, timely claims with compliant receipts and return company equipment and unused advances.
Review claims for business purpose and reasonableness within 5 business days, and escalate hospitality involving officials or state-owned entities.
Run the accountable plan, set receipt and card controls, audit samples quarterly and keep the tax documentation.
Set and review country stipend bands each year against actual cost data and legal reimbursement duties.
Pre-approve hospitality for officials and state-owned-entity staff, keep the gifts register, and screen sanctions-related travel with Trade Compliance.
Process taxable stipends and allowances, and make sure any recovery through payroll has lawful written authorization.

countryAddenda.us: Operate an IRS accountable plan (business connection, substantiation within a reasonable period, return of excess) so reimbursements are excluded from wages; flat stipends are taxable wages. Some states besides California require reimbursement of necessary expenses (e.g., IL 820 ILCS 115/9.5; verify others). Unreimbursed required costs must not take non-exempt pay below the minimum wage (29 CFR 531.35).
countryAddenda.us-ca: Labor Code 2802 requires reimbursement of all necessary business expenses, and the right cannot be waived (LC 2804). For remote and hybrid staff this includes a reasonable percentage of personal phone and internet costs even on unlimited plans (Cochran v. Schwan's, 2014), as well as mileage and necessary home-office equipment. A stipend is lawful only if it fully covers actual expenses, so employees must be able to claim any shortfall, and a policy deadline cannot extinguish a valid claim. Pay outstanding reimbursements with final pay.
countryAddenda.ca: Reimbursing employer-required costs is generally not taxable, while allowances and stipends are taxable employment income unless a CRA exception applies (verify the treatment of home-office equipment and internet). Deductions from wages to recover advances or card balances need written authorization (ON ESA s.13; BC ESA ss.21-22). Quebec remote staff need the policy in French.
countryAddenda.in: Under the default new tax regime most allowances are taxable. Reimbursements supported by bills for official purposes are generally not income (verify under the Income-tax Act 2025). Require GST-compliant invoices, and limit any recovery from wages to authorised deductions within the 50% cap (Code on Wages s.18). Check whether fixed allowances count toward the 50% 'wages' calculation.
countryAddenda.tw: A fixed monthly phone or remote-work allowance paid regularly may be treated as 'wages' for severance and overtime-base calculations (verify), so make true reimbursements against uniform invoices where possible. Pre-deducting damages or disallowed claims from wages is prohibited (LSA Art. 26).
countryAddenda.cn: Require official fapiao for reimbursement and corporate deductibility. Fixed communication or transport allowances are taxable wages for IIT, and local exempt caps vary (verify). Shanghai's 2026 wage measures exclude meal, transport and housing allowances from the overtime base. Deductions for employee-caused loss are capped at 20% of monthly wage and may not take pay below the minimum wage.

decisions: Pay remote staff a stipend or reimburse actual costs? (A stipend is simple and scales but is taxable and must fully cover actual cost in California. Actual-cost reimbursement is exact but more work to administer.)
One global stipend or country bands? (Bands reflect local cost. A single figure is simpler but overpays in India and underpays in the Bay Area.)

Provide company-owned home-office equipment that is returned at exit, or pay a one-time allowance the employee keeps? (Owned assets protect data and can be recovered. Allowances avoid logistics but are taxable.)
Set the receipt threshold and claim deadline (e.g., US$75 and 60 days)? (Tighter deadlines help accruals, but in California they cannot cut off a statutory 2802 claim.)
Allow business-class travel above a flight-duration threshold (e.g., 8 hours), and require pre-trip approval for Tier 2 destinations?
Set a value threshold for pre-approving hospitality for employees of state-owned customers or foundries? (A zero threshold is easiest to audit but adds friction for FAE and sales teams.)
pitfalls: Paying California remote staff a flat stipend that does not cover actual costs, or rejecting late California claims outright.
Treating stipends and home-office allowances as non-taxable.
Deducting unreturned laptops or card balances from final pay without lawful written authorization.
Using expense reports to entertain government or SOE-linked customers without a compliance review, which creates FCPA books-and-records exposure.
Accepting claims without fapiao or GST invoices, which loses deductibility and hides fraud.
policies.training: Acknowledgment at hire and on material change. Approvers complete expense-approval and anti-bribery training every year.

policies.name: Sign-on, Relocation & Repayment Agreements
policies.owner: Total Rewards with Global Mobility and Talent Acquisition
policies.approver: CHRO + General Counsel; Compensation Committee for executive officers
policies.review: Annual + on law change (track California AB 1697 status through 30 Sep 2026)
policies.audience: Candidates and employees receiving sign-on, retention, relocation or other conditional payments; recruiters and approvers
policies.purpose: Govern cash sign-on, retention and relocation support and any condition that requires repayment. Incentives should win talent without creating unenforceable 'stay-or-pay' terms (California AB 692), unlawful wage deductions, or penalty clauses that fail in India, Taiwan and mainland China.
keyProvisions: Sign-on, retention and relocation amounts follow the offer-approval matrix. Awards to executive officers need Compensation Committee approval and may trigger Form 8-K Item 5.02(e) disclosure.
The preferred retention design looks forward: RSUs or deferred cash earned over time, where unvested amounts simply lapse on departure and nothing already paid has to be repaid.

A repayment obligation is used only where local law permits it, and only under a standalone written agreement signed before payment. The agreement states the gross amount, the retention period (normally 12 months, never more than 24), monthly pro-rata reduction, the triggers, and that no interest or fees apply.

Repayment is triggered only by voluntary resignation or termination for serious misconduct. It is never triggered by termination without cause, a reduction in force, or resignation for the employer's breach (e.g., Taiwan LSA Art. 14; China LCL Art. 38).

For California workers, agreements entered on or after 1 Jan 2026 may not require repayment of training, relocation or other costs, or impose quit fees. A sign-on bonus may carry repayment only if it fits the AB 692 discretionary-payment exception. If AB 1697 is signed, the start date moves to 1 Jan 2027 and retention bonuses become eligible.

Relocation is delivered as a lump sum or as managed services through the Travel/mobility vendor. US employer-paid moving costs are taxable wages because OBBBA permanently eliminated the exclusion. Any tax gross-up must be approved in advance.

[Company] pays all H-1B petition, ACWIA and fraud-prevention fees and other legally employer-borne immigration costs. It never recovers them from the employee or imposes an early-departure penalty on sponsored workers.

Repayment is collected by invoice with an optional instalment plan. A payroll deduction is used only with contemporaneous written authorization where local wage law allows it. It must never take pay below the minimum wage and is never made from California final pay.
Repayment is never required for training or relocation that [Company] mandates mainly for its own benefit, such as compliance, safety or onboarding training, or a company-directed transfer.

Buyouts of a prior employer's notice period, forfeited bonus or unvested equity need Legal review for non-compete and trade-secret exposure. [Company] does not indemnify new hires for breaching prior restrictive covenants unless Legal approves.
Sign-on equity is granted on the fixed grant calendar. Executive inducement grants follow Nasdaq Rule 5635(c)(4), including independent-committee approval and a press release.
Agreements are stored in Document management and the retention end dates are tracked in Darwinbox. Total Rewards audits outstanding obligations every year and releases expired ones.
policies.sampleLanguage: Sign-On Bonus Agreement. [Company] will pay you a one-time sign-on bonus of [amount], less applicable withholdings, within [30] days after your start date. This Agreement is separate from your offer letter and employment agreement, and accepting the bonus is not a condition of employment. You may instead choose to receive the bonus at the end of the retention period, in which case no repayment obligation applies. If, within [12] months after your start date, you resign voluntarily or your employment is terminated for misconduct, you agree to repay the unearned portion of the bonus, reduced pro rata for each full month you remained employed. No interest or fees will be charged. No repayment is owed if [Company] ends your employment for any other reason, including a reduction in force. [Company] will not deduct any repayment from your wages; any amount due will be invoiced and may be paid in instalments. You may consult an attorney about this Agreement and have at least five business days to do so before signing. If applicable law does not permit a repayment obligation, this paragraph does not apply to you.

roles.duties: Use the country-approved offer and agreement templates, never add repayment terms to offer letters, and send any non-standard request to Total Rewards.
Design sign-on and retention vehicles by country, keep the approval matrix, and track retention periods and releases.
Administer relocation benefits through the vendor, manage gross-up and tax reporting, and coordinate immigration cost rules.
Maintain country templates (including AB 692/AB 1697 changes), review buyouts of prior-employer obligations, and approve any recovery action.
Process payments and taxes, and process repayments only through invoicing or lawful written authorization.
Approve sign-on, retention and inducement awards for executive officers.

countryAddenda.us: Outside California, repayment clauses are generally enforceable, but many states restrict recovering them through wage deductions (e.g., NY Labor Law 193, IL, WA). Recover by invoice or with contemporaneous written authorization, and never take pay below the minimum wage (29 CFR 531.35). H-1B workers may not be charged petition, ACWIA or fraud fees or penalized for leaving early (20 CFR 655.731(c)(9)-(10)). Other states are considering stay-or-pay limits (verify).
countryAddenda.us-ca: AB 692 (B&P 16608; LC 926): agreements entered on or after 1 Jan 2026 may not require repayment of training, relocation or other debts, or impose quit fees, with minimum damages of $5,000 per worker plus attorney fees. The narrow exceptions cover transferable-credential tuition and discretionary sign-on bonuses under a standalone agreement with pro-rated repayment, no interest, a retention period of no more than 2 years, notice of the right to consult an attorney, and an option to defer receipt (verify conditions). AB 1697, an urgency bill with Governor action due by 30 Sep 2026, would move the start date to 1 Jan 2027 and extend the exception to retention bonuses. Until it is signed, treat 2026 agreements as covered.
countryAddenda.ca: Repayment agreements are enforceable as contracts if they are clear, proportionate and signed before payment (otherwise fresh consideration is needed). Deductions from wages, including final pay, need written authorization and statutory permission (ON ESA s.13; BC ESA ss.21-22), and ESA minimums cannot be reduced. Employer-paid moving costs for an eligible relocation are generally not taxable (verify CRA conditions).
countryAddenda.in: Joining-bonus clawbacks and minimum-service bonds are enforceable only as reasonable, pre-estimated liquidated damages (Indian Contract Act s.74); the Supreme Court upheld a reasonable minimum-service bond in Vijaya Bank v. Prashant Narnaware (2025). Pro-rate the amount, tie it to actual cost, and stamp the agreement (Karnataka e-stamp) so it can be relied on in evidence. Recovery from the full and final settlement is limited to authorised deductions within the 50% cap (Code on Wages s.18), and the settlement is still due within 2 working days.
countryAddenda.tw: A minimum-service clause is valid only if the employer funded specialized training or pays reasonable compensation for the commitment, the period is reasonable, and it is in writing (LSA Art. 15-1; Enforcement Rules Art. 7-2). Repayment is excused if employment ends for reasons not attributable to the employee. Never pre-deduct repayment from wages (LSA Art. 26).
countryAddenda.cn: Liquidated damages are allowed only for breach of a service-period agreement (professional technical training) or a non-compete (LCL Arts. 22-25). Training penalties are capped at the unamortized training cost (SPC Interpretation II Art. 12). Structure sign-on and relocation support as conditional advances or benefits with pro-rated return, not as a penalty (local court practice varies; verify). Deductions for losses are capped at 20% of monthly wage and may not take pay below the minimum wage.

decisions: Replace cash sign-on clawbacks with vesting-based retention (RSUs, deferred cash) worldwide, or only in California? (A global rule is simpler and avoids AB 692 drift. Clawbacks remain a useful tool in India and Canada, where they are lawful.)
Deliver relocation as a lump sum or as managed benefits? (A lump sum is simple and carries no California repayment problem but is fully taxable. Managed benefits control cost and duty of care.)
Gross up relocation taxes? (A gross-up improves the candidate experience but adds roughly 40-60% to the cost.)
Use a 12- or 24-month retention period, and a monthly pro-rata or cliff? (Monthly pro-rata is the most defensible everywhere.)
Pay Indian candidates' notice-period buyouts (common market practice) and, if so, attach a pro-rated clawback?
Until AB 1697 is decided: suspend all California repayment terms, or use the AB 692 sign-on exception with full formalities?
pitfalls: Using national offer templates with relocation or training repayment clauses for California hires.
Putting repayment terms in the offer letter instead of a standalone agreement signed before payment.
Deducting repayment from final pay (California LC 221, Taiwan Art. 26, the India s.18 limits, the China 20% cap).
Charging H-1B petition costs or early-departure penalties to sponsored engineers.
Demanding repayment after a company-initiated termination or RIF.
Forgetting that US employer-paid moving costs are taxable wages after OBBBA.
policies.training: Recruiters and Total Rewards: annual training on country repayment rules and template use. Recipients sign the standalone agreement. Acknowledgment on material change.

policies.name: Employee Referral Program
policies.audience: Regular employees (with the exclusions below); recruiters, hiring managers and interviewers
policies.purpose: Encourage employees to refer qualified candidates, with transparent and fairly paid bonuses. Selection stays merit-based and non-discriminatory, and referrals must not become a channel for conflicts of interest, 'must-place' hires or corruption risk.
keyProvisions: All regular employees may earn a referral bonus except Talent Acquisition staff, the hiring manager and interview panel for the role, the referee's future direct manager, and employees at VP level and above.
A referral counts only if it is submitted through Greenhouse before the candidate applied or was sourced. The first valid referral wins, and a referral is valid for 12 months.

Bonus amounts are set by country and level band, with a premium for designated critical skills (e.g., analog/mixed-signal, physical design). They are published on the intranet and changed only for referrals made after the change.

The bonus is paid after the referred hire completes 90 days (or local probation, if longer). The referrer must be employed on the payout date. This condition is stated in writing as part of how the bonus is earned.

Referred candidates go through the same structured interviews, background checks and export-control screening as everyone else. Referrers may give information but may not interview, score or influence decisions.
No bonus is paid for rehiring anyone who left within the previous 12 months, for converting interns, or for converting contractors supplied by an agency to which [Company] owes a fee.

Referrals of relatives of government officials, or of employees or relatives of customers, suppliers or state-owned entities, go to Ethics & Compliance before any offer. [Company] never makes 'must-place' hires.
Employees may refer relatives or close friends, but the Workplace Relationships policy applies and no direct or indirect reporting line is allowed.

No bonus, target or eligibility rule depends on a candidate's race, sex or other protected characteristic. Referral outreach is open to all. TA reviews referral-hire outcomes under privilege to check for adverse impact.
Referrers must confirm they have the candidate's permission before submitting the candidate's personal data.
Bonuses are paid through payroll as taxable supplemental wages. No side payments or bonus-splitting between referrer and candidate are allowed.
TA reports referral share, quality of hire, time to fill and program cost to the CHRO every year.
policies.sampleLanguage: Employee Referral Program. [Company] welcomes referrals of talented people. To be eligible for a referral bonus, submit the candidate through [Greenhouse] before the candidate applies or is contacted by our recruiters, and confirm that the candidate has agreed to be referred. If your referral is hired into a regular position and remains employed for 90 days (or the local probation period, if longer), you will receive the bonus for that role's level and location, provided you are still employed by [Company] on the payout date. Bonuses are paid through payroll and are subject to tax. Employees in Talent Acquisition, the hiring manager, members of the interview panel and employees at VP level and above are not eligible for bonuses for roles they are involved in. Referred candidates go through the same selection process as all other candidates, and referrers may not participate in interviews or hiring decisions. If a candidate is related to, or recommended by, a government official or an employee of a customer, supplier or state-owned company, tell Talent Acquisition so that Ethics & Compliance can review the referral before any offer.

roles.duties: Submit referrals through Greenhouse with the candidate's consent, disclose any relationship or government or customer connection, and stay out of the selection decision.
Validate referral ownership and eligibility, keep referred candidates in the standard process, and flag conflict or official-connection cases.
Pay bonuses as taxable supplemental wages when the conditions are met, and apply the correct regular-rate treatment for non-exempt referrers.
Review referrals connected to officials, state-owned entities, customers or suppliers before offer, and document the merit basis.
Monitor referral outcomes and adverse impact under privilege, and report program metrics every year.

countryAddenda.us: Keep eligibility and outreach open to all. Do not pay enhanced bonuses tied to a candidate's race or sex: DOJ's first DEI False Claims Act settlement (IBM, $17M, Apr 2026) targeted demographic-linked incentives. Treat referral bonuses as supplemental wages (22% federal withholding) and confirm regular-rate treatment for non-exempt referrers (verify under 29 CFR 778). Draft the payout conditions clearly so an unpaid bonus is not a disputed earned wage at exit.
countryAddenda.us-ca: Once earned under the program terms, a referral bonus is a wage that must be paid with final pay (LC 201-203). Draft the 90-day tenure and 'employed on payout date' conditions as conditions of earning (verify enforceability of the continued-employment condition). No paid referral bonus may be subject to repayment (AB 692), and bonuses count as wages for Equal Pay Act analysis (SB 642).
countryAddenda.ca: Referral bonuses are taxable employment income subject to CPP/EI contributions and withholding. Non-discretionary referral bonuses are generally 'vacationable' wages for 4%/6% vacation pay (verify). Quebec-based employees need French program terms.
countryAddenda.in: Referral bonuses are taxable salary with TDS through payroll. Candidate data from referrers needs notice and a lawful basis (SPDI Rules now; DPDP from 13 May 2027). With 60-90 day notice periods and frequent reneging, keep the payout condition tied to the referred hire's actual joining and tenure, not to offer acceptance.
countryAddenda.tw: Referral bonuses are taxable salary income subject to withholding, and the 2.11% NHI supplementary premium applies if an employee's bonuses in the year exceed 4x the insured monthly amount. Get Legal review before paying for referrals of engineers under paid Art. 9-1 non-competes or working on national core key technology projects. Vet any external recruiter for concealed PRC ownership.
countryAddenda.cn: Referral bonuses are taxable wages subject to IIT withholding. Referrers must have the candidate's consent before sharing personal information (PIPL Art. 13). Before offer, check the candidate's prior-employer non-compete and confidentiality obligations, because hiring someone still bound elsewhere creates joint liability (LCL Art. 91).

decisions: Flat bonus or tiered by level and critical skill? (Tiers target scarce design skills. A flat bonus is simpler and seen as fairer.)
Pay at start date, after 90 days, or split? (A split payout rewards speed and retention. A single payout after 90 days limits cost for early leavers.)
Include directors and managers, or only individual contributors? (Including managers broadens reach but raises influence and conflict concerns.)
Pay for boomerang (rehire) referrals after a minimum gap?
Offer non-cash recognition instead of cash in some countries (e.g., where tax or culture makes cash less effective)?
Cap the bonuses per referrer per year? (A cap limits referral 'farming' but may discourage well-connected senior engineers.)
pitfalls: Paying enhanced bonuses for referrals from particular demographic groups, which creates Title VII and False Claims Act exposure.
Letting referrers sit on interview panels or lobby hiring managers.
Relying so heavily on referrals that the workforce stays homogeneous. Monitor outcomes and keep open sourcing.
Accepting 'recommended' candidates from customers or officials without a compliance review.
Paying bonuses outside payroll or as gift cards without tax treatment.
policies.training: Program terms published on the intranet. Recruiters are trained on eligibility and conflict screening every year. No individual acknowledgment is required.

policies.name: Paid Time Off & Holidays
policies.owner: Total Rewards (Benefits) with People Ops (leave administration)
policies.review: Annual; holiday calendars approved each Q4 for the next year
policies.audience: All employees
policies.purpose: Give every employee at least the statutory vacation and public-holiday entitlement of their work location, plus a competitive company standard. Accrual, scheduling, carryover and payout rules must be clear and lawful, and country holiday calendars published on time.
keyProvisions: Each employee's entitlement is the higher of the statutory minimum and the [Company] country standard published in the PTO schedule (market reference: US 15-20 days or flexible PTO; Canada 3-4 weeks; India 18-24 days; Taiwan and China statutory seniority scale plus company days).

People Ops publishes country holiday calendars by 30 November for the next year. They include Taiwan's 16 national holidays and make-up days, China's 13 statutory days and State Council swapped workdays, the Karnataka/Telangana national and festival list, Ontario's 9 and BC's 11 statutory holidays, and the US company holidays.

Employees request time off in Darwinbox with reasonable notice (normally 2 weeks for 3+ days). Managers respond within 5 business days and may not unreasonably refuse. In Taiwan, the employee chooses when to take annual leave (LSA Art. 38).
Where the law allows, accrual caps apply (US standard cap: 1.5x annual accrual). Accrued vacation is never forfeited where state law treats it as earned wages.

Unused vacation is paid out at separation where law or policy requires: California and other vesting states, Canadian vacation pay, India encashment, Taiwan unused leave, and China's 300% rule for untaken leave.

If flexible or unlimited PTO is adopted in the US, it must be genuinely unlimited (no accrual and no cap) in California. It must track usage enough to meet state paid sick leave laws. It is not used where statutory vacation must be tracked and paid (Canada, Taiwan, China, India), unless it also tracks the statutory minimum.

Employees are expected to take at least 10 days of vacation a year. During tape-out or customer-critical periods, managers may declare a blackout of up to 2 weeks only with VP approval, and never over approved leave or statutory holidays.

Holiday work is paid or compensated at the local rate: Taiwan double pay; China 300% with no time-off substitute; India double pay or a substitute day; BC 1.5x plus an average day's pay; other locations per statute or company policy.

Leave years and carryover follow local rules: Ontario vacation taken within 10 months after the entitlement year; BC within 12 months; India 'workers' carry forward up to 30 days with the excess encashed; Taiwan pays out unused days at year-end (or defers one year by agreement); China carries leave over only by agreement.
Two floating holidays a year are available everywhere so employees can observe religious or cultural days not on the local calendar.
Vacation keeps accruing during statutory leaves and paid notice or garden-leave periods where local law requires.
Balances are shown in Darwinbox and on the payslip where the law requires. Taiwan employees receive an annual written leave statement.
Paid time to vote is given where the law requires, e.g., up to 2 hours in California and polling days as paid holidays in India.
policies.sampleLanguage: Vacation and holidays. You are entitled to the greater of the statutory vacation for your work location and the [Company] standard shown in the PTO Schedule for your country. Request vacation in [Darwinbox] with as much notice as possible, normally at least two weeks for absences of three days or more. Your manager will respond within five business days and will not unreasonably refuse a request. We encourage everyone to take at least ten days of vacation each year. Accrued vacation is not forfeited where local law treats it as earned wages, and any unused balance will be paid at the end of your employment where law or this policy requires. Accrual caps may apply in some locations; when you reach a cap, you stop accruing until you use time. [Company] publishes a holiday calendar for each country by 30 November of the preceding year. If you are asked to work on a public holiday, you will receive the premium pay or substitute day required by local law. You also receive two floating holidays each year to observe days of personal, cultural or religious significance.

roles.duties: Plan and request time off in Darwinbox, keep balances current, and take at least the recommended minimum each year.
Approve requests promptly and fairly, plan coverage, and use blackouts only with VP approval.
Maintain accrual rules and holiday calendars per country, issue statutory leave statements, and process payouts.
Pay holiday premiums, encashments and separation payouts correctly and on time.
Benchmark entitlements every year and model the balance-sheet liability for accrued PTO.

countryAddenda.us: There is no federal mandate: where state law treats vacation as earned wages (e.g., CA, CO, IL, MA, MT, NE), it cannot be forfeited and must be paid at separation, and elsewhere the written policy governs. A combined PTO bank that also satisfies state and local paid sick leave laws must meet the strictest accrual, carryover, use and notice rules. Holiday premium pay is not required; market practice is 10-12 paid holidays.
countryAddenda.us-ca: Vacation vests as earned, cannot be forfeited, and must be paid at the final rate on separation (LC 227.3; Suastez). Caps are allowed. 'Unlimited' PTO must be genuinely unlimited (McPherson v. EF Intercultural, 2020), or payout risk follows. Allow up to 2 hours' paid voting time (Elections Code 14000). Employers may not require vacation to be used before PFL (AB 2123).
countryAddenda.ca: Ontario: 2 weeks plus 4% vacation pay (3 weeks and 6% after 5 years), taken within 10 months after the entitlement year; paying vacation pay on each paycheque requires a written agreement; 9 public holidays. BC: 2 weeks (4%) after 12 months and 3 weeks (6%) after 5 years, taken within 12 months, with 11 statutory holidays including 30 September (high-tech professionals are exempt from the Part 5 holiday rules). Vacation pay includes non-discretionary bonuses and is paid out on termination.
countryAddenda.in: OSH Code s.32 for 'workers': 1 day for every 20 days worked, if 180+ days are worked in the calendar year; up to 30 days carry forward, and the excess is encashed, as is any balance on separation. Apply the Karnataka or Telangana Shops Act where it is more favourable. Display the annual national and festival holiday list (Karnataka: 26 Jan, 1 May, 15 Aug, 2 Oct, 1 Nov plus festival holidays; verify) and treat polling days as paid holidays. Holiday work earns double pay or a substitute day.
countryAddenda.tw: LSA Art. 38 seniority scale runs from 3 days after 6 months up to 30 days, and the employee chooses when to take leave. Unused days are paid at year-end or on termination (deferral by one year only by agreement), and the employee receives an annual written statement. There are 16 paid national holidays (since 28 May 2025), with make-up days when a holiday falls on a regular day off or rest day. Holiday work is paid double.
countryAddenda.cn: Employees get 5, 10 or 15 working days by cumulative work experience, once they have 12 months' continuous work, pro-rated for joiners and leavers. Untaken leave is paid at 300% unless the employee waived it in writing. There are 13 statutory holidays plus the State Council's swapped workdays, and holiday work is paid at 300% with no time-off substitute. Adopt the policy through the democratic procedure and get acknowledgment.

decisions: US: accrual-based or flexible (unlimited) PTO? (Flexible PTO avoids California payout liability but must be genuinely unlimited and tracked. Accrual is easier for sick-leave compliance and budgeting.)
One combined PTO bank or separate vacation and sick banks? (A combined bank is simpler but must meet the strictest sick-leave law in every covered state.)
A global minimum (e.g., 20 days everywhere) or country market levels? (A global floor signals fairness and helps mobility, at extra cost in some countries.)
Carryover caps or a firm use-it-or-lose-it rule where lawful? (Caps limit liability without forfeiture risk.)
A year-end company shutdown, and does it draw on PTO? (It needs advance notice and is not possible in Taiwan without the employee choosing the dates.)
How long a tape-out blackout may last, and who approves it?
pitfalls: Use-it-or-lose-it vacation in California or other vesting states.
Rolling out US-style unlimited PTO in Taiwan, China or Canada without tracking the statutory minimum and the payout duties.
Missing Taiwan's four holidays added in 2025 and the make-up-day rule.
Not paying China's 300% for untaken leave when no written waiver exists.
Publishing holiday calendars late, which disrupts swapped workdays in China and shift planning.
policies.training: Acknowledgment at hire and on material change. Managers get an annual leave-administration briefing before the holiday calendar is published.

policies.name: Sick Leave
policies.review: Annual + each 1 January and 1 July local change
policies.audience: All employees
policies.purpose: Give every employee paid or protected time to recover from illness, get care and look after family members, at least to the level the local law requires. Protect medical privacy, prevent penalties for lawful absence, and route longer absences into leave and accommodation processes.
keyProvisions: Every employee gets the statutory sick entitlement of their work location. Where statute provides less, [Company] provides at least 5 paid sick days (40 hours) a year at full pay.

Sick leave may be used for the employee's own illness, injury or preventive care; to care for a family member (or a designated person where local law allows); for reasons related to domestic or sexual violence; and for any other purpose the local law lists.
Employees tell their manager as soon as practicable, and before the start of the shift where possible. For foreseeable absences, up to 7 days' notice may be requested where the law allows.

Medical evidence is not requested where the law forbids it (e.g., Ontario's 3 ESA days; BC's first two absences of up to 5 consecutive days). Elsewhere it is requested only after 3 consecutive days, and it confirms fitness or need without a diagnosis.

Lawful sick leave is never counted as an attendance 'occurrence' and is never used against the employee in ratings, promotions or transfers. Attendance bonuses are reduced only pro rata where the law requires (Taiwan).
Sick pay is at least the statutory rate. [Company] tops up to full pay for the first 5 days (and in Taiwan and China up to [X] days, per the country schedule).

Absences expected to last more than 5 working days are referred to the Leave team, which starts the leave-of-absence and accommodation processes (POL-35, POL-36) and protects job-protected medical-treatment periods (China).
Balances show in Darwinbox and on wage statements where the law requires (e.g., California).
Sick leave is not paid out at separation unless local law or a combined PTO policy requires it. California balances are restored for rehires within 1 year.
Employees are not required to use vacation before sick leave or statutory disability or family benefits where the law prohibits it.
Medical information is kept in confidential leave files separate from personnel files, with access limited to the Leave team.
Local ordinances and collective terms apply where they are more generous (e.g., San Francisco, Los Angeles, New York City).
policies.sampleLanguage: Sick leave. If you are ill or injured, need medical care, or need to care for a family member, you may use sick leave. You receive at least the paid sick leave required where you work and, where the law provides less, at least five paid sick days each year at full pay. Tell your manager as early as you can, preferably before your workday starts. We will not ask for a medical note where local law prohibits it. Otherwise, we may ask for a short note confirming your need for leave or your fitness to return after three or more consecutive days of absence; you will never be required to disclose a diagnosis. Using sick leave in accordance with this policy will not count against you in performance reviews, promotions or attendance programs. If your absence is likely to last longer than five working days, the Leave team will contact you to explain your options, including leave of absence, disability benefits and workplace adjustments. Medical information you share is kept confidential and stored separately from your personnel file.

roles.duties: Notify their manager promptly, record the absence in Darwinbox, and provide evidence only when properly requested.
Accept lawful sick leave without penalty, never ask about a diagnosis, and refer longer absences to the Leave team.
Configure country accruals and pay rules, manage medical documentation confidentially, and trigger leave and accommodation processes.
Apply statutory and top-up sick pay rates and show balances on wage statements where required.
Track state, local and national changes (e.g., Shanghai, BC, US states) and approve country schedules.

countryAddenda.us: About 19 states plus DC, and many cities, mandate paid sick leave (e.g., IL for any reason; MI ESTA; AK from Jul 2025; NE from Oct 2025; MO's law was repealed Aug 28, 2025). NY adds 20 hours of paid prenatal leave. One PTO bank can satisfy most laws only if it meets the strictest accrual, carryover, use and notice rules. Longer absences bring in FMLA, ADA and state PFML (POL-35).
countryAddenda.us-ca: LC 245-249: at least 40 hours or 5 days usable per year, accrued at 1 hour per 30 worked with a cap of at least 80 hours or 10 days, or front-loaded; permitted uses include the AB 406 jury, witness and victim court reasons. Show the balance on every wage statement, restore balances for rehires within 1 year, and do not pay out. Kin care lets employees use half their annual accrual for family members, and local ordinances (SF, LA, Oakland, Berkeley, San Diego) may be more generous.
countryAddenda.ca: Ontario: 3 unpaid sick days a year after 2 weeks' service, for which no medical note may be required (since Oct 28, 2024), though other reasonable evidence may be; plus a 27-week unpaid long-term illness leave after 13 weeks' employment, with a practitioner certificate. BC: 5 paid plus 3 unpaid days after 90 days, with no sick note for absences of up to 5 consecutive days for the first 2 absences each calendar year (since Nov 12, 2025), plus a 27-week serious illness or injury leave (since Nov 28, 2025).
countryAddenda.in: There is no central statutory sick leave for non-workers. The Karnataka Shops Act provides about 12 days a year of sickness or casual leave (verify). ESI sickness cash benefit covers employees earning up to INR 21,000/month. Apply the company standard (e.g., 12 days paid sick or casual leave) plus group medical insurance, and handle health data as sensitive (SPDI Rules now; DPDP from May 2027).
countryAddenda.tw: Up to 30 days a year of non-hospitalized sick leave at half pay; hospitalization up to 1 year within 2 years. From 1 Jan 2026, up to 10 sick days a year cannot lead to adverse appraisal, promotion or transfer decisions, and attendance bonuses may only be reduced pro rata (Regulations of Leave-Taking Art. 9-1). Menstrual leave is 1 day a month at half pay, with 3 days a year outside the sick-leave count. Work-injury leave is on full pay.
countryAddenda.cn: A service-based medical treatment period of 3-24 months protects the employee from Art. 40 termination. Sick pay is at least 80% of the local minimum wage, and in Shenzhen at least 60% of normal wage. Shanghai's 1995/2000 sick-pay notices lapsed on 15 Aug 2026, so the handbook or contract now sets Shanghai sick pay (floor about RMB 2,192). Reducing legacy terms needs the democratic procedure.

decisions: Keep a separate sick bank or fold it into PTO? (A separate bank is easier for statutory tracking. A combined bank is simpler for employees.)

How much to top up above statutory pay (Taiwan half pay; China 80% of minimum wage)? (Topping up is market-competitive in Hsinchu and Shanghai, and a clear handbook term avoids disputes after the Shanghai lapse.)
At what point to ask for documentation where the law allows it (e.g., 3 consecutive days)?
Front-load or accrue California paid sick leave? (Front-loading 40 hours is simpler and avoids per-period tracking.)
Offer paid menstrual leave in India (Karnataka's policy is contested) and top it up to full pay in Taiwan?
Coordinate with short-term disability: US STD, Canadian STD (EI premium reduction), and China and Taiwan statutory benefits?
pitfalls: Asking for sick notes in Ontario or BC where the law now forbids it.
Counting sick days in Taiwan appraisals or cutting full attendance bonuses.
Attendance-point systems that penalize protected leave in US states or in California.
Leaving Shanghai sick pay undefined in the handbook after the August 2026 lapse.
Leaving the paid sick leave balance off California wage statements.
policies.training: Acknowledgment at hire and on material change. Managers get an annual briefing on protected absences and medical privacy.

policies.name: Leaves of Absence
policies.audience: All employees; managers and HR business partners
policies.purpose: Administer statutory and company leaves consistently and lawfully: parental, family and medical, military, bereavement, victims', and personal leave. This covers job protection, benefits continuation, coordination with government benefits and top-ups, and a planned return to work.
keyProvisions: Every employee receives the statutory leave of their work location. On top of that, [Company] provides a global paid parental leave floor of [16] weeks for birthing parents and [12] weeks for other parents at full base pay, integrated with statutory benefits and usable within 12 months of birth or placement.

Leave requests go through the Darwinbox leave module. People Ops sends an eligibility and rights notice within 5 business days of learning of the need (the FMLA standard, applied globally), and a designation notice once it has the information needed.

Employees on statutory leave return to the same or an equivalent role with the same pay. Seniority and service accrue where the law requires. HRBP and Legal review any adverse action during protected leave or within 6 months after it.
Group health and other benefit contributions continue during statutory leave on the same basis as active employment, unless the law allows the employee to opt out.

Company top-ups are coordinated with state PFML, Canadian EI (through a registered SUB plan), India maternity benefits, Taiwan Employment Insurance parental allowances and China maternity allowances, so total pay does not exceed 100% of base.
Intermittent and reduced-schedule leave is given where the law provides it (e.g., FMLA/CFRA, Taiwan single-day parental leave and hourly family-care leave).
Medical certification is requested only where the law permits and only to the extent needed. Certifications are stored in confidential leave files.
Bereavement leave: at least [5] paid days for immediate family, and more where local law requires (California 5 days; Taiwan 3-8 days by relationship).
Military and reservist leave follows USERRA and the Canadian provincial reservist leave rules. Differential pay is a company decision.
Personal unpaid leave of up to 6 months needs VP and HRBP approval, with written terms on benefits, equity vesting (per plan terms) and the return date.
People Ops tells Immigration about any leave of a sponsored employee (e.g., H-1B) and tells Stock Admin about leaves that affect vesting under plan terms.

The return to work is planned 2-4 weeks ahead. It covers fitness-for-duty only where job-related and consistent, any accommodation (POL-36), and a documented return-to-work process where the law requires one (Ontario AODA, 50+ employees).
Leave status is never shared beyond people with a need to know. Managers do not contact employees on leave about work except for agreed keep-in-touch arrangements.
policies.sampleLanguage: Leaves of absence. [Company] provides the leaves required by the laws of your work location and the additional company leaves described in this policy, including paid parental leave of [16] weeks for birthing parents and [12] weeks for other parents. To request leave, submit a request in [Darwinbox] as early as possible, normally at least 30 days before foreseeable leave. The Leave team will confirm your eligibility, your rights and responsibilities, and any documents needed within five business days. While you are on statutory leave, your group health and other benefits continue on the same terms as if you were working, and you will return to the same or an equivalent position with the same pay. Company pay during leave is coordinated with government or insurance benefits so that combined payments do not exceed your base pay. If you are sponsored for immigration purposes or hold equity awards, the Leave team will help you understand any effect of leave. [Company] does not tolerate retaliation against anyone for requesting or taking leave.

roles.duties: Request leave early, provide the certification the law allows, and plan a handover and return date with their manager.
Refer leave requests to People Ops within 2 business days, plan coverage, and never discourage or penalize leave.
Determine eligibility, issue notices, coordinate pay, top-ups and benefits, and manage return-to-work plans.
Apply statutory pay, SUB-plan top-ups and benefit deductions during leave, and issue Canadian ROEs for interruptions of earnings.
Review adverse actions near protected leave and keep country leave schedules current.
Advise on the status effects of leave for sponsored employees and update filings where needed.

countryAddenda.us: FMLA (50+ employees within 75 miles; employees with 12 months' service and 1,250 hours) gives 12 weeks of job-protected leave (26 for military caregivers) with group health continuation. Give eligibility and designation notices within 5 business days and describe FMLA in the handbook. Register for and coordinate state PFML (e.g., NJ, NY, WA, MA, CT, OR, CO, DC; MN and DE benefits from Jan 1, 2026; ME from May 1, 2026; MD benefits from 2028), USERRA and state leaves. ADA leave beyond FMLA may be a required accommodation.
countryAddenda.us-ca: CFRA (5+ employees; 12 months' service and 1,250 hours) gives 12 weeks, including care for a designated person, and PDL gives up to 4 months per pregnancy, separate from CFRA bonding. PFL wage replacement (70-90%, up to 8 weeks) is not job-protected and cannot be conditioned on using vacation (AB 2123). Add bereavement (5 days), reproductive loss (5 days per event, max 20 a year), victims' leave (Gov Code 12945.8), school activities (40 hours a year at 25+ employees), organ and bone marrow donor leave, and military spouse leave, and describe CFRA and PDL in the handbook.
countryAddenda.ca: Pregnancy leave is 17 weeks and parental leave up to 61 weeks (63 in ON, 62 in BC, for non-birth parents); EI pays 55% up to about C$729/week for 35 weeks, or 33% over 61 weeks, and top-ups must run through a registered SUB plan. Ontario adds family responsibility (3 days), bereavement (2), family caregiver (8 weeks), critical illness, domestic/sexual violence (5 paid + 5 unpaid days + 15 weeks), long-term illness (27 weeks) and child death leave. BC adds family responsibility (5), bereavement (3), compassionate care (27 weeks) and serious illness (27 weeks). Continue benefit contributions unless the employee opts out.
countryAddenda.in: Maternity (SS Code Ch. VI): 26 weeks for the first two children (at most 8 before delivery), 12 weeks from the third child, 12 weeks for adoption of a child under 3 months or for commissioning mothers, and 6 weeks for miscarriage, after 80 days worked in the prior 12 months. Give written intimation at appointment, and provide nursing breaks, WFH by agreement, and a creche (or allowance) at 50+ employees. No dismissal during maternity absence. Paternity leave is market practice only (1-2 weeks; competitive GCCs offer 4-12+).
countryAddenda.tw: Maternity leave is 8 weeks (full pay after 6 months' service), and prenatal check-up and paternity leave are 7 paid days each. Unpaid parental leave runs up to 2 years per child under 3, with an EI allowance of 80% for up to 6 months per parent; from 2026 up to 30 days can be taken in single days on 5 days' notice. Family care leave is 7 days (56 hours) usable hourly, marriage leave 8 paid days and bereavement 3-8 paid days. No termination during maternity leave, and no refusal or penalty for family leave.
countryAddenda.cn: National maternity leave is 98 days; Shanghai gives 158 days plus 10 days' paternity leave and 5 days a year of childcare leave per parent until the child is 3, and Guangdong/Shenzhen gives 178 days plus 15 days' paternity leave and 10 days a year of childcare leave. Top up the maternity allowance to salary where local rules require; marriage leave is 3 days (Shanghai 10) and bereavement 1-3 days. No Art. 40/41 termination or contract expiry during pregnancy, maternity or nursing (LCL Arts. 42, 45).

decisions: Set a global paid parental leave floor (e.g., 16/12 weeks) or offer statutory leave only? (A floor helps attract and retain engineers but must be coordinated with PFML and EI to avoid double pay.)
Top up EI through a SUB plan in Canada, and if so to what percentage and for how many weeks? (Tech market: 80-100% for roughly 15-26 weeks.)
Continue or suspend equity vesting during unpaid personal leave longer than a set period? (It must follow plan terms and be communicated in advance.)
Outsource US leave administration to a third-party administrator, or keep it in-house? (A TPA handles multi-state PFML complexity. In-house keeps control of the employee experience.)
Offer gender-neutral paid parental leave in India and China beyond the statutory minimums?
Offer sabbatical or extended personal leave, and at what eligibility (e.g., 5 years' service)?
pitfalls: Running only FMLA and ignoring separate CFRA and PDL entitlements in California.
Terminating or downgrading employees during or soon after protected leave without HR and Legal review.
Paying Canadian top-ups outside a registered SUB plan, which reduces the employee's EI.
Missing India's written maternity intimation or the creche duty at 50+ employees.
Refusing Taiwan's day-based parental leave or hourly family-care leave introduced in 2026.
policies.training: Acknowledgment at hire and on material change. Managers: leave and anti-retaliation training on appointment and every 2 years.

policies.name: Reasonable Accommodation
policies.owner: People Ops (Leave & Accommodation team) with Employee Relations
policies.audience: Applicants and employees worldwide; managers, recruiters, EHS and lab managers
policies.purpose: Provide workplace adjustments through a timely, documented, good-faith interactive process. This covers disability, pregnancy and related conditions, lactation, religious belief or practice, family status (Canada) and other grounds protected locally. It applies in recruitment and AI-based assessments, in labs and in remote work.
keyProvisions: Applicants and employees may ask for an adjustment related to disability, pregnancy, childbirth or related conditions, lactation, religious belief or practice, family status or any other ground protected where they work. No special words or forms are required.
Managers and recruiters must pass any request, or any obvious need, to the Accommodation team within 2 business days. They do not decide requests themselves.

The Accommodation team acknowledges within 2 business days and holds an interactive discussion with the employee. The target is a decision within 10 business days, with interim measures while the request is assessed.

Documentation is requested only when the need is not obvious, and only enough to establish the limitation and the need. Diagnosis, genetic information and family medical history are never requested. Records go in a confidential medical file separate from the personnel file.

Possible adjustments include modified schedules or duties, remote or hybrid work, equipment and assistive software, alternative assessment formats, leave, temporary suspension of an essential function (pregnancy), reassignment to a vacant role, and lab-duty modification.
Pregnant or post-partum employees in labs with reproductive hazards are offered risk assessment, protective adjustments or reassignment at the same pay. They are never excluded against their wishes.

Recruiting accommodations: every posting and interview invitation says how to request an adjustment. Coding tests, AI-scored assessments and video interviews always have an alternative or human-reviewed format.
Lactation: reasonable break time and a private, non-bathroom space with seating, a surface, power, and nearby sink and refrigerator access at every site.

Undue hardship is assessed by HR and Legal against [Company]'s overall resources. For US religious requests the test is substantial increased cost (Groff v. DeJoy); in Canada the undue-hardship bar is high. A denial must be in writing and explain the alternatives offered.
Employees may ask the Head of Employee Relations to review a denial within 15 business days.
Accommodations are reviewed on a change of role, location or need. Where the law requires, an individual accommodation plan and emergency response information are documented (e.g., Ontario AODA).
Accommodation costs are charged to a central budget, not the team's budget.
Retaliation against anyone who asks for an accommodation or supports a request is prohibited.
policies.sampleLanguage: Workplace adjustments. [Company] provides reasonable accommodations to applicants and employees with disabilities, pregnancy or related conditions, lactation needs, religious beliefs or practices, and other needs protected by the law where they work, unless doing so would cause undue hardship. You may ask for an adjustment at any time, orally or in writing, by speaking to your manager, your recruiter or the Accommodation team at [contact]. You do not need to use any particular words. We will acknowledge your request within two business days and work with you to understand your needs and identify effective options; where appropriate we will put interim measures in place while we assess your request. We will ask only for information needed to understand your limitation and the adjustment required, and we will never ask for a diagnosis unless the law requires it. Medical information is kept confidential and separate from your personnel file. If we cannot provide the specific adjustment you requested, we will explain why in writing and offer alternatives. You will not be treated unfavorably for requesting an accommodation.

roles.duties: Tell a manager, recruiter or the Accommodation team about a need, take part in the interactive discussion, and share the necessary information.
Recognize requests, pass them on within 2 business days, carry out agreed adjustments, and keep information confidential.
The Accommodation team runs the interactive process, documents options and decisions, manages confidential files and reviews plans.
Advise on undue hardship, religious and pregnancy requests, denials and cross-border questions.
Assess lab and reproductive hazards, recommend protective adjustments and approve lab-duty changes.
Offer alternative interview and assessment formats and make sure AI-based tools have accessible alternatives.

countryAddenda.us: ADA Title I and the PWFA apply at 15+ employees; the PWFA allows temporary suspension of essential functions, bars forcing leave when another accommodation works, and bars requiring documentation when the need is obvious. Its elective-abortion provisions were vacated (W.D. La., May 21, 2025), and the EEOC plans an NPRM narrowing 'related medical conditions'. Religious accommodation uses the Groff v. DeJoy 'substantial increased cost' test, and the PUMP Act requires lactation breaks for 1 year.
countryAddenda.us-ca: FEHA (5+ employees) makes failure to accommodate and failure to engage in a timely, good-faith interactive process separate violations (Gov Code 12940(m),(n)). CRD rules effective Oct 2025 require accommodation for AI/ADS assessments. PDL includes reasonable accommodation and transfer, and a written lactation policy is required (LC 1030-1034). Employers with 25+ employees must accommodate alcohol or drug rehabilitation (LC 1025).
countryAddenda.ca: There is a duty to accommodate disability, family status, creed and other Code grounds to the point of undue hardship (ON Human Rights Code ss.11, 17; BC Code s.13). HRTO and BCHRT claims must be filed within 1 year and carry uncapped general damages. AODA (50+ employees) requires documented individual accommodation plans, a return-to-work process, accommodation notices in recruitment, and individualized workplace emergency response information.
countryAddenda.in: The RPwD Act 2016 requires reasonable accommodation, a published equal opportunity policy (s.21) and a liaison officer at 20+ employees. HIV status must be kept confidential, with a complaints officer at 100+ persons. A transgender equal opportunity policy and complaint officer are also required. Pregnancy-related WFH by agreement and nursing breaks apply under SS Code Ch. VI.
countryAddenda.tw: The People with Disabilities Rights Protection Act prohibits discrimination and supports job redesign (government subsidies may be available; verify). OSH maternal health protection requires risk assessment and duty adjustment for pregnant and post-partum (1 year) workers, with no work from 10pm to 6am. Provide 60 minutes a day of paid lactation time until the child is 2, and a lactation room at 100+ employees.
countryAddenda.cn: The Employment Promotion Law bars disability and infectious-disease-carrier discrimination. For female employees: no overtime or night work from 7 months' pregnancy, prenatal visits on paid time, a 1-hour daily nursing break until the child is 1, and reassignment away from prohibited hazards. Health information is sensitive personal information that needs separate consent and a PIPIA under the PIPL.

decisions: A central accommodation team or HRBP-led handling? (A central team gives consistency and expertise. HRBPs know the business better but vary in practice.)
Fund adjustments from a central budget? (A central budget stops managers resisting because of cost, and supports AODA and ADA defenses.)
Treat remote work as a possible accommodation even for roles covered by return-to-office rules? (Required case by case. A blanket refusal is high-risk.)
Use third-party medical reviewers for complex cases? (They add expertise and privacy distance, at extra cost and time.)
How much documentation to require for religious requests? (Minimal documentation is the safer default.)
pitfalls: Rigid '100% healed' return-to-work rules or maximum-leave policies with no individual assessment.
Treating remote-work requests linked to health as ordinary flexibility requests and refusing them under return-to-office policy.
Excluding pregnant lab workers 'for their protection' instead of offering assessment and choice.
Asking for a diagnosis or full medical records.
Using AI assessment or video-interview tools with no alternative format.
policies.training: Managers and recruiters: accommodation awareness on appointment and every 2 years (Ontario: included in AODA training). Acknowledgment at hire.
