policies.name: Benefits Eligibility
policies.approver: CHRO + CFO; the US Benefits/ERISA fiduciary committee for plan terms
policies.review: Annual renewal cycle + on law change
policies.audience: All employees and their eligible dependants; People Ops and Payroll
policies.purpose: Define who is eligible for which statutory and company-sponsored benefits in each country, when coverage starts and ends, and how status changes are handled. Enrolment must be timely, compliant (ACA/ERISA, CPP/EI, PF/ESI, labor insurance, social insurance) and consistent across entities.
keyProvisions: Each benefit's eligibility is set by its plan document or statute. This policy and the country benefits schedule summarize those rules, and the plan documents prevail if they conflict.

Regular employees scheduled for 30+ hours a week (US) or who meet the local definition are eligible for company plans. Part-time employees are eligible pro rata where offered, and interns and temporary employees as statute or the schedule provides. Contractors are not eligible, and any misclassification concern is escalated.

Statutory social insurance is enrolled on day one or within the statutory deadline: US FICA/FUTA/state; Canada CPP/EI; India EPF (INR 25,000 wage ceiling from 17 Sep 2026) and ESI; Taiwan Labor, Employment and Occupational Accident Insurance and NHI (day one), with the pension reported within 7 days; China social insurance and housing fund within 30 days.
Company medical, dental, vision, life and disability coverage starts on the date of hire (US: never later than the ACA 90-day waiting period; Canada, India, Taiwan, China: day one market standard).
Eligible dependants are defined per plan: spouse or registered partner, and children to 26 in the US or per local plan. People Ops verifies dependant eligibility at enrolment and every 2 years.
Elections may change only at open enrolment or within 30 days of a qualifying life event (60 days for Medicaid/CHIP events in the US), through the Benefits admin platform.
Coverage ends at the end of the month of separation unless the plan or law says otherwise. Continuation notices (COBRA, Cal-COBRA, conversion) are issued on time.

Changes of status (full-time to part-time, change of entity or country, exempt to non-exempt) are processed through MV-05. Eligibility is re-determined from the effective date, with no gap in statutory coverage.
During statutory leave, benefits continue as set out in POL-35.

Retirement benefits: US 401(k) with auto-enrolment where required; Canada group RRSP/DPSP; India PF, EPS and gratuity (NPS optional); Taiwan labor pension; China basic pension (enterprise annuity optional).
ESPP eligibility follows the IRC 423 plan and non-423 country sub-plans. Permitted exclusions are used consistently, and China participants join only after SAFE Circular 7 registration.
Benefits are never tied to a protected characteristic, and plans pass the applicable nondiscrimination tests.
Health information in benefits administration is handled under the HIPAA firewall and POL-46. HR decision-makers do not see claims data.
policies.sampleLanguage: Benefits eligibility. You become eligible for [Company]'s benefit plans in your country on your date of hire if you are a regular employee who meets the eligibility rules for that plan, including any minimum scheduled hours. Statutory social insurance programs begin as required by local law. You must enrol, or confirm your elections, in [Benefits Platform] within 30 days of your eligibility date; otherwise default coverage (where available) will apply. You may add eligible dependants as defined by each plan and will be asked to provide proof of eligibility. After enrolment, you may change your elections only during annual open enrolment or within 30 days of a qualifying life event such as marriage, birth, adoption or loss of other coverage. If your status changes, for example from full-time to part-time or to a different country entity, your eligibility will be reviewed from the effective date of the change. Coverage generally ends on the last day of the month in which your employment ends, and you will receive information about any continuation rights. The official plan documents govern if they differ from this summary.

roles.duties: Enrol on time, give accurate dependant information, and report qualifying life events within 30 days.
Maintain plan documents and country schedules, run open enrolment and renewals, and oversee vendors and nondiscrimination testing.
Pass hires, terminations and status changes from Darwinbox to the benefit vendors and statutory registrations on time.
Withhold and remit statutory contributions and benefit deductions correctly, including wage-base caps and floors.
Budget plan costs, fund the plans, and oversee ACA/ERISA filings and actuarial valuations (gratuity, pensions).

countryAddenda.us: ACA employer mandate (50+ FTEs): offer affordable coverage (9.96% of household income in 2026) that provides minimum value to 95% of full-time (30+ hour) employees, with waiting periods of no more than 90 days; 2026 penalties are $3,340 (4980H(a)) and $5,010 (4980H(b)). Furnish Forms 1095-C by about Mar 2 and e-file by Mar 31; COBRA applies at 20+ employees. SECURE 2.0 auto-enrolment applies to plans set up after Dec 29, 2022, and Roth catch-up is mandatory for those with prior-year FICA wages over $150,000. 2026 limits: 401(k) $24,500, HSA $4,400/$8,750, health FSA $3,400, DCAP $7,500.
countryAddenda.us-ca: Withhold SDI at 1.3% of all wages (no cap) and file the CalSavers exemption if a 401(k) is offered. Cal-COBRA covers insured plans with 2-19 employees, and the HIPP and LC 2800.2 notices are due at termination. The Bay Area commuter benefit applies at 50+ full-time employees, and SF HCSO expenditures apply at 20+ employees for SF-based staff. Self-insured plans report health coverage to the FTB by Mar 31.
countryAddenda.ca: Enrol hires in group health, dental, life, LTD and EAP on day one (market practice); BC MSP has a waiting period for relocating hires (rest of the arrival month plus 2 months), so provide interim private cover. Offer a group RRSP/DPSP match with DPSP vesting of no more than 2 years. Employer-paid life and wellness accounts are taxable benefits, and private health premiums are taxable in Quebec. Continue benefit contributions through the ESA notice period (ON) and statutory leaves, and confirm the carrier contracts allow this.
countryAddenda.in: EPF is mandatory for employees earning up to INR 25,000/month from 17 Sep 2026: 12% + 12% on Code 'wages', with the EPS diversion capped at INR 2,083/month. International workers contribute on full salary from day one unless they hold a certificate of coverage (the Karnataka HC 2024 ruling is on appeal). ESI applies up to INR 21,000, and gratuity after 5 years (1 year for fixed-term). Group medical (family floater INR 5-10 lakh), term life and accident cover are market standard; collect nominations at joining.
countryAddenda.tw: Enrol Labor Insurance (11.5% + 1% EI), Occupational Accident Insurance and NHI from the first day of work at the correct insured-salary grade (lowest grade NT$29,500 in 2026). Report the labor pension (at least 6% employer) within 7 days of hire or exit. The 2025 Foreign Professionals Act amendments extend pension and EI coverage to more foreign professionals, so confirm eligibility for each hire. Periodic health checks and an employee welfare committee are expected.
countryAddenda.cn: Register social insurance and housing fund within 30 days of hire in the city of employment, on the actual prior-year average wage within the city floor and cap (Shanghai RMB 7,546-37,731 from 1 Jul 2026). Foreigners must be enrolled, and there is no US-China totalization agreement. Waivers or cash in lieu are void (SPC Interpretation II Art. 19). Enterprise annuity and supplementary medical are optional and may not replace statutory coverage.

decisions: Day-one coverage or first of the following month? (Day one is the market norm for engineering talent. First of month simplifies administration.)
Self-insured or fully insured US medical plan? (Self-insured saves cost at scale but brings HIPAA, PCORI and nondiscrimination duties.)
A global minimum benefits standard (e.g., life insurance 2x salary, AD&D, EAP, mental health) or local market practice only?
Cover domestic partners where the law does not require it? (Inclusive, with some imputed-income administration in the US.)
Set the part-time eligibility threshold at 20 or 30 scheduled hours?
Provide international private medical insurance for globally mobile employees and their families?
Make employer contributions to employees' Trump accounts (IRC 128, up to $2,500 a year, proposed regulations Aug 2026)?
pitfalls: Classifying variable-hour lab contractors or long-term temps out of US benefits, which creates ACA penalties and ERISA claims.
Missing the 30-day qualifying-life-event window, or processing it late.
Paying China social insurance on the minimum base instead of actual wages.
Leaving Indian CTC structures unchanged after the 50% wages rule, which understates PF and gratuity.
Failing to enrol Taiwan hires in Labor Insurance and NHI on their first day.
policies.training: Benefits enrolment guide and acknowledgment at hire and at each open enrolment. Annual training for People Ops on status-change processing.

policies.name: Hybrid & Remote Work
policies.audience: All employees and managers; Payroll, Tax, Mobility, IT/Security and Trade Compliance
policies.purpose: Define the on-site, hybrid and remote work categories, how arrangements are approved and changed, and the legal, tax, security and export-control guardrails that follow the employee's actual work location. Flexibility must not create hidden payroll, permanent-establishment or deemed-export exposure.
keyProvisions: Every role is designated On-site (e.g., lab, cleanroom-support and facilities roles), Hybrid (at least [3] days a week in the assigned office, with team anchor days) or Remote (approved individually, from a registered work address).

Arrangements are requested and approved through MV-04 by the manager and HRBP, and recorded in Darwinbox with the work address. They are based on policy and revocable with [8] weeks' notice unless a contract, accommodation or law says otherwise.

Employees work only from their approved address in their country of employment. Working from another state, province or country for more than 10 working days a year needs prior approval from Mobility, Tax and Trade Compliance.

Temporary work from abroad is limited to 20 working days a year and is never allowed from comprehensively sanctioned countries or regions. While abroad, employees may not access export-controlled technology or source code unless Trade Compliance clears it.

Work is done only on company-managed devices over approved secure connections. Export-controlled or Restricted data must not be viewable by household members or others and is never stored on personal devices or personal cloud accounts.
Remote workers receive equipment and reimbursement under POL-30. Hours rules and the right to disconnect (POL-29, POL-39) apply fully to remote and hybrid staff.
Remote employees complete a home-workspace ergonomic self-assessment within 30 days and report work-related injuries within 24 hours, as on-site staff do.
Performance is judged on outcomes. Hybrid or remote status may not reduce access to projects, development, promotion or pay decisions.
Remote-work requests linked to disability, pregnancy or caregiving are handled as accommodations under POL-36, not as discretionary flexibility.
Any monitoring of remote work (e.g., security telemetry, badge data used for attendance) is limited to what POL-47 discloses. Always-on webcams and keystroke-based productivity scoring are not used.
Pay ranges are location-based. A move to a different pay zone is approved in advance, and pay is reviewed with effect from the move date.
Changes to office-attendance expectations are communicated at least [8] weeks in advance, with country-specific legal review where remote terms are contractual.
policies.sampleLanguage: Where you work. Your role is designated as on-site, hybrid or remote, and your approved work location is recorded in [Darwinbox]. Because employment, tax, immigration and export-control rules depend on where you actually perform work, you must work from your approved location. If you want to work from a different state, province or country, even temporarily, request approval in advance through [MV-04 workflow]; work from another country is limited to 20 working days per year and requires approval from Mobility, Tax and Trade Compliance. You may not work from, or access company systems in, comprehensively sanctioned countries or regions. While working remotely, use only company-managed devices and approved connections, and do not allow others to view confidential or export-controlled information. Hybrid and remote arrangements are provided under this policy and may be changed with reasonable notice, except where a written agreement or an approved accommodation provides otherwise. Your performance will be assessed on results, and your work location will not limit your access to development or advancement.

roles.duties: Work from the approved location, get approval before working elsewhere, and protect company information in shared spaces.
Apply the role designations consistently, judge performance on outcomes, and route accommodation-related requests to HR.
Record work locations, register payroll and statutory accounts for new work states or provinces, and keep country notices current.
Assess requests to work across borders for immigration, tax, social security and permanent-establishment exposure.
Clear any access to controlled technology from outside the home country, and keep geo-blocking rules for sanctioned regions.
Provide managed devices, secure connectivity, and geo-location controls that block access from sanctioned regions.

countryAddenda.us: The work state (and city) governs payroll registration, minimum wage, overtime, sick leave, PFML, final pay, non-competes and required notices, so register before an employee starts working from a new state. Buy workers' comp in each work state (monopolistic funds in ND, OH, WA and WY); OSHA does not inspect home offices, but work injuries there are recordable. Remote I-9 document review is allowed only for E-Verify employers in good standing, and NY, CT and DE require electronic-monitoring notices.
countryAddenda.us-ca: Reimburse a reasonable share of personal phone and internet costs and necessary home-office costs (LC 2802). Pay non-exempt remote staff the local minimum wage of their actual work location, and give home-office ergonomics guidance (8 CCR 5110). Remote workers are outside the WVPP, but any monitoring must be disclosed in the CCPA notice.
countryAddenda.ca: Document hybrid and remote arrangements as policy-based and revocable: a remote term written into a contract makes a later return-to-office mandate a constructive dismissal risk (Potter, 2015 SCC 10). Ontario requires disconnecting and e-monitoring policies (25+ employees), and OHSA covers virtual harassment. WorkSafeBC expects home-office ergonomic and working-alone assessments. Do not let remote hires or relocations into Quebec happen without setup (French documents, QPP/QPIP, OQLF registration at 25+ employees).
countryAddenda.in: The services-sector model standing orders in the IR (Central) Rules 2026 include WFH provisions, so mirror them in service rules for establishments with 300+ workers. SEZ unit staff may work from home only in line with SEZ Rule 43A. Maternity WFH may be agreed where the work allows (SS Code). Disclose remote monitoring and rely on DPDP s.7(i) for security controls.
countryAddenda.tw: Minute-level attendance recording applies to remote work (LSA Art. 30), and evening calls with US HQ count as working time. The OSH Act workplace bullying chapter (from 1 Jul 2026) covers remote work. Changes of work location must follow the five transfer principles (LSA Art. 10-1). Keep controlled and national core key technology work on managed devices in approved locations.
countryAddenda.cn: There is no specific remote-work statute (verify local guidance). A change of work location or a permanent remote arrangement should be agreed in writing (LCL Art. 35), and social insurance stays in the city of employment. Injuries while working from home may be claimed as work injuries (verify local practice). Monitoring of remote devices requires prior notice under the PIPL, and the employer bears the burden of proof on attendance.

decisions: A fixed hybrid minimum (e.g., 3 days) or team-set patterns? (A fixed minimum is easier to explain and enforce. Team-set patterns suit globally distributed design teams.)
Which role families are eligible for remote work (e.g., design and verification yes; lab, bring-up and facilities no)?
Location-based pay zones or a single national range? (Zones control cost. A single range simplifies transparency and relocations.)
How many work-from-abroad days a year (0, 10, 20)? (More days aid retention but increase tax, immigration and export-control review.)
Use badge data to enforce attendance? (It must be disclosed under POL-47 and US NLRA and state notice rules, and it can hurt trust.)
Pay for co-working spaces for remote employees far from an office?
pitfalls: Employees quietly working from undisclosed states or countries, which creates payroll, tax, permanent-establishment and export exposure.
Writing remote status into Canadian contracts, then mandating a return to office.
Engineers accessing controlled EDA projects or source repositories from a D:5 country while travelling.
Using badge-swipe data for discipline without disclosing it.
Remote hires in Quebec with no French documentation or payroll setup.
policies.training: Acknowledgment when an arrangement is approved or changed. Managers of distributed teams: training on leading hybrid teams and on location rules.

policies.name: Right to Disconnect
policies.review: Annual; for Ontario, confirm by 1 March each year that the policy is current
policies.audience: All employees and managers, especially teams working across US-Asia time zones
policies.purpose: Set expectations for communications outside working hours across time zones, protect rest and wellbeing, and satisfy Ontario's written 'disconnecting from work' policy requirement. Pay and hours rules must still be met for hours-regulated staff in the US, Taiwan, mainland China and India.
keyProvisions: 'Disconnecting from work' means not engaging in work-related communications, including emails, telephone calls, video calls or sending or reviewing other messages, so as to be free from the performance of work (the ESA definition, applied globally).

Core collaboration windows are published for each region pair (e.g., US Pacific-Taipei/Shanghai and US Pacific-Bengaluru). Recurring meetings outside a participant's local 8:00-19:00 need that participant's agreement and a fair rotation.

Employees are not expected to read or respond to work communications outside their working hours, except on an approved on-call rota, during an approved critical period (tape-out, customer escalation), or in an emergency (safety, security incident, production outage).
Managers use scheduled send and do not send non-urgent messages outside the recipient's working hours with an expectation of a response. Urgent matters go by phone to the designated on-call contact.
Hours-regulated staff (US non-exempt, Taiwan, mainland China, India 'workers') may be contacted after hours only for approved overtime or on-call work, and all such time is recorded and paid.
On-call rotas are published at least 2 weeks ahead, compensated under the local on-call policy, and limited to [1 week in 4] per person unless the employee agrees otherwise.
Employees on vacation or leave are not expected to monitor messages. They set an auto-reply and delegate.
No employee may be penalized or rated down for not responding outside working hours in line with this policy.
Critical-period exceptions are approved by a VP, time-limited (normally no more than 3 weeks) and logged by HR.
HR reviews aggregate after-hours messaging and meeting data each year as a wellbeing indicator. It is never used to assess individuals.

Ontario: the policy shows its preparation date and the date of any change, is given to Ontario employees within 30 days of preparation or change (new hires within 30 days of hire), and is kept for 3 years after it stops applying.
policies.sampleLanguage: Disconnecting from work. [Company] recognizes that working across time zones can blur the line between work and personal time. 'Disconnecting from work' means not engaging in work-related communications, including emails, telephone calls, video calls or sending or reviewing other messages, so as to be free from the performance of work. Outside your normal working hours you are not expected to read or respond to work communications unless you are on an approved on-call rotation, during an approved critical period, or in a genuine emergency. Managers should schedule non-urgent messages to arrive during the recipient's working hours and must not expect replies outside those hours. If you are paid for hours worked, any work you are asked to perform outside your scheduled hours must be recorded and will be paid. You will not be treated unfavorably for disconnecting in accordance with this policy. This policy was prepared on [date] and last changed on [date]. A copy is provided to Ontario employees within 30 days of preparation or change and within 30 days of hire.

roles.duties: Set working hours and status in collaboration tools, use auto-replies when away, and record any after-hours work if hours-regulated.
Respect local working hours, rotate meeting times fairly, use scheduled send, and get approval for critical-period exceptions.
Approve critical-period exceptions, and design on-call rotas and staffing so they do not depend on after-hours work.
Maintain and distribute the policy (Ontario dating, distribution and retention), log exceptions, and report aggregate wellbeing indicators.
Pay recorded after-hours work and on-call compensation for hours-regulated employees.

countryAddenda.us: No federal or state right-to-disconnect statute is in force (verify). For non-exempt staff, after-hours emails, calls and messaging are compensable hours worked under the FLSA and must be recorded. Do not restrict employees' Section 7 communications about working conditions.
countryAddenda.us-ca: No California right-to-disconnect statute is in force (a 2024 bill did not pass; verify). Non-exempt employees must be paid for after-hours work, and California does not apply the federal de minimis doctrine to regularly recurring off-the-clock tasks (Troester v. Starbucks, 2018), so small after-hours tasks create wage, overtime and PAGA exposure.
countryAddenda.ca: Ontario: employers with 25+ Ontario employees on 1 January must have a written disconnecting-from-work policy by 1 March, showing the preparation date and change dates. Give a copy within 30 days (new hires within 30 days of hire) and keep it for 3 years after it stops applying (ESA Part VII.0.1); the policy does not itself create a right to disconnect. BC has no equivalent statute, so the global policy applies.
countryAddenda.in: There is no statutory right to disconnect. 'Workers' are limited to 8 hours a day and 48 a week, with consent-based overtime at double pay, and the Karnataka 24x7 conditions cap daily hours at 10 including overtime. After-hours contact with women on night shifts must respect the consent and transport conditions.
countryAddenda.tw: There is no standalone statute, but after-hours calls and messages with US HQ are working time that must be recorded to the minute and paid (LSA Arts. 24, 30). Employees must have 11 hours' rest between shifts, and the regular day off may be worked only in emergencies (LSA Art. 40). Overwork prevention duties apply to long-hours staff (OSH Act Art. 6(2)).
countryAddenda.cn: There is no statutory right to disconnect (verify). Courts have treated after-hours messaging work (e.g., on WeChat) as overtime (verify local case law), subject to the 36-hour monthly cap and 150/200/300% premiums unless comprehensive or flexible hours are approved. A sudden death at work within 48 hours of onset counts as a work injury, so manage crunch periods actively.

decisions: Apply the policy globally or only in Ontario? (Global application supports a sustainable cross-time-zone culture; Ontario-only is the legal minimum.)
Use technical controls (message delay or muting after hours) or guidance only?
How to share late-night meetings fairly between US and Asia teams (fixed windows vs rotation)?
How to pay for on-call: a weekly stipend, per-incident pay, or time off in lieu (subject to local law)?
Who approves critical-period exceptions, and for how long at most?
pitfalls: An Ontario policy that is not dated, distributed within 30 days or kept for 3 years.
Assuming 'exempt' language covers Taiwan or mainland China engineers, whose after-hours work is paid overtime.
Asia-based teams carrying all late-night meetings with US HQ.
Using after-hours activity data to judge individual commitment or performance.
policies.training: Acknowledgment at hire and on change (Ontario: copy within 30 days). Managers: guidance on cross-time-zone working norms every year.

policies.name: Global Mobility
policies.approver: CHRO + CFO (tax equalization and cost) + General Counsel
policies.review: Annual + on immigration or tax rule change
policies.audience: Employees on international assignments, commuter arrangements, extended business travel or permanent cross-border transfers; their managers
policies.purpose: Govern international assignments, commuter arrangements, extended business travel and permanent cross-border transfers so every move complies with immigration, tax, social security, employment and export-control rules and is cost-effective and fair to the employee.
keyProvisions: Move types are defined as: business travel (under 30 days, with meetings but no productive work beyond incidental tasks), short-term assignment (up to 12 months), long-term assignment (1-3 years), commuter, and permanent transfer (localization).
Every move needs a business case and cost estimate approved by the Dept Head, Mobility and Finance. Moves of executive officers also need CHRO approval.

No productive work starts in a host country until immigration authorization is granted. Mobility confirms visas and permits, tax registration and withholding (including shadow payroll), social security coverage (certificates of coverage where available), and permanent-establishment risk.

Trade Compliance screens each move for export control before it starts: relocating a foreign national, or moving controlled technology access to a new country, can be a deemed reexport that needs a license.

Assignment letters set out the home and host entity, duration, pay and allowances (housing, cost of living, hardship), benefits, home leave, repatriation, and termination during the assignment. Host-country statutory minimums always apply.
Assignments use tax equalization; permanent transfers are localized. US taxpayers abroad get 409A and equity-sourcing review, and equity income is tracked by work-day allocation across countries.
Dependants' immigration and schooling are supported where the policy tier provides. Spousal work authorization is not guaranteed and is assessed before the move.
Travelers and assignees register with the Travel/mobility vendor and follow POL-41. Duty-of-care support includes medical evacuation cover.
Relocation repayment terms follow POL-31 and never apply to California workers after AB 692.

A permanent transfer ends the home employment in line with home-country law (e.g., China termination certificate, Canadian ROE, Taiwan service certificate). The new host contract recognizes prior service where agreed.
Immigration sponsorship follows POL-19. [Company] pays all employer-borne immigration costs and never recovers H-1B fees.
Mobility tracks workdays by country for business travelers so it can manage 183-day rules, Canadian Regulation 102 waivers and US state sourcing.
policies.sampleLanguage: International moves. If [Company] asks you to work in another country, or approves your request to do so, Global Mobility will support you and must approve the arrangement before you begin any work there. Before you travel, Mobility will confirm that you have the right to work in the host country, arrange tax and social security coverage, and coordinate any export-control review needed for your role. Your assignment letter will describe your home and host employer, the expected duration, your compensation and allowances, benefits, and what happens at the end of the assignment. Assignments are generally tax-equalized so that you pay approximately the same tax as you would have paid at home; permanent transfers are localized to the host country's pay and benefits. You must keep Mobility informed of changes in your family, travel or work location, and you may not extend your stay or change your duties without approval. Host-country employment laws, including minimum statutory benefits, will apply to you while you work there.

roles.duties: Start work only when cleared, keep accurate travel and workday records, and meet immigration and tax filing duties.
Raise mobility needs early, justify the business case, and never ask an employee to start work before authorization.
Assess, approve and administer moves, run the vendor, calculate packages and tax equalization, and track workdays.
Get work authorization, prepare filings (including I-129 Part 6 with Trade Compliance), and maintain status.
Screen deemed-export and deemed-reexport implications and license conditions for each move.
Run home, host and shadow payroll, equity withholding across jurisdictions, and social security certificates.

countryAddenda.us: Inbound routes: H-1B (wage-weighted lottery; the $100K proclamation fee was vacated by D. Mass. but the proclamation is extended to Sept 21, 2027; a $103,265 cap-petition fee is proposed), L-1, O-1, TN and E-3. The I-129 Part 6 export attestation must reflect the beneficiary's actual technology access. US taxpayers abroad remain subject to US tax, so review tax equalization, 409A and FICA (totalization certificates, e.g., with Canada); RSU supplemental withholding is 22%, or 37% over $1M, and equity income must be sourced across states and countries for mobile employees.
countryAddenda.us-ca: California taxes residents on worldwide income and sources equity compensation earned partly while working in California (verify the allocation method for mobile employees). California assignees keep California-compliant terms: no repayment clauses under AB 692, and no non-California law or forum (LC 925). Inbound assignees working in California are paid under California wage-hour rules.
countryAddenda.ca: Inbound routes include intra-company transfer (1 year with a related entity in the last 3), CUSMA Professional and the Global Talent Stream (10-business-day LMIA standard); submit LMIA-exempt offers in the IRCC Employer Portal, pay the C$230 compliance fee and keep records 6 years. Since 21 Jan 2025, spousal open work permits are limited to spouses of TEER 0/1 (or listed TEER 2/3) workers with 16+ months left on their permit. US employees on short Canadian trips need Regulation 102 waivers or Non-Resident Employer Certification, and Canada-US totalization certificates cover temporary assignments.
countryAddenda.in: Foreign assignees need an Employment (E) visa (salary generally over USD 25,000 a year) and FRRO registration within 14 days of arrival if staying 180+ days (Immigration and Foreigners Act 2025; verify employer duties). International workers contribute PF on full salary with no ceiling because there is no India-US social security agreement. Releasing US-origin controlled technology to third-country nationals in India is a deemed reexport, while Indian nationals in India fall in Country Group A:5 and are often license-exception eligible.
countryAddenda.tw: Foreign professionals need a WDA work permit (specialized-work salary threshold about NT$47,971/month; verify) or an Employment Gold Card. The 2026 Foreign Professionals Act amendments open permits to graduates of top universities, give spouses work rights and speed up APRC. Qualifying foreign professionals may exempt 50% of salary above NT$3M from tax for 5 years, and non-residents are withheld at 18%. Enrol NHI from the ARC start date.
countryAddenda.cn: Foreigners need a Foreigner's Work Permit (A/B/C tier), a Z visa and a residence permit within 30 days of entry before working. Foreign labor contracts run for at most 5 years, and employment is recognized only with a valid permit (SPC Interpretation II Art. 4). Enrol foreigners in social insurance (there is no US-China totalization agreement); tax-exempt expatriate allowances are available until 31 Dec 2027. US persons supporting advanced-node PRC fabs need EAR 744.6 clearance before assignment.

decisions: Tax equalization, tax protection or laissez-faire? (Equalization is fair and predictable for employees but costly and complex. Protection is cheaper but creates windfalls.)
Core/flex relocation packages or fixed tiers? (Core/flex lets employees tailor support within a budget. Fixed tiers are simpler to administer.)
Localize long-term assignees automatically after [3] years, or case by case?
Keep long-term assignees on home or host payroll and benefits?
Use Canada, India or Taiwan hubs as alternatives when US H-1B costs rise (proposed $103,265 cap fee)?
Recognize prior service for severance and leave after a permanent transfer?
pitfalls: Letting employees start productive work before permits are granted, including 'business visitors' who actually do hands-on work.
Ignoring the deemed-reexport issue when a PRC-national engineer transfers from the US to Canada or India with the same repository access.
Missing shadow payroll or multi-country sourcing on RSU vests during assignments.
Not enrolling foreign assignees in China social insurance.
Assuming a spouse can work in the host country.
policies.training: Assignees receive pre-departure briefings (immigration, tax, security, host-country conduct) and sign an acknowledgment. Managers are briefed before sponsoring a move.

policies.name: Travel Safety & Restricted Travel
policies.approver: General Counsel + Chief Security Officer + CHRO
policies.review: Every 6 months + immediately after a major geopolitical or regulatory event
policies.audience: All employees and contractors travelling on business or carrying company devices or data across borders; approvers
policies.purpose: Protect travelers and company technology during travel. Set pre-approval rules for high-risk and restricted destinations, including mainland China, Hong Kong, Macau and sanctioned regions. Meet legal travel-approval duties, such as Taiwan's rules for national core key technology personnel, and export-control rules for technology carried on or accessed from devices.
keyProvisions: All business travel is booked through the Travel/mobility vendor, and itineraries are registered with the duty-of-care provider. Personal trips taken with company devices are also registered.

Destinations are tiered by Security and Trade Compliance. Tier 1 is normal travel. Tier 2 is heightened-risk (including mainland China, Hong Kong and Macau) and needs Dept Head, Security and Trade Compliance approval at least 10 business days before departure. Tier 3 is prohibited: comprehensively sanctioned countries and regions (currently Cuba, Iran, North Korea and the Crimea, DNR and LNR regions of Ukraine; verify), with no business travel, remote work or reimbursed expenses.

Tier 2 travelers use loaner laptops and phones issued by IT. No source code, design databases, GDS/RTL, customer NDA material or export-controlled technology is stored on them. Remote access to such data from Tier 2 locations is blocked unless Trade Compliance clears it in writing, and devices are wiped and inspected on return.

Carrying or accessing EAR-controlled technology or source code abroad is an export or reexport unless an exclusion or exception applies. The end-to-end encryption carve-out (15 CFR 734.18(a)(5)) does not cover data intentionally stored in D:5 countries such as China; license exception TMP needs Trade Compliance confirmation. ITAR data never travels without Empowered Official approval.

U.S. persons (citizens and green-card holders) may not support development or production at advanced-node PRC fabs without a license (EAR 744.6). Customer-fab and OSAT visits in mainland China are pre-cleared by Trade Compliance.

Taiwan: employees on government-commissioned or subsidized national core key technology projects must get government approval before travelling to mainland China, including for the required period after they leave. HR keeps the covered-person roster and tells covered employees in writing.

Every Tier 2 traveler completes a pre-travel briefing on local counter-espionage, data and export laws, border device inspections, and exit-ban risk, and does not carry documents that could be treated as state secrets or 'important data'.

If authorities demand access to a device or account, the traveler complies with lawful orders, does not volunteer credentials to company systems beyond what the law compels, and reports to Security within 24 hours. The event is handled as a potential data incident.
Meetings with parties on the Entity List, the SDN list or other restricted-party lists need Trade Compliance approval, and gifts and hospitality follow the anti-bribery policy.
The 24/7 Security hotline coordinates emergency support, medical evacuation and crisis response (HS-02). Travelers check in when Security asks.
If [Company] holds a facility clearance, cleared employees report foreign travel and foreign contacts as the security rules require.
Rules apply by destination, role and technology access, never by the traveler's nationality or national origin.
Approvals and export determinations are kept for 5 years.
policies.sampleLanguage: Travelling safely and protecting our technology. Before you travel for business, book through [Travel Vendor] so we can reach you in an emergency. Some destinations require advance approval: for travel to mainland China, Hong Kong, Macau or any other Tier 2 location, submit your request at least 10 business days before departure and complete the pre-travel briefing. Travel to comprehensively sanctioned countries or regions is not permitted. When travelling to a Tier 2 location, use the loaner laptop and phone issued by IT, and do not carry or remotely access source code, design data, customer confidential information or export-controlled technology unless Trade Compliance has approved it in writing. If a border or other official asks you to unlock a device, comply with lawful instructions, do not volunteer passwords to company systems, and contact Security within 24 hours. If you work in Taiwan on a government-designated core key technology project, you must obtain government approval before travelling to mainland China; HR will tell you if this applies to you, including after you leave [Company].

roles.duties: Book through the vendor, get approvals, complete briefings, follow device rules, and report incidents within 24 hours.
Approve only necessary Tier 2 travel, and plan customer and fab support so it avoids unlicensed technology releases.
Maintain destination tiers, issue loaner devices, deliver briefings, run the 24/7 hotline, and handle device-access incidents.
Clear technology carried or accessed abroad, 744.6 U.S.-person issues, restricted-party meetings and license exceptions.
Keep the Taiwan core key technology covered-person roster, send notices before and after employment, and add travel rules to onboarding and exit.
Provision and sanitize loaner devices, and enforce geo-blocking and conditional access for Tier 2 and Tier 3 locations.

countryAddenda.us: Taking controlled technology or source code abroad is an export, and records are kept 5 years (EAR Part 762). Business travel to or services involving comprehensively sanctioned regions is prohibited without OFAC authorization. If a facility clearance is held, cleared employees report foreign travel and contacts (SEAD 3), and U.S.-person travelers supporting PRC advanced-node fabs need EAR 744.6 review.
countryAddenda.us-ca: Non-exempt California travelers are paid for travel time that is hours worked, including daily overtime on travel days. All necessary travel expenses are reimbursed under LC 2802, with no policy deadline that forfeits a valid claim.
countryAddenda.ca: Canadian staff with access to US EAR technology follow the same device rules; deemed-reexport rules follow the traveler's citizenship or permanent residency, and ITAR items also trigger the Controlled Goods Program. University collaborations in sensitive technology areas follow the federal Policy on Sensitive Technology Research and Affiliations of Concern, so brief travelers accordingly.
countryAddenda.in: Indian staff travelling with US-origin controlled technology follow the global device rules, and exports of items or technology from India may also need SCOMET authorization. Night travel for women employees requires consent, safe transport and security arrangements (OSH Code s.43).
countryAddenda.tw: Staff on government-commissioned or subsidized national core key technology projects need prior approval to travel to mainland China, and the duty continues after they leave (Cross-Strait Act Art. 9; fines NT$2M-10M). Misappropriating listed technologies (including AI/HPC chip design and chiplet interconnect design) carries up to 12 years under the National Security Act. With MJIB questioning 114 people across 17 PRC-funded firms in Jul-Aug 2026, apply a PRC travel and device policy to all Taiwan staff.
countryAddenda.cn: Brief travelers and PRC-based staff on the Counter-Espionage Law (revised 2023), 'important data' under the Data Security Law, and China's Export Control Law and technology export catalogue, which can restrict taking PRC-developed technology out of China. Keep HR and engineering data exports within PIPL cross-border rules, and route any request from authorities for device access through Legal. Get Anti-Foreign Sanctions Law advice where travel involves US Entity List issues.

decisions: Make loaner devices mandatory for all mainland China, Hong Kong and Macau travel, or decide by role? (Mandatory is simpler and safer; role-based lowers cost for non-technical staff.)
Block remote access to design repositories from Tier 2 locations completely, or allow it case by case with Trade Compliance approval?
Which function gives final approval for Tier 2 trips: Security, Trade Compliance, or both?
Track personal travel of Taiwan core key technology personnel through HR? (Legal duties apply to personal travel too; tracking requires PDPA notice.)
How to treat employees visiting family in a Tier 2 country with company devices? (Apply destination and access rules, not nationality.)
Which duty-of-care and evacuation provider, and what level of cover?
pitfalls: Engineers carrying design databases or PDK files on laptops to foundry or OSAT visits in mainland China.
Using nationality as a proxy for travel restrictions, which creates discrimination exposure.
Forgetting that Taiwan's core key technology travel approval continues after an employee leaves.
Travelers handing over company system passwords at borders without contacting Legal and Security.
US-person FAEs supporting advanced-node PRC fabs without an EAR 744.6 review.
policies.training: Tier 2 travelers: pre-travel briefing and acknowledgment before each trip (valid 12 months). Taiwan covered personnel: written notice at designation and at exit. Annual export-control refresher for engineers and FAEs.

policies.name: Performance Management
policies.owner: Talent Management with HR Business Partners
policies.audience: All employees and managers (sales and executive plans also governed by their plan documents)
policies.purpose: Set clear expectations, give regular feedback and assess performance consistently. Outcomes link to pay and development, and the documented record must be fair and able to support decisions in countries without at-will employment.
keyProvisions: The annual cycle runs in the Performance module (Darwinbox): goals set by 15 February (PD-01), at least quarterly check-ins, a mid-year review, and a year-end review and calibration (PD-02). Employees who join mid-cycle have pro-rated goals.
Performance is rated on a 5-point scale with behavioral and results anchors for each level. Distribution guidelines are used; forced quotas are not.
HRBPs facilitate calibration by level and organization. Before ratings are final, HR Analytics runs a privileged adverse-impact review by sex, age band and other lawful categories.
Merit increases, bonus modifiers and equity refresh follow the compensation guidelines and the calibrated rating. Pay decisions do not deviate from the rating without documented approval.
Time on statutory leave or approved accommodation cannot lower a rating. Goals are pro-rated, and Taiwan's rule that up to 10 sick days a year cannot affect appraisal is applied.

Underperformance is handled in stages: timely coaching, then written expectations, then a Performance Improvement Plan (PD-03) of 30-90 days with measurable objectives, support and weekly check-ins. In Canada, India, Taiwan and China, the PIP file also records training and consideration of reassignment.
HRBP and Employee Relations review PIP outcomes before any adverse action. Terminations follow POL-53.
AI tools may help managers draft feedback, but no rating or adverse decision is made by an automated system. A named human decision-maker owns every rating (POL-50).
Employees may ask the HRBP to review their final rating within 15 business days. The review goes to the skip-level manager.
Managers complete performance-management training before their first cycle and a refresher every year.
Reviews and PIPs are written in, or translated into, a language the employee understands (Chinese for mainland China). Employees acknowledge them in the system.
Performance records are kept under POL-49 and are available to employees where the law gives access rights (e.g., the California personnel file).
Sales and FAE incentive and performance goals include compliance modifiers (e.g., export screening, anti-bribery). Violations can reduce or cancel incentive credit.
policies.sampleLanguage: Performance reviews. At the start of each year you and your manager will agree goals in [Performance Module] that describe what you are expected to achieve and how. You will have regular check-ins, at least quarterly, and a year-end review in which your manager assesses your results and behaviors against those goals. Ratings are calibrated across teams so that similar performance is assessed consistently, and they inform merit increases, bonuses and equity refresh awards. Time you spend on protected leave or with an approved accommodation will not lower your rating. If your performance is not meeting expectations, your manager will discuss this with you promptly and, where appropriate, put in place a written improvement plan with clear objectives, support and a reasonable timeframe. A person, not an automated tool, is responsible for every rating decision. If you disagree with your final rating, you may ask your HR Business Partner for a review within 15 business days. Your review will be provided in a language you understand, and you will be asked to acknowledge that you have received it.

roles.duties: Set and update goals, prepare for check-ins, give self-assessments, and raise concerns about ratings through the review route.
Set clear expectations, document feedback as it happens, rate fairly, and start PIPs only with HRBP involvement.
Facilitate calibration, review PIPs and adverse decisions, handle rating reviews, and coach managers.
Run privileged adverse-impact analyses of ratings and PIP outcomes, and report patterns to the CHRO.
Review adverse actions arising from performance, and make sure local procedures are followed in Canada, India, Taiwan and China.

countryAddenda.us: At-will employment does not remove pretext risk: document legitimate reasons, check ratings for adverse impact, and check timing against protected activity. Muldrow (2024) lets transfer or assignment claims proceed on 'some harm'. Automated performance tools can trigger Illinois HB 3773 notice duties (from Jan 2026) and Colorado SB 26-189 duties (from Jan 2027).
countryAddenda.us-ca: Keep a human decision-maker and documented reasons for any ADS-assisted rating (CRD regulations, Oct 2025). SB 947, with Governor action due 30 Sep 2026, would bar relying mainly on ADS for discipline or termination. Adverse action within 90 days of a wage, whistleblower or equal-pay complaint is presumed retaliatory (LC 98.6, 1102.5). The personnel file, including performance and training records, must be produced within 30 days of a request.
countryAddenda.ca: Poor performance rarely amounts to just cause. The employer must show clear expectations, warnings, a real chance to improve and a proportionate response (McKinley), and in Ontario ESA amounts are forfeited only for wilful misconduct. Unilateral demotions or pay cuts after a review risk constructive dismissal (Potter).
countryAddenda.in: There is no statutory PIP. For non-workers, termination on contractual notice ('termination simpliciter') is lawful if the letter is non-stigmatic. For 'workers', exits for poor performance carry a risk of reinstatement by the Tribunal, so document a fair process and consider mutual separation. Service rules or standing orders should describe the appraisal process.
countryAddenda.tw: An Art. 11(5) incompetence dismissal needs objective standards, coaching or training, a genuine improvement plan and consideration of reassignment (the last-resort principle). From 2026, up to 10 sick days a year may not affect appraisal, promotion or transfer. Performance rules used for discipline should be in the filed work rules (30+ employees).
countryAddenda.cn: An Art. 40(2) incompetence termination needs objective, communicated standards, evidence of failure, training or job adjustment, and then renewed failure, plus 30 days' notice or pay in lieu and N. Performance rules that affect vital interests must go through the democratic procedure and be acknowledged. Rating evidence must be in Chinese and signed or electronically confirmed.

decisions: Numeric ratings or a no-ratings model? (Ratings make pay decisions and defending terminations easier. No-ratings models need strong documentation in other ways.)
Forced distribution or guidelines? (Guidelines lower legal and morale risk while keeping calibration discipline.)
One global cycle, or local cycles (e.g., India's April-March financial year)?
How much 360-degree feedback to use, and whether it feeds the rating directly?
Standard PIP length (30, 60 or 90 days), by country and level?
Allow AI drafting help for reviews, and with what safeguards?
pitfalls: Running a US-style 30-day PIP followed by termination in China or Taiwan without evidence of training or reassignment.
Lower ratings for employees who were on protected leave or had approved accommodations.
Calibration results that differ by demographic group with no documented, job-related reason.
English-only reviews used as evidence in China or Taiwan disputes.
Managers writing reviews after the fact to support a decision already made.
policies.training: Managers: training before their first cycle and a refresher every year (calibration, bias, documentation, local rules). Employees: acknowledgment of their review each cycle.

policies.name: Promotion & Internal Mobility
policies.audience: All employees, managers and recruiters
policies.purpose: Give employees a fair, transparent route to promotion and internal moves based on the job architecture and documented criteria. Every move must meet pay-transparency, contract-variation, export-control and securities-disclosure requirements.
keyProvisions: All open roles are posted internally for at least 5 business days before external candidates are considered. Exceptions (confidential searches, executive roles, reorganizations, visa-driven moves) need CHRO approval. Internal postings show the pay range where the law requires it and, as company standard, for all US and Canadian roles.

Employees may apply for internal roles after 12 months in their current role (6 months for early-career employees) if their performance meets expectations and they are not on a PIP. Managers may not block applications. The current manager is told when the employee reaches the interview stage.

Internal candidates are assessed in structured interviews against the role scorecard. Referrers and friends on the panel recuse themselves, and unsuccessful internal candidates get feedback within 10 business days.

Promotions are nominated in the [semi-annual] promotion cycle against the leveling criteria for the job family (PL-03), calibrated across the organization, and approved in the matrix. An off-cycle promotion needs a documented business reason and VP approval.
A promotion carries an increase of at least [8]% or brings pay to the minimum of the new range, whichever is greater. Total Rewards checks internal pay equity and range position before approval.
The promotion equity refresh is granted on the fixed grant calendar, never off-cycle around MNPI.
When the new role is agreed, the employee moves within 30-60 days. The releasing manager may delay the move only for a documented critical deliverable, and by no more than 30 days.
Every transfer, promotion or change of project triggers export-control re-screening, with access updated through identity management before the employee starts in the new role.
HR tells Legal the same business day when anyone is appointed or promoted to Section 16 officer status, so that the Form 3, 8-K Item 5.02 and insider-list steps can follow.

Contractual formalities are completed before the effective date: a new appointment letter (India), a written variation (China), a transfer meeting Art. 10-1 (Taiwan), and fresh consideration for new restrictive or termination terms (Canada).
Exempt or non-exempt status and India 'worker' status are re-checked on every role change.
Selection criteria are job-related. Protected characteristics play no part, and HR Analytics reviews promotion rates for adverse impact every year under privilege.
International internal moves follow POL-40 (Global Mobility).
policies.sampleLanguage: Growing your career at [Company]. Open positions are posted on [Internal Careers] for at least five business days before external candidates are considered, except where confidentiality or other approved reasons apply. If you have been in your current role for at least 12 months, are meeting performance expectations and are not on an improvement plan, you may apply without your manager's approval; your manager will be informed if you are invited to interview. Internal candidates are assessed using the same structured process and criteria as external candidates, and you will receive feedback if you are not selected. Promotions are based on the leveling criteria for your job family and are reviewed and calibrated across the organization during the promotion cycle. When you are promoted, your pay will be reviewed against the new range and internal equity. Some moves require additional steps, such as an updated employment agreement, a review of your access to export-controlled technology or, for senior officers, notice to Legal for securities filings. Your new manager and your HR Business Partner will guide you through these steps.

roles.duties: Apply through internal postings, prepare for structured interviews, and complete contract and access steps before starting the new role.
Nominate against the leveling criteria, support moves without blocking them, and release employees on the agreed timeline.
Post roles internally with the required pay information, run structured assessments, and give feedback to internal candidates.
Set the promotion pay guidelines, check range and pay-equity position, and schedule equity refresh grants.
Run calibration, make sure contractual and classification changes are completed, and alert Legal to officer appointments.
Re-screen export access for new roles and projects before access is granted.

countryAddenda.us: Several state pay-range laws reach internal postings and promotion opportunities (e.g., Virginia ranges in internal postings from Jul 1, 2026; Colorado promotional-opportunity notices; verify others). Muldrow (2024) lowers the harm threshold for transfer claims, so document the criteria. Promotion to officer status triggers Section 16 reporting (Form 3 within 10 days) and possibly an 8-K Item 5.02 filing.
countryAddenda.us-ca: Give the pay scale for the employee's current position on request (LC 432.3), and include good-faith ranges on internal postings for roles that may be filled in California. From 2026, stock and bonuses count as wages under the Equal Pay Act (SB 642). Newly promoted supervisors need 2 hours of harassment training within 6 months, and exempt status must be re-checked on role changes.
countryAddenda.ca: Ontario's ESA posting rules cover publicly advertised postings, not internal-only ones, and BC requires pay ranges in public postings. A promotion or transfer with materially different duties or location needs consent to avoid a constructive dismissal claim. New termination or restrictive terms need fresh consideration to be enforceable.
countryAddenda.in: Issue a revised appointment letter showing the new designation and wages. Re-assess 'worker' versus managerial status, because it changes retrenchment, overtime and standing-order coverage. Keep the revised CTC compliant with the 50% 'wages' rule.
countryAddenda.tw: Transfers must meet the five principles of LSA Art. 10-1: business need, wages and terms no worse, suitability, help with relocation, and consideration of family life. A manager title does not remove LSA coverage or overtime rights unless Art. 84-1 applies. Update the employee roster (LSA Art. 7).
countryAddenda.cn: Changes to position, work location or pay need written agreement (LCL Art. 35), and a transfer between Shanghai and Shenzhen needs consent and a new social insurance registration. Sign a contract variation before the effective date. Reassess non-compete eligibility if trade-secret access changes.

decisions: Minimum time in role before internal applications: 6, 12 or 18 months?
When to tell the current manager: at application or at interview stage?
A separate promotion budget or promotions funded from the merit pool?
Annual or semi-annual promotion cycles, and whether off-cycle promotions are allowed?
Post all roles internally first, or allow direct external searches for critical skills?
A fixed minimum promotion increase, or pay guided only by range position?
pitfalls: 'Tap on the shoulder' promotions with no posting or documented criteria.
Unilateral transfers in China or Taiwan without written agreement or consideration of Art. 10-1.
Moving engineers to new projects without updating export-controlled access.
Missing pay ranges on internal postings in states that require them.
Forgetting to notify Legal of a new Section 16 officer.
policies.training: Managers: annual briefing before the promotion cycle. Recruiters: internal-posting and pay-transparency training every year.

policies.name: Learning & Tuition Assistance
policies.audience: All regular employees; managers approving development spend
policies.purpose: Fund job-related learning, certifications, conferences and degree study in a way that builds engineering capability, is tax-efficient, and uses repayment terms only where the law allows (California AB 692, China service periods, Taiwan minimum-service rules, Indian bonds). Training records must also satisfy personnel-file and evidence requirements.
keyProvisions: There are three types of learning: required training (compliance, safety, role-mandatory), which is company-paid, done on working time and never repayable; job-related development (courses, certifications, conferences); and tuition assistance for accredited degree or certificate programs.

Tuition assistance is capped at US$5,250 a calendar year in the US, which is the IRC 127 tax-free limit, with local-currency equivalents in the country schedule. Job-related development is funded from team budgets.

Regular employees with at least 6 months' service who are meeting expectations are eligible. Manager and L&D approval is required before enrolment. Programs must relate to the employee's current or reasonably expected role.
Tuition is reimbursed on completion with a passing grade (C or better, or Pass) and proof of payment. Prepayment through approved vendors is allowed for certifications.

Repayment applies only where local law permits and only under a signed agreement made before enrolment. It is pro-rated monthly over no more than 24 months, and it is never required when [Company] ends employment without cause. For California workers it is limited to the AB 692 transferable-credential exception.
Non-exempt and hours-regulated employees are paid for required training time. Voluntary courses outside working hours are not working time only where local law allows.
Conference talks, papers and course projects that use company information need pre-approval through the publication-review process, which covers confidential information, patents and export control.
Coursework may not use company confidential information, customer data or controlled technology. Inventions made in funded programs are handled under POL-48.
Training vendors and academic partners are screened against restricted-party lists (Entity List, SDN, UFLPA) before engagement.
Every training record in the LMS includes the provider or trainer, date, duration, competencies covered and any certification.
Amounts above tax-free limits are taxed through payroll under local rules.
L&D reports participation, spend and outcomes, broken down by function and location, every year.
policies.sampleLanguage: Learning and tuition assistance. [Company] invests in your growth. Training that [Company] requires you to complete, such as compliance, safety or role-mandatory courses, is paid for by [Company], takes place during working time where possible, and is never subject to repayment. For job-related courses, certifications and conferences, discuss your plan with your manager and submit a request in [LMS] before you enroll. Employees with at least six months of service who are meeting expectations may also apply for tuition assistance of up to [US$5,250] per calendar year (or the local equivalent) for accredited programs related to their current or anticipated role. Approved tuition is reimbursed after you complete the course with a passing grade and submit proof of payment. In some countries, and only where the law permits, you may be asked to sign a separate agreement before enrollment under which a pro-rated portion of tuition is repayable if you resign within a stated period; no repayment applies if [Company] ends your employment without cause. Coursework must not use confidential or export-controlled company information.

roles.duties: Get approval before enrolling, complete programs, submit proof, and protect company information in coursework and talks.
Approve development linked to role needs, fund team development, and support time for learning.
Run the program, the LMS records and vendor screening, and apply the country repayment and tax rules.
Process reimbursements, tax amounts above the limits, and handle any lawful repayment only by invoice or with written authorization.
Keep country repayment templates up to date (including AB 692/AB 1697) and review publication approvals together with Trade Compliance.

countryAddenda.us: IRC 127 educational assistance excludes up to $5,250 a year, including permanently eligible student-loan repayment (the cap is indexed after 2026), under a written plan that meets nondiscrimination rules; job-related courses may also qualify as a working-condition fringe (IRC 132(d)). Voluntary training outside working hours is non-compensable only if it meets 29 CFR 785.27-.31. Several states restrict recovering training costs through wage deductions (e.g., NY Labor Law 193).
countryAddenda.us-ca: AB 692 bars requiring repayment of training costs under agreements from 1 Jan 2026 (1 Jan 2027 if AB 1697 is signed). The only exception is tuition for a transferable credential under a separate agreement that discloses the cost up front, pro-rates repayment, imposes no penalty if the employer terminates other than for misconduct, and is not a condition of employment (verify conditions). Under SB 513, training records (provider, date, duration, competencies, certification) are part of the personnel file and must be produced within 30 days of a request.
countryAddenda.ca: Repayment agreements must be signed before the course starts and be clearly pro-rated. Deductions from wages need written authorization (ON ESA s.13; BC ESA ss.21-22). Employer-paid training that mainly benefits the employer is generally not a taxable benefit (verify CRA guidance). Keep technical training time separate from SR&ED project time codes.
countryAddenda.in: Service bonds tied to training costs are enforceable only if reasonable and proportionate (Indian Contract Act s.74); the Supreme Court upheld a reasonable minimum-service bond in Vijaya Bank (2025). Stamp the agreement. Reimbursements may be taxable perquisites under the new regime (verify), and any recovery from the full and final settlement must stay within Code on Wages s.18 limits.
countryAddenda.tw: A minimum-service commitment requires employer-funded specialized training and a reasonable period, agreed in writing (LSA Art. 15-1; Enforcement Rules Art. 7-2). Repayment is pro rata only, and none is owed where employment ends for reasons not attributable to the employee. OSH training is mandatory and paid (new hires typically at least 3 hours).
countryAddenda.cn: Service-period agreements are allowed only for employer-funded professional technical training (LCL Art. 22). Liquidated damages are capped at the unamortized training cost and need evidence of actual spending (fapiao, vendor contracts); ordinary onboarding or safety training cannot support a service period. Keep training records as evidence for Art. 40(2) incompetence cases.

decisions: Use repayment agreements for tuition at all? (Many companies drop them worldwide after AB 692 and rely on vesting equity for retention.)
Annual tuition cap: align it with IRC 127 ($5,250) or set it higher and tax the excess?
Support full degree programs (e.g., MS in EE) or only certificates and courses?
Prepay tuition or reimburse on completion? (Prepaying widens access. Reimbursing controls completion risk.)
Include IRC 127 student-loan repayment support for US early-career engineers?
Pay certification bonuses (e.g., for functional-safety or security certifications)?
pitfalls: Requiring California employees to repay training costs under agreements covered by AB 692.
Making employees repay mandatory compliance or safety training.
Paying more than the IRC 127 cap tax-free.
Training records that do not capture the fields SB 513 requires.
China service-period claims with no fapiao or proof of actual training cost.
policies.training: Program terms published in the LMS. Employees sign the pre-enrolment agreement where one applies. Managers are briefed every year during budget planning.

policies.name: Mandatory Training & Policy Acknowledgment
policies.owner: Learning & Development with Ethics & Compliance (policy governance)
policies.approver: CHRO + General Counsel; Audit Committee oversight of Code of Conduct certification
policies.review: Annual curriculum review + on law change
policies.audience: All employees, contractors with system access (per contract), managers and designated role groups (lab, FAE, sales, insiders, export-flagged roles)
policies.purpose: Define the mandatory training curriculum by audience and country, set deadlines and consequences, and collect defensible acknowledgments of key policies. Statutory training duties, Nasdaq and SEC expectations, and export and trade-secret controls must all be met and provable.
keyProvisions: L&D and Legal maintain a curriculum matrix. Global modules: Code of Conduct, anti-harassment, speak-up and non-retaliation, insider trading, anti-bribery, privacy and security, and trade secrets. Statutory country modules and role-based modules follow (lab and EHS safety, TCP/export for flagged roles, sales and FAE anti-bribery and export, manager modules).

New hires complete the global modules within 30 days, statutory modules by the legal deadline, and TCP or lab-safety modules before any access is granted. Newly promoted managers complete manager modules within 6 months, or sooner where the law requires.
Annual certification of the Code of Conduct and insider trading policy is completed in Q4, and the results are reported to the Audit Committee.

Training is on paid working time and is recorded for hours-regulated staff. It is available in a language employees understand (e.g., Traditional Chinese, Simplified Chinese, French for Quebec) and accommodated on request.
Where the law requires interactive training (e.g., California and New York harassment training), the modules include live or interactive elements and a way to ask questions.

The LMS keeps completion records with provider or trainer, date, duration and content, for at least the statutory period (e.g., California harassment training 2 years; SB 513 fields) and at least 5 years for export and TCP training.

Employees acknowledge policies electronically at hire, on material change, and every year for the Code and insider trading policy. In mainland China, a policy is published for acknowledgment only after the democratic procedure is complete.
No acknowledgment may be worded to limit reporting to regulators. All acknowledgment forms carry the protected-rights carve-out (SEC Rule 21F-17, NLRA, DTSA).
Reminders go out at 7 and 14 days before a deadline. After it, the manager and HRBP are told, and system or lab access tied to safety or export training is suspended until the training is done.
Persistent non-completion is a conduct issue under POL-13 and is reflected in the performance review.
Contractors with system access complete the modules their contract requires before access.
Legal reviews content every year and after significant law changes. Retired versions are archived with their dates.
policies.sampleLanguage: Required training and acknowledgments. As a condition of your role, you must complete the training assigned to you in [LMS] by the due date, including training required by the laws of your work location and training specific to your role, such as laboratory safety or export-control training. New employees must complete core modules within 30 days of starting. Some training must be completed before you receive access to laboratories, controlled technology or certain systems. Training takes place on paid working time; if you are paid for hours worked, record the time you spend. You will also be asked to acknowledge that you have read and will follow key policies when you join, each year for the Code of Conduct and Insider Trading Policy, and whenever a policy changes materially. Nothing in any acknowledgment limits your right to report possible violations of law to, or communicate with, any government agency, or to receive an award for information provided to a government agency. If you need an accommodation or a different language version, contact [L&D].

roles.duties: Complete assigned training and acknowledgments by the deadline, and ask for accommodations or language versions when needed.
Give time for training, follow up on overdue items, and complete manager-specific modules.
Maintain the curriculum matrix, the LMS assignments, reminders, records and reporting.
Own the Code and policy acknowledgments, report certification rates to the Audit Committee, and maintain policy versions.
Map statutory requirements by country, approve content and acknowledgment wording, and track law changes.
Define lab and safety training prerequisites and confirm that access gating works.

countryAddenda.us: State harassment training: New York annual and interactive; Illinois annual; Connecticut 2 hours within 6 months of hire (3+ employees); Delaware within 1 year and every 2 years (50+); Maine within 1 year (15+). Nasdaq Rule 5610 requires a code of conduct, and the insider trading policy is filed as 10-K Exhibit 19, so collect acknowledgments for both. OSHA HazCom and lab training applies to exposed staff, and every acknowledgment needs Rule 21F-17 protected-rights language.
countryAddenda.us-ca: Harassment prevention training (5+ employees): 2 hours for supervisors and 1 hour for non-supervisors within 6 months of hire or promotion and every 2 years, covering abusive conduct, gender identity and expression, and sexual orientation; keep records 2 years. Also required: annual interactive WVPP training (LC 6401.9), IIPP and heat training, and the SB 294 Know Your Rights notice by 1 February each year and at hire. Training records must include the SB 513 fields.
countryAddenda.ca: Ontario: AODA and Human Rights Code training for all staff; OHSA basic awareness training for workers and supervisors (O. Reg. 297/13); and information on the violence and harassment programs. Give the ESA poster and the disconnecting and e-monitoring policies within 30 days of hire. BC: new and young worker orientation before work starts, including bullying and harassment procedures, with an annual policy review.
countryAddenda.in: POSH awareness at induction and every year, plus training for Internal Committee members. Distribute the standing orders or service rules, privacy notice and IT policy with acknowledgment. Display statutory abstracts in English and Kannada or Telugu.
countryAddenda.tw: General OSH training for new hires (typically at least 3 hours) plus lab or hazard training. Publicize the sexual harassment complaint channel (10+ employees) and rules (30+), and the workplace bullying channel and rules from 1 Jul 2026. Distribute the filed work rules, and provide Traditional Chinese versions of all modules and acknowledgments.
countryAddenda.cn: Handbooks and policies that affect vital interests must go through the democratic procedure and be acknowledged (signed or electronically) before they can be relied on (LCL Art. 4), and this is repeated for each amendment. Deliver anti-sexual-harassment training (Women's Rights Law Art. 25), work safety training, and anti-commercial-bribery training for sales and FAE staff. Keep Chinese-language records.

decisions: Link completion to bonus eligibility, or treat it only as a conduct matter? (A bonus link drives completion but may conflict with local wage rules. A conduct approach is universally lawful.)
Train annually or every 2 years for non-statutory modules? (Annual suits the Code, insider trading and export training. Every 2 years reduces fatigue elsewhere.)
Microlearning or long-form modules? (Microlearning improves engagement. Statutory minimum durations still apply in California and Connecticut.)
Which contractors must complete which modules, and who pays?
Which languages to cover beyond statutory needs (e.g., Hindi, Kannada)?
pitfalls: Using non-interactive videos to meet California or New York interactive training rules.
Not triggering California supervisor training within 6 months of a promotion.
English-only policies and acknowledgments in mainland China, or skipping the democratic procedure.
Acknowledgment wording that requires notice to the company before contacting regulators (a Rule 21F-17 violation).
Requiring training outside paid time for non-exempt or hours-regulated employees.
policies.training: This policy defines the training program. Employees acknowledge it at hire, and L&D reviews the curriculum every year.
