policies.name: Employee Privacy & HR Data Protection
policies.approver: General Counsel + CHRO + Chief Privacy Officer
policies.review: Annual + on law change (DPDP May 2027, Taiwan PDPC, CCPA ADMT)
policies.audience: All employees, applicants and contractors whose data we process; everyone who handles HR data, including HR, managers, IT, vendors
policies.purpose: Process applicant, employee, former-employee, contractor and dependant data lawfully, transparently and securely in every country. This includes compliant notices, cross-border transfers from the US-hosted HRIS, rights handling, breach response, and US national-security data rules (the DOJ Data Security Program).
keyProvisions: Scope: personal data in Darwinbox, Greenhouse, payroll, benefits, equity, badge and CCTV systems, investigations, monitoring tools and AI tools, for applicants, employees, former employees, contractors and dependants.

HR data is processed only for documented purposes (recruiting, employment administration, pay and benefits, legal compliance, security and trade-secret protection), limited to what is necessary, kept accurate, and kept only as long as POL-49 allows.
A country privacy notice is given at or before collection. It lists categories, purposes, recipients (including the US parent and vendors), cross-border transfers, retention periods and rights.

Sensitive data (health, biometrics, government ID numbers, bank accounts, criminal records, race or ethnicity and other demographics, union membership) is collected only where necessary, with separate or written consent where the law requires. Access is restricted, and demographic data is stored separately from personnel records.

Data-subject requests go through one intake channel. Identity is verified, and responses meet the strictest applicable deadline (CCPA 45 days; DPDP 90 days; local law otherwise). Legal assesses employment exceptions.

Cross-border transfers run under an intra-group data transfer agreement. China transfers follow the PIPL pathway, Quebec transfers need a PIA, and India and Taiwan transfers are disclosed and monitored for government restrictions.

DOJ Data Security Program: no person resident in mainland China, Hong Kong or Macau, and no China-organized entity or covered vendor, gets access to bulk US sensitive personal data except as an exempt intra-group HR/payroll transfer (s202.506) or under restricted-transaction controls. Global HRIS and identity administrators are not located in those places.
HR vendors are onboarded through DS-06: data processing agreement, security review, restricted-party and covered-person screening, and CCPA service-provider terms.
HRIS access is role-based, with segregation of duties and quarterly user-access reviews (DS-04). Exports of HR data need approval and encryption.

Suspected incidents are reported to the Privacy Office within 1 hour of discovery. The Privacy Office manages regulator and individual notifications (e.g., CERT-In within 6 hours) and escalates to the Disclosure Committee for any Form 8-K Item 1.05 materiality assessment.
Before high-risk processing starts, the required assessment is completed: PIPIA (China), CPPA risk assessment (California), Quebec PIA, or DPIA-equivalent elsewhere.
HR data is not entered into AI tools that are not approved under POL-50.
Everyone who handles HR data completes privacy and security training every year.
policies.sampleLanguage: How we protect your personal information. [Company] collects and uses personal information about applicants, employees and contractors only for legitimate purposes connected with recruitment and employment, such as paying you, providing benefits, meeting legal obligations and keeping our people, systems and technology secure. Your country privacy notice explains what we collect, why, who receives it (including our US parent company and service providers), where it is stored, how long we keep it and your rights. Sensitive information, such as health or biometric data, is collected only when necessary and, where the law requires, with your separate consent, and access to it is strictly limited. You may request access to, correction of or, where applicable, deletion of your information through [Privacy Portal]; we will respond within the time the law requires. Personal information transferred between countries is protected by intra-group agreements and the transfer mechanisms required by local law. If you handle HR data as part of your role, you must access only what you need, keep it secure and report any suspected incident to the Privacy Office within one hour.

roles.duties: Keep their own data up to date, use their rights through the portal, and protect any personal data they handle.
Collect only necessary data, give notices, handle sensitive data under restricted access, and route rights requests to the Privacy Office.
The Privacy Office maintains notices, transfer mechanisms and assessments, handles requests and incidents, and advises on DSP and PIPL.
Run role-based access, encryption, logging and quarterly access reviews for HR systems, and support incident response.
Detect and investigate incidents, and make sure no administrator access sits in DSP countries of concern.
Process HR data only on instructions under the data processing agreement, and report incidents within the contractual deadline.

countryAddenda.us: Outside California there is no omnibus employee privacy law; comply with HIPAA for the group health plan (firewall), FCRA, ADA/GINA/FMLA medical confidentiality, Illinois BIPA, and state SSN and breach laws. Under the DOJ Data Security Program (28 CFR 202), restricted transactions with covered persons (e.g., China-resident employees or China-organized entities) that give access to bulk US sensitive personal data need CISA security controls, a data compliance program and an annual audit. Intra-group HR and payroll transfers are exempt (s202.506), but R&D access is not.
countryAddenda.us-ca: CCPA/CPRA covers employees, applicants and contractors. It requires a notice at collection with a retention period for each category, a privacy policy, rights to know, delete, correct and limit sensitive PI within 45 days (subject to employment-law exceptions), and CCPA terms in vendor contracts. Under the CPPA regulations effective 1 Jan 2026, risk assessments are required for high-risk processing (monitoring, ADMT), with existing processing assessed by 31 Dec 2027 and attestations due 1 Apr 2028; ADMT duties start 1 Jan 2027. Store pay-data demographics separately (SB 464).
countryAddenda.ca: In Ontario, PIPEDA does not cover employee data of provincially regulated employers, so apply BC PIPA-level standards company-wide (intrusion upon seclusion is actionable). Under BC PIPA, employee information may be collected without consent if reasonable for the employment relationship, with notice, and a privacy officer must be designated. Quebec Law 25 requires a PIA before transfer outside Quebec, breach reporting and notice of automated decisions. Watch Bill C-36 (tabled 15 June 2026).
countryAddenda.in: Until 13 May 2027 the SPDI Rules apply: a published privacy policy, written consent for sensitive data (health, biometrics, financial) and a grievance officer. Under the DPDP Act and Rules (notified Nov 2025), consent managers start on 13 Nov 2026, and notice, security, breach reporting (72-hour detailed report to the Board) and rights (90 days) start on 13 May 2027; s.7(i) covers employment purposes. CERT-In requires incident reports within 6 hours, and only masked Aadhaar may be stored.
countryAddenda.tw: PDPA: notice at collection; written consent or a statutory basis for sensitive data (health exams, criminal records); and security maintenance measures (fines up to NT$15M). The 2025 amendment (promulgated 11 Nov 2025) creates the PDPC and mandatory breach reporting, with the effective date to be set by the Executive Yuan (verify); draft rules propose 72-hour reporting. Transfers to US HQ are allowed unless restricted, and must be disclosed.
countryAddenda.cn: PIPL: rely on HR-management necessity under lawfully adopted rules, with separate consent for sensitive PI, third-party provision and cross-border transfer, and keep PIPIAs for 3 years. HR transfers genuinely necessary for cross-border HR management are exempt from filing; otherwise a standard contract or certification is needed (100,000-1M individuals), or a CAC security assessment (over 1M, or over 10,000 sensitive). The amended Cybersecurity Law (from 1 Jan 2026) raises fines to RMB 10M, and a PIPO must be registered above 1M individuals.

decisions: Host the global HRIS in the US only, or keep regional data residency for China HR data? (Residency simplifies PIPL transfers but complicates global reporting and SOX controls.)
One global privacy notice with country annexes, or standalone country notices?
In India after May 2027, rely on the s.7(i) employment basis or on consent for which purposes? (Use consent for voluntary and wellness programs.)
A central privacy request team or HR-handled requests with Privacy oversight?
Collect voluntary demographic data outside countries that require it, and for what purposes?
Which HR vendors may access data from India, Taiwan or China support centers, given DSP and PIPL?
pitfalls: Treating California HR data as outside CCPA: no notice, no retention schedule, no request process.
Moving China employee data into the global HRIS or investigation tools without separate consent and a PIPIA.
Giving China-based IT or HRIS staff administrator access to bulk US employee data (a DSP restricted transaction).
Exporting investigation evidence from China without meeting transfer rules.
Storing full Aadhaar copies or biometric templates without legal basis.
policies.training: All employees: privacy and security awareness at hire and every year. HR, Payroll and HRIS staff: role-based HR data-handling training every year. Acknowledgment of the country privacy notice at hire.

policies.name: Electronic Monitoring & Acceptable Use
policies.owner: Security (IT Security and Insider Risk) with the Privacy Office and HR
policies.review: Annual; for Ontario, confirm by 1 March each year; before any new monitoring tool is deployed
policies.audience: All employees and contractors using [Company] systems, devices, networks or premises
policies.purpose: Set rules for acceptable use of company technology, and disclose honestly what electronic monitoring [Company] does, why, and with what safeguards. The goal is to protect trade secrets, export-controlled technology and systems while meeting notice, consent and proportionality rules (Ontario ESA, New York, California, PIPL, DPDP and PDPA).
keyProvisions: Company systems and devices are provided for business use. Limited, reasonable personal use is allowed if it does not interfere with work or breach policy. Employees should expect monitoring of company systems, as described here.

[Company] may monitor the following, as disclosed in this policy and the country privacy notice: email, chat and collaboration-platform metadata and content; endpoint and DLP telemetry; web proxy and DNS logs; VPN and identity logs; code and design repository access logs; printing; badge access; and CCTV in common areas and labs.

Monitoring is used for security, protecting trade secrets and export-controlled technology, legal compliance, and investigations. It is not used for keystroke logging, screenshots, webcam activation or continuous productivity scoring of individuals.

Only Security has routine access to monitoring data. Reviewing the content of an individual's communications needs written approval from Legal and HR, is limited to a defined purpose and period, and is logged.

Biometric access (fingerprint or face) is optional where the law requires consent. It needs prior written or separate consent and a non-biometric alternative, and templates are deleted within 30 days of exit.
Personal devices (BYOD) may access company data only through a managed container. [Company] may wipe the container, not the personal data.

Prohibited: installing unlicensed or unapproved software; moving company data to personal email or cloud; storing export-controlled or Restricted data outside approved systems; using unapproved generative AI tools with confidential or personal data; bypassing security controls; accessing systems from sanctioned regions.
Recording meetings or calls needs the notice or consent required by local law (all-party consent in California). There is no audio or video recording in restrooms, locker rooms or lactation rooms.
[Company] never asks for passwords or access to employees' personal social media accounts.
Monitoring logs are kept for 12 months by default, unless a legal hold or investigation needs them longer, and then deleted under POL-49.
No new monitoring tool or use goes live until the Privacy Office has completed the required assessment (CPPA risk assessment, PIPIA, Quebec PIA) and updated this policy and the notices.
Monitoring is never used to identify or interfere with legally protected concerted or union activity, or with whistleblower communications to regulators.
Violations may lead to discipline, up to dismissal, and to access restrictions.
policies.sampleLanguage: Electronic monitoring. To protect our people, systems, trade secrets and export-controlled technology, [Company] electronically monitors the use of company-provided systems, networks and devices. This monitoring includes security logging of email and collaboration tools, data loss prevention on company devices, web and network logs, access logs for code and design repositories, badge access records and video surveillance of common areas and laboratories. We monitor for security, legal compliance and the investigation of suspected misconduct; we do not use keystroke logging, screenshots, webcam activation or continuous productivity scoring. Only authorized Security personnel may access monitoring data, and review of the content of an individual's communications requires written approval from Legal and HR. Monitoring data is normally kept for 12 months. We do not record in restrooms, locker rooms or lactation rooms, and we never ask for access to your personal social media accounts. Nothing in this policy restricts your right to discuss terms and conditions of employment or to communicate with government agencies. This policy was prepared on [date] and last changed on [date].

roles.duties: Use company technology responsibly, keep company data in approved systems, and report suspected security incidents.
Operate monitoring tools as disclosed, restrict access to monitoring data, and log content reviews.
The Privacy Office approves new monitoring uses after assessments, keeps notices and the Ontario policy current, and approves content reviews with HR.
Co-approve investigations that need content review, distribute policies (the Ontario 30-day rule), and apply discipline consistently.
Enforce device management, BYOD containers, geo-blocking and approved-software lists.

countryAddenda.us: Give prior written notice of email, phone and internet monitoring, with acknowledgment in New York (Civil Rights Law 52-c) and notices in Connecticut (31-48d) and Delaware (19 Del. C. 705). Before collecting any fingerprint or face data (timeclocks, lab access), get Illinois BIPA consent and publish a retention schedule. Keep monitoring from chilling Section 7 activity.
countryAddenda.us-ca: Disclose monitoring in the CCPA notice, and from 2026 complete a CPPA risk assessment before systematic observation used to infer employee traits (e.g., productivity monitoring). No audio or video in restrooms, locker rooms or changing rooms (LC 435); all-party consent to record confidential communications (Penal Code 632); vehicle tracking only on owned or leased vehicles (637.7); and no demands for access to personal social media (LC 980). Watch AB 1331 and AB 1883 (Governor action due 30 Sep 2026).
countryAddenda.ca: Ontario (25+ employees on 1 January): a written electronic monitoring policy is due by 1 March, stating whether, how, in what circumstances and for what purposes employees are monitored, with preparation and change dates. Give copies within 30 days and keep the policy 3 years after it stops applying (ESA Part XI.1). BC PIPA requires reasonable purposes and notice, and intrusion upon seclusion is actionable in Ontario (Jones v. Tsige).
countryAddenda.in: Disclose email, DLP and CCTV monitoring and their purposes in policy. DPDP s.7(i) supports processing to protect trade secrets and prevent corporate espionage, but monitoring must stay proportionate. Biometrics are sensitive data that need written consent under the SPDI Rules until DPDP duties start on 13 May 2027.
countryAddenda.tw: Disclose email, endpoint and DLP monitoring in policy and in the PDPA notice, and keep it proportionate to protecting trade secrets; covert monitoring risks privacy claims. Documented, disclosed monitoring also helps show 'reasonable protective measures' under the Trade Secrets Act.
countryAddenda.cn: Monitor company systems only with prior notice in the democratically adopted handbook or privacy notice, proportionate to the purpose, and avoid personal chat content. From 1 Jun 2025, facial recognition for attendance or access needs separate consent, a non-biometric alternative, a PIPIA, and provincial CAC filing once face data of 100,000+ individuals is stored. Keep investigation evidence in China unless the cross-border rules are met.

decisions: Use any productivity analytics at all? (It adds CPPA risk-assessment, NLRA and trust issues. Security-only monitoring is easier to defend.)
What threshold and approvers for reviewing an individual's communications content?
Allow BYOD for engineers, or require company devices only? (Company devices only is safer for controlled technology.)
Offer biometric lab access (with consent and an alternative) or badges only?
Which generative AI tools are approved, and with what data rules?
How long to keep logs (6, 12 or 24 months), balancing investigations against minimization?
pitfalls: Undisclosed monitoring, or monitoring beyond what the notice describes.
Collecting biometrics without consent and an alternative (BIPA, PIPL).
Having no Ontario written monitoring policy, or not distributing it within 30 days.
Using DLP or badge data to rate individual performance.
Recording calls in California without all-party consent.
policies.training: Acknowledgment at hire, every year, and on material change (Ontario: copy within 30 days). Security awareness training every year.

policies.name: Confidential Information, IP & Inventions
policies.owner: Legal (IP and Employment) with Security (Insider Risk)
policies.audience: All employees, interns and contractors; hiring managers; departing employees
policies.purpose: Protect [Company]'s chip designs, source code, process and customer information, and make sure the Company owns the inventions and works its people create. Agreements must be enforceable in each country (invention statutes, copyright formalities, non-compete limits) and must preserve whistleblower rights.
keyProvisions: Every employee signs the Proprietary Information and Invention Assignment Agreement (PIIA), or the country version, before starting work (in Canada, before the start date). It includes the DTSA immunity notice, a protected-rights carve-out (SEC Rule 21F-17, NLRA, California Gov Code 12964.5), state invention-law notices and a prior-inventions schedule.

Information is classified as Public, Internal, Confidential or Restricted. Restricted covers RTL, netlists, GDS, PDKs, test programs, roadmaps, pricing, customer NDA material and export-controlled technology, and is handled only on approved systems with need-to-know access.

Employees assign to [Company] all inventions, mask works, designs, software and works of authorship created in the scope of employment or using company resources, as a present assignment. Where local law requires, the agreement names the employer as author (Taiwan), states worldwide territory and perpetual duration (India), and waives moral rights (Canada).

Inventions are disclosed through the invention-disclosure portal within 30 days of conception. Patent awards and statutory inventor remuneration follow the Inventor Reward policy (mandatory in China and relevant in Taiwan).

New hires certify in writing that they bring no prior employer's confidential information. Hires from direct competitors, foundries, or Entity-List-affiliated companies get an access review and project wall-offs as Legal directs.
Third-party confidential information (customer NDAs, foundry PDKs, EDA licenses) is used only as the governing agreement allows, and access is restricted to named users.
Outside activities, open-source contributions, publications and talks that relate to [Company]'s business need pre-approval (POL-03 and the publication-review process).
Company code and design data may be used only with generative AI tools that are approved for that purpose under POL-50.
Export-controlled technology is also governed by the Technology Control Plan (POL-18). Access is revoked immediately when a role changes or employment ends.

Post-employment non-competes are used only where lawful and compensated (Taiwan LSA Art. 9-1; China for eligible staff). They are not used in California, Ontario (below the C-suite) or India, and narrow non-solicits are used only where enforceable.
Suspected misappropriation is reported immediately to Security and Legal. Employees and managers do not investigate on their own.

Nothing in this policy or any agreement stops anyone from reporting possible violations of law to a government agency, taking part in an investigation, or receiving a government award. Disclosure in confidence to government officials or an attorney for that purpose is immune under the DTSA.
policies.sampleLanguage: Confidential information and inventions. In your work you will create and have access to information that is critical to [Company]'s success, including chip designs, source code, test methods, product roadmaps and information entrusted to us by customers and foundry partners. You must use this information only for [Company]'s business, store it only in approved systems, share it only with people who need it, and return it when your employment ends. Inventions, designs, mask works, software and other works you create within the scope of your employment or using [Company] resources belong to [Company], and you must disclose inventions promptly through [Invention Portal]. Do not bring or use confidential information belonging to a former employer or anyone else. Notice under 18 U.S.C. 1833(b): you will not be held liable under any federal or state trade secret law for disclosing a trade secret in confidence to a government official or an attorney solely for the purpose of reporting or investigating a suspected violation of law, or in a sealed court filing. Nothing in this policy limits your right to communicate with any government agency.

roles.duties: Sign the PIIA before starting, handle information according to its classification, disclose inventions, and report suspected leaks.
Enforce need-to-know access, approve outside activities through the process, and make sure new hires are clean-room onboarded.
Maintain country agreements and invention notices, run invention disclosure and inventor rewards, and lead misappropriation responses.
Run DLP and insider-risk monitoring, access reviews and exit forensics, and preserve evidence.
Make sure agreements are signed before start, send outside-activity requests to Legal, and run exit certifications with Security.
Align the TCP with information classification, and screen new-hire and project access for export control.

countryAddenda.us: Include the DTSA immunity notice (18 U.S.C. 1833(b)) in every agreement governing confidential information, or lose exemplary damages and fees against that individual. Add state invention carve-out notices (e.g., IL, MN, WA, DE, NJ, NY), plus Rule 21F-17 and NLRA savings language. Non-competes are void in MN, ND, OK and WY, and from 30 Jun 2027 in WA, where notices to affected workers are due by 1 Oct 2027.
countryAddenda.us-ca: PIIAs must give written notice of LC 2870 (LC 2872): inventions developed entirely on the employee's own time without company equipment, supplies, facilities or trade secrets are excluded, unless they relate to the company's business or R&D or result from company work. Non-competes and most non-solicits are void even if signed elsewhere (B&P 16600-16600.5); no non-California law or forum clauses are allowed (LC 925); and NDAs must include the Gov Code 12964.5 carve-out.
countryAddenda.ca: Canada has no statutory employee-invention regime, so use an express present-tense assignment, a disclosure duty and a prior-inventions schedule signed before the start date. Copyright in work made in the course of employment vests in the employer (Copyright Act s.13(3)), but moral rights can only be waived (s.14.1). Ontario bans employee non-competes except for the C-suite and on the sale of a business (ESA s.67.2), and Criminal Code s.391 criminalizes obtaining trade secrets by deceit.
countryAddenda.in: Copyright in works made in the course of employment belongs to the employer (s.17(c)), but assignments must state duration and territory or they default to 5 years and India only (s.19); patents need an express assignment. There is no trade-secret statute, so protection relies on contract, equity and injunctions. Post-employment non-competes are void (Contract Act s.27), while in-term exclusivity, garden leave and reasonable employee non-solicits can be used; stamp the agreement.
countryAddenda.tw: Name the employer as author of work-made copyrights (Copyright Act Art. 11) and deal with service-invention remuneration (Patent Act Art. 7). Maintain 'reasonable protective measures' (Trade Secrets Act) and document best-efforts prevention to avoid corporate fines (Art. 13-4). Misappropriating national core key technologies (e.g., AI/HPC chip design, chiplet interconnect design) carries up to 12 years under the National Security Act, and non-competes must meet Art. 9-1 (at most 2 years, at least 50% compensation, in writing).
countryAddenda.cn: Service inventions belong to the employer (Patent Law Art. 6), but inventor reward and remuneration are mandatory, so adopt a policy to avoid the statutory defaults (Art. 15). Protect trade secrets with measures that qualify under the AUCL (revised 15 Oct 2025). Non-competes are allowed only for senior management, senior technical staff and staff bound by confidentiality, for at most 2 years, with monthly post-exit compensation of at least 30% of prior 12-month average pay (generally 50% if over 1 year; MOHRSS 2025 Guidelines). They are void for staff without trade-secret access (SPC Interpretation II Art. 13).

decisions: Use paid non-competes in Taiwan and China for key design engineers? (They are enforceable if compliant but cost 30-50% or more of pay during the restriction. Compare with garden leave and trade-secret enforcement.)
Patent award amounts and structure (filing and issuance awards), in line with the China and Taiwan remuneration duties?
Open-source contribution policy: pre-approval for every contribution, or approved project lists?
Allow company code in generative AI tools, and only on enterprise-licensed, no-training instances?
Mandatory classification labels on design files and documents, or classification by repository?
How far clean-room certification goes for hires from foundries and direct competitors?
pitfalls: PIIAs without the DTSA notice, which loses exemplary damages and fees.
Using generic US assignment language in India, which defaults to 5 years and India only.
Leaving Taiwan employees as the authors of work-made copyrights.
Signing non-competes with all China engineers and then not paying monthly compensation.
Having Canadian PIIAs signed after the start date without fresh consideration.
Relying on customer or employee non-solicits against California employees.
policies.training: PIIA signed before the start date. Trade-secret and information-classification training at hire and every year, and exit certification at departure.

policies.name: HR Records Retention
policies.owner: HR Operations (People Ops) with Legal (Records Management)
policies.audience: HR, Payroll, Benefits, TA, EHS, Legal, IT and managers who create or hold HR records
policies.purpose: Keep HR records for as long as the law and business need require, and no longer. Legal holds must be applied reliably, and retention must match privacy notices (CCPA, DPDP, PIPL, PDPA). Records must also support the employer's burden of proof in Taiwan and mainland China disputes.
keyProvisions: Legal maintains a retention schedule in Document management by record category and country: recruiting, right-to-work, personnel file, payroll, time and attendance, benefits, medical and leave, investigations, training, safety, equity, immigration, export, monitoring logs and AI/ADS data.

For each category, the retention period is the longest one that applies in the country where the employee works. Global copies held in the US HRIS follow the employee's country period unless a US rule is longer.

Examples: US I-9s, the later of 3 years after hire or 1 year after termination; FLSA payroll 3 years; California applications and ADS data 4 years; Canada payroll 6 years; Taiwan wage and attendance records 5 years; China terminated contracts at least 2 years; EAR export records 5 years; exposure and medical records for the length of employment plus 30 years.
Medical, accommodation, I-9, investigation and demographic (self-identification) records are kept in separate restricted files, never in the general personnel file.

Legal holds (ER-09) override all destruction. Legal tells the record owners and IT within 1 business day, automatic deletion is suspended for the covered custodians and systems, and holds are reviewed every quarter.
When the retention period ends, records are securely destroyed or anonymized, destruction is logged, and vendors certify destruction. Nothing under hold is destroyed.

Candidate data is kept for [4] years in the US (California requirement, applied US-wide). Elsewhere it is kept for 2 years unless the candidate consents to a talent pool; Ontario posting and interview records are kept 3 years.

Statutory registers are kept in the required format and language: India's unified electronic registers, Taiwan's minute-level attendance and employee roster, and China's Chinese-language contracts and wage records.

Requests from employees and former employees for access to records are handled by People Ops within the legal deadline (e.g., California personnel file 30 days, payroll 21 days; Taiwan attendance copies on request).
Privacy notices state retention periods by category (required by CCPA). Personal data is deleted when its purpose ends, subject to legal minimums and holds.
Every year, each record owner certifies compliance with the schedule, and Internal Audit tests it periodically.
System migrations keep the retention metadata and legal holds, and Legal approves them before the legacy system is decommissioned.
policies.sampleLanguage: Keeping and disposing of HR records. [Company] keeps HR records only for as long as the law requires and our business reasonably needs them, as set out in the HR Records Retention Schedule maintained by Legal. The schedule sets a retention period for each category of record in each country; where more than one rule applies, the longest period governs. Medical, accommodation, immigration verification, investigation and voluntary self-identification records must be kept separately from personnel files, with access restricted to those who need it. When a retention period ends, records must be securely destroyed or anonymized, and the destruction must be documented. However, if Legal issues a legal hold notice, you must preserve all records described in the notice, including emails, chat messages and files on any device, until Legal tells you in writing that the hold has been released. Automatic deletion will be suspended for records under hold. If you are unsure whether a record may be destroyed, ask Legal before disposing of it.

roles.duties: HR Operations applies the schedule in Darwinbox and Document management, separates restricted files, and handles record-access requests.
Maintains the schedule, issues and releases legal holds, and approves destruction exceptions and migrations.
Configures automated retention and deletion, suspends deletion for holds, and keeps deletion logs.
Keeps payroll and tax records for the statutory periods (e.g., CRA 6 years, US 4 years for tax).
Keeps and destroys HR records as the contract instructs, and certifies destruction.

countryAddenda.us: I-9: the later of 3 years after hire or 1 year after termination, stored separately. FLSA payroll 3 years (timecards 2); Title VII/ADA personnel records 1 year (until final disposition once a charge is filed); FMLA 3 years. OSHA 300 logs 5 years and exposure or medical records for employment plus 30 years; ERISA 6 years; payroll tax 4 years. FCRA reports 5 years as a litigation-safe practice, and EAR export records 5 years.
countryAddenda.us-ca: Applications, personnel records and ADS data: 4 years (Gov Code 12946; CRD regs). Personnel files 3 years after termination (LC 1198.5); payroll and wage statements 3 years (4 recommended); job title and wage history for employment plus 3 years (LC 432.3). PSL records 3 years, harassment training 2 years, WVPP incident and hazard records 5 years (training 1 year), and SB 294 notices 3 years. The CCPA notice must state a retention period for each category.
countryAddenda.ca: CRA payroll and tax records and ROE records: 6 years from the end of the tax year. Ontario ESA employee and wage records 3 years; job postings, applications and interview-outcome notices 3 years; disconnecting and e-monitoring policies 3 years after they stop applying. BC ESA payroll records 4 years after employment ends (verify), and foreign-worker documents 6 years; keep harassment investigation files for the limitation period plus any hold.
countryAddenda.in: Keep the Labour Codes' unified electronic registers (employee, wages, attendance, overtime, deductions, leave) for the period the state rules set (verify; typically 3+ years), and tax records 6+ years. Under DPDP (from 13 May 2027), erase personal data once the purpose is served but keep processing logs for at least 1 year. CERT-In requires ICT logs to be kept for 180 days in India.
countryAddenda.tw: Employee roster: 5 years after departure (LSA Art. 7). Wage and minute-level attendance records: 5 years (Arts. 23, 30). Health exam records: at least 7 years (longer for special hazards). Missing records shift the burden of proof to the employer under the Labor Incident Act, and candidate and former-employee data is deleted or anonymized once retention and limitation periods end (PDPA Art. 11).
countryAddenda.cn: Terminated or expired labor contracts: at least 2 years (LCL Art. 50); wage payment records at least 2 years. PIPIA reports and processing records 3 years, accounting vouchers 30 years. Keep attendance and wage evidence, because the employer bears the burden of proof in disputes, and delete or anonymize personal information when its purpose ends (PIPL Art. 47).

decisions: One global 'longest period' schedule, or country-specific periods? (A global schedule is simpler but over-retains, which conflicts with DPDP, PIPL and CCPA minimization.)
Keep candidate talent pools longer with consent? (This helps recruiting but needs consent management in India, China and Taiwan.)
How long to keep investigation files after closure (e.g., limitation period plus 1 year)?
Email and chat retention defaults (e.g., 2-3 years) balanced against e-discovery cost?
Digitize and destroy legacy paper files, or keep originals where evidence rules prefer them (China, Taiwan)?
pitfalls: Over-retaining everything 'just in case', which breaches privacy minimization and increases breach impact.
Destroying records under legal hold because automatic deletion was never suspended.
Keeping I-9s or medical records in the general personnel file.
Leaving the retention period for each category out of the CCPA notice.
Losing minute-level attendance or Chinese-language wage records needed to defend claims.
policies.training: Record owners get annual training on the schedule and certify compliance. Legal hold recipients acknowledge each notice.

policies.name: AI in Employment Decisions
policies.owner: HR Technology with Legal (Employment and Privacy) and HR Analytics
policies.approver: CHRO + General Counsel + AI Governance Committee
policies.review: Every 6 months + before any new tool or material change
policies.audience: HR, Talent Acquisition, managers, HR Technology, vendors, and all applicants and employees affected by AI tools
policies.purpose: Govern the use of AI, automated decision systems (ADS) and automated decision-making technology (ADMT) in recruiting and employment. Every tool must be inventoried, bias-tested, disclosed, accessible and subject to real human judgment, in line with the California CRD and CCPA rules, NYC Local Law 144, Illinois HB 3773, Colorado SB 26-189, Ontario posting disclosure and PIPL Art. 24.
keyProvisions: Scope: any AI, ADS or ADMT, including vendor features in Greenhouse, Darwinbox or assessment platforms, that screens, ranks, scores, interviews, evaluates, sets pay, allocates work, promotes, disciplines or terminates, or that predicts attrition or productivity.
No such tool is used until it is registered in the AI Register through DS-06, risk-tiered and approved by the AI Governance Committee. Shadow use of unapproved tools is prohibited.

No hiring, promotion, pay, discipline or termination decision is made solely by an automated system. A named, trained human decision-maker reviews the output, has authority to override it, and records the reasons.

High-risk tools are tested for adverse impact before deployment and at least once a year, by sex, race/ethnicity and age where data is lawfully available. NYC-covered tools get an independent bias audit with a published summary. Legal decides when testing is done under privilege.

Candidates and employees get the legally required notice before a tool is used (e.g., NYC at least 10 business days; Illinois; Ontario postings; California ADMT pre-use notice from 1 Jan 2027; Colorado from 1 Jan 2027). As company standard, every job posting discloses AI use in screening.
An alternative process or a human review is always available on request, and accommodations for disability are provided (e.g., alternatives to timed or video-analysis assessments).
People who get an adverse decision that a tool materially influenced receive a plain-language explanation on request (Colorado within 30 days; PIPL Art. 24), and can correct inaccurate data.

Prohibited uses: emotion or facial-expression analysis in interviews; inferring protected characteristics; zip code or other proxy variables for protected traits; and using predicted attrition or health risk to make adverse decisions.
Inputs and outputs of employment AI tools are kept for 4 years (the California requirement, applied globally where lawful) and minimized in line with POL-46.

Vendor contracts give audit and testing cooperation, disclosure of model changes, limits on data use (no training on [Company] data without approval), accessibility commitments, and indemnities where they can be obtained.

Employees may use approved generative AI tools to help draft job descriptions or feedback, but they remain accountable for the content and may not enter confidential or personal data into tools that are not approved.
HR Analytics monitors outcomes every quarter. Any suspected discriminatory effect is escalated, and the tool may be suspended.
This policy is reviewed every 6 months because of pending changes (e.g., California SB 947 and the EEOC's review of UGESP).
policies.sampleLanguage: Use of artificial intelligence in employment decisions. [Company] may use tools that rely on artificial intelligence or automated processing to help recruit, assess and manage our workforce, such as tools that help match applicants to job requirements or schedule interviews. We use these tools only after they have been reviewed and approved, tested for bias, and, where required by law, disclosed to you in advance. Automated tools do not make final decisions about hiring, promotion, pay, discipline or termination: a trained person reviews the relevant information, may disregard the tool's output, and is responsible for the decision. If you would prefer an alternative assessment method, or need an accommodation because of a disability, contact [Recruiting/HR] and we will provide one. If a decision about you was materially influenced by an automated tool, you may ask for an explanation of the main factors and correct any inaccurate information. We do not use tools that analyze facial expressions or emotions, or that attempt to infer protected characteristics.

roles.duties: Use only registered tools, give the required notices and alternatives, and make sure a human reviews every screening decision.
Treat tool outputs as input only, record the reasons for decisions, and request accommodations or alternatives when needed.
Run pre-deployment and periodic adverse-impact testing, monitor outcomes every quarter, and support independent audits.
Map legal duties by jurisdiction, approve notices and privileged testing, review vendor contracts, and track pending laws.
HR Technology maintains the AI Register, configures and logs tools, keeps data for 4 years, and enforces the ban on unapproved tools.
Provide model documentation, bias-testing support, change notices and data-use limits as the contract requires.

countryAddenda.us: NYC Local Law 144: an annual independent bias audit, a published summary, and notice at least 10 business days before using an AEDT for NYC candidates or employees. Illinois HB 3773 (from 1 Jan 2026): notice of AI use, no discriminatory effect and no zip-code proxies (IDHR postponed its notice rules on 2 Jun 2026, but the statute applies). Colorado SB 26-189 (effective 1 Jan 2027): notice of AI use in consequential decisions, a plain-language explanation within 30 days of an adverse decision, data correction and human review. Title VII disparate-impact liability still applies.
countryAddenda.us-ca: CRD ADS regulations (effective 1 Oct 2025): discriminatory ADS outcomes violate FEHA, employers are liable for vendors acting as their agents, anti-bias testing informs defenses, accommodation is required, and ADS inputs and outputs are kept 4 years. CCPA ADMT rules for significant decisions start 1 Jan 2027: pre-use notice, opt-out or a qualifying human appeal, and access and explanation rights, with a risk assessment required now. SB 947 (Governor action due 30 Sep 2026; operative 1 Jul 2027 if signed) would bar relying mainly on ADS for discipline or termination.
countryAddenda.ca: Ontario (25+ employees, since 1 Jan 2026): publicly advertised postings must disclose any AI used to screen, assess or select applicants. Quebec Law 25 requires notice when a decision is based exclusively on automated processing, and a right to have it reviewed. Assess tools for Human Rights Code bias, and give notice of purposes under BC PIPA.
countryAddenda.in: There is no AI-specific employment statute. From 13 May 2027, the DPDP requires notice, purpose limitation, accuracy and security for personal data used in AI tools, plus rights to correction and grievance. Test tools for gender, disability and transgender discrimination under Code on Wages s.3, the RPwD Act and the Transgender Persons Act.
countryAddenda.tw: There is no AI-specific employment statute (verify). PDPA notice and purpose limits apply to candidate and employee data processed by AI tools, and Employment Services Act Art. 5 bars discrimination and requests for data that is not job-related. Keep human review for Art. 11 decisions, which require documented, objective evidence.
countryAddenda.cn: PIPL Art. 24: automated decision-making must be transparent and fair, and individuals may request an explanation and refuse decisions made solely by automated means that significantly affect their rights. A PIPIA is required before automated decision-making (Art. 55). The algorithm-recommendation and generative-AI service rules (2022-2023) may apply to some HR tools (verify applicability).

decisions: Allow AI-based resume screening at all, or only scheduling and administrative automation? (Screening saves recruiter time for high-volume new-grad hiring but carries the heaviest legal duties.)
Commission independent bias audits beyond NYC for all high-risk tools? (This strengthens defenses under the CRD rules and Title VII, at a cost.)
Offer an opt-out or human alternative globally, or only where the law requires? (A global approach simplifies operations and builds trust.)
Allow generative AI to help write performance reviews, and with what disclosure?
Build tools in-house or buy them? (Vendor tools still leave the employer liable as the vendor's principal under the CRD rules.)
Use productivity or attrition-prediction analytics, and with what limits on individual-level use?
pitfalls: Relying on a vendor's claim of compliance without testing or contractual audit rights.
Having no inventory, so features are switched on in the ATS without review.
Ontario postings that do not disclose AI screening.
Not keeping ADS inputs and outputs for 4 years (California).
Automated rejections with no human review, especially knockout questions scored by AI.
policies.training: Recruiters, HRBPs and people managers using AI tools: training before access and every year. The AI Governance Committee is briefed every 6 months on regulatory changes.

policies.name: Health & Safety
policies.approver: SVP Operations + CHRO; annual report to the CEO
policies.review: Annual (Ontario, BC and Taiwan require at least annual program reviews) + after any serious incident
policies.audience: All employees, contractors and visitors at [Company] sites; employees working remotely or visiting foundry, OSAT and customer sites
policies.purpose: Keep people safe in offices and in the validation, characterization, reliability, failure-analysis and RF/photonics labs of a fabless semiconductor company, and when employees visit foundry and OSAT cleanrooms or work from home. Written programs, committees, training, incident reporting and regulator notifications must meet the law in every country.
keyProvisions: [Company] runs a health and safety management system aligned with ISO 45001. It names a responsible person for each site, does risk assessments, sets controls, trains people, investigates incidents and reviews the system every year.

Each site has a written hazard assessment and a job hazard analysis for lab work, covering chemicals and solvents (decapsulation acids), compressed and toxic gases, lasers, X-ray and inspection equipment, high-voltage benches, thermal chambers and solder fumes, as well as ergonomics and working alone.

Required written programs are kept current for each site: the California IIPP and WVPP; hazard communication and lab chemical hygiene; emergency action and fire prevention; laser safety (ANSI Z136) with a laser safety officer; electrical safety (NFPA 70E); radiation equipment registration; heat illness where applicable; and working-alone procedures.
Nobody enters a lab until the lab-specific safety training in the LMS is complete and the lab manager has signed off. PPE is provided at no cost.

Employees report all injuries, illnesses, near misses and hazards to their manager and EHS within 24 hours. EHS notifies regulators within the statutory deadlines (e.g., US fatality 8 hours and hospitalization 24 hours; Cal/OSHA serious injury 8 hours; Taiwan 8 hours; Ontario WSIB 3 business days; WorkSafeBC 3 days).

Safety committees and representatives are set up wherever the law requires (Ontario JHSC at 20+ workers; BC JOHSC at 20+; China safety function above 100 employees) and meet at least quarterly. Worker members are consulted on changes.
Pregnant, post-partum and nursing employees get a reproductive-hazard risk assessment and adjustments. Reassignment happens by consent at no loss of pay, and nobody is excluded against their wishes.
Every employee may stop or refuse work they reasonably believe is unsafe and report hazards without retaliation.
Contractors and visitors get a site safety induction and are escorted in labs. Contractor safety performance is part of vendor selection.
Workplace violence and harassment prevention (POL-09, POL-10, POL-11) is part of the program, including site-specific violence prevention plans where required.
Remote workers complete a home-workspace self-assessment and receive ergonomic equipment. Work injuries at home are reported like any other.
Occupational health surveillance (pre-placement, periodic and exit exams) is provided for exposed roles where the law or a risk assessment requires it.
Every quarter EHS reports leading and lagging indicators (training completion, inspections, near misses, TRIR) to site leadership and every year to the executive team.
policies.sampleLanguage: Health and safety. Everyone at [Company] has the right to a safe workplace and a responsibility to work safely. Before you enter any laboratory, you must complete the safety training assigned to you and be authorized by the lab manager; you must follow the lab's written procedures and use the protective equipment provided at no cost to you. Report every injury, illness, near miss or hazard to your manager and to EHS within 24 hours, even if it seems minor, including injuries while working from home or visiting a partner's facility. If you reasonably believe a task is unsafe, you may stop and ask for help, and you will not be penalized for doing so. If you are pregnant, breastfeeding or planning a pregnancy and work with chemicals, radiation or other potential reproductive hazards, you may request a confidential risk assessment; any adjustment will be made with your agreement and without loss of pay. Contractors and visitors must complete a site induction and be escorted in laboratories. Managers are responsible for making sure their teams are trained and that hazards are corrected promptly.

roles.duties: Complete training, follow procedures and PPE rules, report incidents and hazards within 24 hours, and stop unsafe work.
Make sure their teams are trained and authorized, correct hazards, take part in investigations, and support people returning to work.
Maintain the written programs and risk assessments, notify regulators, run committees, investigate incidents and report metrics.
Maintain safe buildings, emergency systems and lab infrastructure (ventilation, gas monitoring, interlocks).
Coordinate workers' compensation and work-injury claims, accommodation and return-to-work, and the handling of reproductive-hazard cases.
Worker members of the joint health and safety committees (Ontario, BC) and Taiwan labor representatives take part in inspections and consultation.

countryAddenda.us: OSHA requires written emergency action and fire prevention plans (more than 10 employees), a HazCom program (2024 update phase-in; verify dates) and a Chemical Hygiene Plan for labs (29 CFR 1910.1450). Keep 300/300A/301 records, post the 300A from 1 Feb to 30 Apr, and submit through ITA by 2 March where covered. Report fatalities within 8 hours and inpatient hospitalizations, amputations or eye loss within 24 hours. Follow ANSI Z136 for lasers, register X-ray equipment with the state, and buy workers' comp in every work state.
countryAddenda.us-ca: California requires a written IIPP (8 CCR 3203) and a site-specific WVPP with annual interactive training, a violent incident log and 5-year records (LC 6401.9). The indoor heat plan applies at 82 F, with controls at 87 F or at 82 F where clean-room garments restrict heat removal (8 CCR 3396); HazCom (5194), lab chemical hygiene (5191) and Prop 65 also apply. Report serious injuries to Cal/OSHA within 8 hours, and allow employees to leave during emergency conditions (LC 1139); the Cal/OSHA general-industry workplace violence standard is due by 31 Dec 2026.
countryAddenda.ca: Ontario: a written OHS policy reviewed every year and posted at 6+ workers; a JHSC at 20+ (health and safety representative at 6-19); violence and harassment policies and programs, including virtual harassment, reviewed every year; WHMIS; and injury reports to WSIB (Form 7) within 3 business days. BC: a formal OHS program at 50+ workers (or 20+ with moderate hazards such as labs), a JOHSC at 20+ and a worker representative at 10-19, a first-aid assessment, working-alone procedures, and reports to WorkSafeBC within 3 days.
countryAddenda.in: Under the OSH Code, establishments with 10+ workers register and must keep the workplace free of hazards with the required welfare facilities. Validation or test labs with 20+ workers using power (40+ without) may count as 'factories', which brings licensing, a safety committee and hazardous-process duties. Provide annual health check-ups for employees aged 40+ where the rules prescribe them (the Karnataka draft rules are broader; verify), report serious accidents as the rules require, and apply the safeguards for women on night shifts.
countryAddenda.tw: The OSH Act requires an OSH plan and management personnel by risk category, with labs, test and fab areas classed as high-risk. Occupational health services must be contracted at 50-299 workers, with employed nurses at 300+, and written plans for workplace violence, overwork and maternal health are required at 100+ workers. The workplace bullying chapter applies from 1 Jul 2026 (complaint channel at 10+ employees, full rules at 30+, MOL case registration, fines NT$30,000-750,000). Report deaths, 3+ injuries or any hospitalization within 8 hours.
countryAddenda.cn: The Work Safety Law (2021) requires a safety responsibility system, training and hazard checks, and enterprises with over 100 employees need a safety management function or full-time safety staff. Under the Occupational Disease Prevention Law, provide hazard notices, PPE and pre-, on- and exit-job health exams for exposed lab staff (no termination without an exit exam), and follow the hazardous chemicals regulations. Apply for work-injury recognition within 30 days and observe female-employee job restrictions.

decisions: Seek ISO 45001 certification, or only align with it? (Certification helps with customer and RBA audits but adds audit cost.)
Central EHS team or site-level EHS coordinators? (A central team gives consistency. Site coordinators give responsiveness in Hsinchu, Bengaluru and Shanghai.)
Control lab access by badge, linked to LMS training status? (Strong control. It needs HRIS, LMS and badge-system integration.)
How to manage contractors in labs (pre-qualification, supervision)?
Include safety metrics in the operations leaders' bonus modifiers? (Use leading indicators to avoid discouraging reporting.)
pitfalls: Assuming a fabless company has no significant hazards and running labs without a chemical hygiene plan or laser program.
Ignoring the California indoor heat rule where clean-room gowning restricts heat removal.
Excluding pregnant employees from labs instead of offering assessment and choice.
Not recording work-related injuries of remote employees.
Terminating China lab staff exposed to hazards without an exit health exam.
policies.training: All employees: safety orientation at hire (Ontario awareness training; BC orientation; Taiwan at least 3 hours). Lab staff: role-specific training before access and a refresher every year. California: annual WVPP training. Committee members: certification training where required.

policies.name: Resignation, Notice & Garden Leave
policies.audience: All employees; managers, HRBPs, Security and Payroll
policies.purpose: Handle voluntary resignations consistently. This covers notice, early release, garden leave, counter-offers and the protection of trade secrets and export-controlled technology, while meeting each country's final-pay deadlines and exit documents.
keyProvisions: Employees resign in writing (email or Darwinbox) to their manager and HR. Within 1 business day HR confirms the last working day, final pay timing and the offboarding checklist.

Notice follows the country schedule and the employment contract: US 2 weeks requested; California none required; Canada as in the contract (typically 2-4 weeks); India as in the contract (typically 30-90 days); Taiwan LSA Art. 16 (10/20/30 days); China 30 days (3 days during probation).
[Company] may waive all or part of the notice. Where local law requires, it pays through the notice period or treats early release as a termination (e.g., California, Ontario, Taiwan by agreement).

Where the contract allows or the employee agrees, [Company] may put the employee on paid garden leave for the notice period. The employee stays employed with full pay and benefits, does no work for any other employer, and has system and site access limited as Security directs. Vesting continues only as the plan terms provide.

High-risk departures, such as moves to a competitor, foundry, PRC-linked company or customer, or departures of employees with Restricted or export-controlled access, trigger ER-10. Security narrows access immediately and reviews downloads and uploads from the previous 30-90 days, and Legal reminds the employee of their obligations.
Counter-offers need VP and Total Rewards approval and must fit internal pay equity. No one is treated unfavorably for resigning or for turning down a counter-offer.
Whether a resignation may be withdrawn before its effective date is decided by [Company] and confirmed in writing. There is no automatic right to withdraw except where local law provides one.
Final pay, accrued vacation or leave payouts and statutory amounts are paid by the local deadline. Clearance steps run in parallel and never delay statutory payments.

Vesting of equity awards stops on the termination date unless the plan says otherwise. Departing employees are told their exercise windows (e.g., 3 months for ISOs) and that insider-trading restrictions continue until the policy says they end.
Departures of Section 16 officers and named executive officers are reported to Legal on the day notice is received, for any Form 8-K Item 5.02 filing within 4 business days.
Statutory exit documents are issued on time: service or termination certificates, relieving letters, ROE, separation notices.

Every departing employee is invited to the exit survey or interview (OF-07), which asks whether they know of any unreported compliance concerns. The rehire-eligibility decision is recorded under OF-10.
policies.sampleLanguage: Resigning from [Company]. If you decide to resign, please give written notice to your manager and HR through [Darwinbox] or by email, observing the notice period in your employment agreement or required by local law. HR will confirm your last working day, how and when you will receive your final pay and any statutory documents, and the steps for returning [Company] property. [Company] may, at its discretion, release you before the end of your notice period; where local law or your agreement requires, you will be paid for the remainder of the notice period. [Company] may also place you on paid garden leave for all or part of your notice period, during which you remain an employee, continue to receive your pay and benefits, must not perform work for any other organization, and may have limited access to systems and premises. Your obligations regarding confidential information, inventions, export-controlled technology and insider trading continue after you leave. We will invite you to share feedback in an exit survey, including any concerns about compliance that you have not already reported.

roles.duties: Give written notice, hand over work, return property, and complete the exit certification and survey.
Tell HR within 1 business day, plan the handover, flag high-risk departures, and not retaliate or make unapproved counter-offers.
Confirm dates and the checklist, issue statutory documents, and coordinate final pay and benefits.
Narrow access and review data movement for high-risk departures, and run the exit forensic protocol where needed.
Pay final wages, notice pay and leave payouts by the local deadlines.
Handle trade-secret, non-compete and Section 16 matters, and send reminder letters.

countryAddenda.us: Neither side owes statutory notice; two weeks is customary. If the Company accepts a resignation early, some states then require prompt final pay, and UI eligibility can change (e.g., NY, IL). Garden leave is not statutory except in Massachusetts, where garden leave at 50% of base or other agreed consideration supports a non-compete, and a Section 16 officer's departure triggers Form 8-K Item 5.02 within 4 business days of notice.
countryAddenda.us-ca: No notice may be required and no quit fees may be charged (AB 692). With 72+ hours' notice, final pay (including accrued vacation) is due on the last day, and without notice within 72 hours (LC 202). If the Company brings the separation date forward, it either pays through the notice period or treats the change as a discharge and pays immediately. Garden leave during notice is lawful, but no post-employment non-compete or non-solicit may follow it.
countryAddenda.ca: Neither ESA requires resignation notice, but at common law employees owe reasonable notice (usually the contractual 2-4 weeks). In Ontario, waiving the notice early can amount to a dismissal, so pay out the notice period (at least the ESA portion); garden leave needs a contractual right or consent. Final pay: BC within 6 days of quitting; Ontario by the later of 7 days or the next regular payday. Resignations must be clear and unequivocal.
countryAddenda.in: Contractual notice applies (60-90 days is market practice for engineers). The Company may waive it, accept a buyout or place the employee on paid garden leave, but cannot force the employee to work. Final wages are due within 2 working days of the last working day (Code on Wages s.17(2)), and in Karnataka a service certificate is due within 7 days of request. Do not withhold relieving letters or keep original certificates, and have a written rule on accepting withdrawn resignations.
countryAddenda.tw: Employees resign on LSA Art. 16 notice (10/20/30 days by tenure); longer contractual notice or resignation penalties are generally unenforceable. The Company may release the employee early by agreement and pay through the agreed date; garden leave requires full pay, and leave keeps accruing. Issue a service certificate on request (Art. 19) and settle wages and unused leave immediately.
countryAddenda.cn: Employees give 30 days' written notice (3 days during probation), no employer acceptance is needed, and longer contractual notice is unenforceable. There is no statutory garden leave, but an earlier release date can be agreed with pay to that date. Issue the termination certificate, transfer the personnel file and social insurance within 15 days, and decide at exit whether to activate or release any non-compete.

decisions: Default response to resignations: accept the full notice, release early, or garden leave for departures to competitors? (Garden leave protects IP but keeps paying salary. Early release reduces risk but may trigger pay-in-lieu duties.)
Standard notice periods in India offer letters (60 vs 90 days)? (Longer periods protect projects but make hiring harder and encourage buyouts.)
Counter-offer policy: allowed, discouraged or prohibited above certain levels?
Allow resignations to be withdrawn, and who decides?
Which departures count as 'high-risk' and trigger forensic review?
pitfalls: Accepting a California resignation early but paying final wages on the original date.
Waiving an Ontario employee's notice without paying at least the ESA portion.
Withholding Indian relieving letters or experience certificates to force the notice period to be served.
Relying on 60-90 day contractual notice clauses in Taiwan or China.
Forgetting the China non-compete activation decision at exit.
policies.training: Acknowledgment at hire. Managers: offboarding and high-risk-departure briefing on appointment. People Ops: country final-pay refresher every year.

policies.name: Termination of Employment
policies.owner: Employee Relations with HR Business Partners
policies.audience: Managers, HRBPs, Employee Relations, Legal, Payroll, IT/Security; all employees for transparency
policies.purpose: Make sure every involuntary termination (for performance, conduct or other individual reasons) rests on a documented, lawful basis under local law, goes through independent HR and Legal review, is delivered respectfully, and comes with correct final pay, documents and access removal. Terminations in countries without at-will employment need particular care.
keyProvisions: No involuntary termination goes ahead without review by the HRBP and Employee Relations. Legal also reviews terminations of employees who are protected, senior (Director and above), sponsored or license-conditioned, based outside the US, or in a 90-day retaliation window.

The pre-termination checklist is completed and filed. It covers: documented reason and evidence; consistency with comparators; recent protected activity, leave, accommodation or complaints; immigration status; export-license conditions; equity and insider status; the local statutory ground and procedure (notice, union notification, enquiry); and final pay readiness.
Approval: Dept Head plus HRBP for individual contributors and managers; CHRO for Directors and above; CEO and Legal for executive officers, including 8-K Item 5.02 assessment for covered officers.

Dismissals for misconduct follow an investigation (ER-02) and the local procedure: domestic enquiry (India), action within 30 days of learning the facts (Taiwan Art. 12), rules adopted by democratic procedure (China), and just-cause proportionality (Canada).
Terminations for performance follow POL-42 and a documented improvement process, except in the US where the at-will exception applies with Legal approval.

The termination meeting is held in person or by video with an HR witness. A script prepared with ER is used, and the employee receives a written notice in a language they understand stating the effective date, entitlements and next steps.
Final pay is ready at the meeting where the law requires immediate payment (e.g., California) and otherwise meets local deadlines. Statutory amounts are never made conditional on signing a release.
System and site access removal is timed to the meeting (OF-06), and device recovery and the exit certification follow POL-55.
Any separation agreement follows POL-54 release standards, including protected-rights carve-outs.
For sponsored workers, Immigration completes the required steps (e.g., for H-1B: USCIS notice, LCA withdrawal and an offer of return transportation) and advises on grace periods.
The reason recorded and given is truthful and consistent across the termination letter, HRIS, unemployment responses and references.
No termination decision is made or recommended solely by an automated tool (POL-50).
Terminations are reviewed each quarter by HR Analytics for adverse impact and by ER for process quality.
policies.sampleLanguage: Ending employment. [Company] ends employment only for legitimate, documented business reasons and in accordance with the law and procedures of the country where the employee works. Before any involuntary termination, the employee's manager must consult their HR Business Partner, and Employee Relations must review the decision, the supporting documentation and any local legal requirements, such as notice periods, required procedures or consultation with employee representatives. Legal will also review terminations involving senior employees, employees on protected leave or with recent complaints, sponsored employees and employees outside the United States. Terminations will be communicated respectfully, in private, with an HR representative present, and the employee will receive written confirmation of the effective date, final pay, benefits, equity treatment and any statutory documents. Final pay and statutory entitlements will be paid on time and are never conditional on signing any agreement. Access to systems and premises will be managed to protect both the employee's dignity and [Company]'s information.

roles.duties: Document performance and conduct issues as they arise, consult the HRBP early, and take part in the termination meeting respectfully.
Complete the pre-termination checklist, coordinate approvals, run the meeting with the manager, and make sure documents and final pay are ready.
Review evidence and consistency, make sure local procedures are followed, and handle investigations and appeals.
Review high-risk and non-US terminations, separation agreements, immigration and securities implications.
Calculate and pay final wages, notice pay, severance and leave payouts by the local deadlines.
Remove system access at the agreed time and support device recovery with Security.

countryAddenda.us: Employment is at-will (Montana requires good cause after probation), but check comparators, timing near protected activity (complaints, FMLA/ADA/PWFA requests, whistleblowing, Section 7) and what decision-makers have said; EEOC charge windows are 180/300 days. Pay final wages by the state deadline (e.g., Colorado and Massachusetts immediately on involuntary termination; New York and Illinois by the next payday), give state separation and UI notices, and send the COBRA qualifying-event notice. For H-1B workers, notify USCIS, withdraw the LCA and offer return transportation.
countryAddenda.us-ca: Pay all wages, accrued vacation and meal/rest premiums immediately at termination, including remote terminations (LC 201, 203; up to 30 days' waiting-time penalties). Give the UI Code 1089 notice and DE 2320 pamphlet, and the HIPP and COBRA/Cal-COBRA notices. Adverse action within 90 days of protected activity is presumed retaliatory (LC 98.6, 1102.5), and a human decision-maker must own any decision with ADS input.
countryAddenda.ca: There is no at-will employment. Without cause, give ESA notice or pay (Ontario up to 8 weeks; BC CLOS up to 8 weeks) plus Ontario ESA severance (1 week per year, max 26, at 5+ years with C$2.5M+ global payroll), and common-law reasonable notice unless an enforceable clause limits entitlement (Waksdale; Baker v. Van Dolder's, 2026 ONCA 568). Just cause is a high proportionality bar (McKinley). Issue the ROE within 5 calendar days after the pay period, and make sure equity terms meet the Matthews standard.
countryAddenda.in: Non-workers may be terminated on contractual notice or pay in lieu with a non-stigmatic letter, plus Karnataka Shops Act s.39 notice (1 month for 6+ months' service, except for misconduct). Misconduct dismissals need a domestic enquiry (charge sheet, hearing, report, second show-cause, reasoned order), and 'workers' can seek reinstatement before the Industrial Tribunal, so mutual separation is the default tool. Pay the full and final settlement within 2 working days and gratuity within 30 days; there can be no dismissal during maternity absence.
countryAddenda.tw: Termination needs either an LSA Art. 11 ground, with notice of 10/20/30 days, severance of 0.5 month per year (capped at 6 months) within 30 days and the Employment Services Act Art. 33 notification 10 days before separation, or an Art. 12 ground used within 30 days of learning the facts. Courts apply the last-resort principle. No termination during maternity leave or occupational-injury treatment. Issue service and involuntary-separation certificates, and withdraw insurance on the last day.
countryAddenda.cn: Terminate only on the LCL Arts. 36, 39, 40, 41 or 44 grounds, with evidence, and notify the union before any unilateral termination (Art. 43). Art. 40 requires 30 days' notice or one month's pay plus N (for high earners, capped at 3x the local average wage and 12 years). Respect the Art. 42 protected categories: wrongful termination costs 2N or reinstatement. Issue the termination certificate at termination and transfer the file and social insurance within 15 days; mutual termination (Art. 36) is the market norm.

decisions: Offer severance for individual performance terminations in the US, in exchange for a release? (It reduces litigation risk at modest cost, but must be applied consistently.)
Make mutual separation the default in India, Taiwan and China? (It avoids statutory-ground disputes but costs more than statutory minimums.)
Require an HR witness always, or only for higher-risk cases?
Standards for remote (video) termination meetings, and timing of access removal?
Working notice, pay in lieu or garden leave for notice periods in Canada and Asia?
pitfalls: Treating Canada, India, Taiwan or China as at-will.
Missing California's immediate final pay in remote terminations.
Not notifying the union before a unilateral termination in China.
Relying on an Ontario termination clause that the Waksdale reasoning makes void.
Skipping the H-1B bona fide termination steps, which leaves back-wage liability running.
policies.training: Managers: termination and documentation training on appointment. HRBPs and ER: annual country-procedure training. Employees: acknowledgment of the handbook at hire.
