policies.name: Severance & Reduction in Force
policies.owner: HR (Employee Relations and Total Rewards) with Legal
policies.approver: CHRO + General Counsel + CFO for each RIF plan; Compensation Committee for executive severance plans; Board informed of material restructurings
policies.audience: Executives and HR/Legal/Finance teams planning restructurings; affected employees; managers delivering notifications
policies.purpose: Plan and carry out reductions in force and severance lawfully, fairly and humanely across all countries. This covers objective selection with adverse-impact review, statutory notices and consultation, consistent packages exchanged for enforceable releases, and coordination with securities disclosure, immigration and trade-secret protection.
keyProvisions: Every RIF has a written business case and organization design (PL-04), approved by the CEO, CFO and CHRO. Work on it is done under legal privilege, and the need-to-know list is kept by Legal.

Selection uses objective, documented criteria within defined decisional units (e.g., role elimination, skills needed for the future roadmap, documented performance). Before decisions are final, HR Analytics runs a privileged adverse-impact analysis by age, sex, race or ethnicity, national origin and visa status, and checks for employees on leave or with pending complaints.
Open roles are reviewed for redeployment before selection is final. Redeployment offers are documented (and required in the Taiwan and China analysis).

All statutory notices and consultations are completed before notifications take effect: federal and state WARN and Cal-WARN; Ontario Form 1 and BC group notice; India retrenchment notice and Re-skilling Fund payment; Taiwan Art. 33 and Mass Redundancy Protection Act filings; China Art. 41 explanation and labor bureau report.

The US standard package is [2] weeks' base per year of service plus a base amount of [4] weeks, with a minimum of [8] weeks and a maximum of [26] weeks, plus a COBRA premium subsidy for the severance period and [1-3] months of outplacement. Other countries use the country schedule, which always includes statutory amounts in full.
Statutory entitlements are paid unconditionally. Only amounts above them are offered in exchange for a release.

Releases carry a protected-rights carve-out (SEC Rule 21F-17, NLRA Section 7 for non-supervisors, EEOC and state agencies, Speak Out Act). There is no waiver of SEC award rights and no no-rehire clause where prohibited, and they include the local formalities (OWBPA, California Civil Code 1542 and Gov Code 12964.5, local language).
Equity follows the plan terms. Any acceleration is a program approved by the Compensation Committee, not negotiated case by case. Canadian common-law exposure (Matthews) is modelled before decisions.
Immigration reviews the effect on sponsored employees and pending petitions (the Sept 18, 2026 US executive order weighs recent layoffs in H-1B adjudication) and takes the required termination steps.

Communications are sequenced with Legal and Investor Relations for any 8-K or earnings disclosure and Reg FD. Notifications happen in private meetings with written packages, and there are no mass-email terminations.
Access removal and the trade-secret exit protocol (POL-55) are coordinated with notification timing, with extra forensic review for roles with Restricted or export-controlled access.
Executive severance and change-in-control benefits follow the Executive Severance Plan, with 409A-compliant payment timing and a best-net 280G approach (no excise tax gross-ups).
After each RIF, the team reviews selection outcomes, cost, legal issues and survivor engagement, and Legal keeps the records under privilege.
policies.sampleLanguage: Reductions in force. When business needs require [Company] to eliminate positions, we will make selection decisions using objective, job-related criteria applied consistently within defined groups, and we will consider available redeployment opportunities before employment ends. We will comply with all notice, consultation and reporting requirements that apply where affected employees work, including advance notice to employees, employee representatives and government authorities where required. Affected employees will be told in a private meeting and will receive written information about their last day, final pay, benefits, equity treatment and any severance offered. All pay and benefits required by law will be provided regardless of whether an employee signs any agreement. Additional severance benefits under [Company]'s severance program are offered in exchange for a release of claims, with a reasonable period to consider the agreement and to seek advice. No agreement will prevent an employee from reporting possible violations of law to, or communicating with, any government agency, or from receiving an award from a government agency.

roles.duties: Sponsors the RIF plan, approves the packages and communications, and makes sure selection and notice processes are complete.
Directs privileged analysis, maps notice and consultation duties, drafts releases and disclosures, and advises on immigration and securities issues.
Runs privileged adverse-impact and leave-status checks on proposed selections and documents the results.
Models severance, equity and Matthews exposure costs, and sets up the Compensation Committee-approved programs.
Prepares managers, delivers notifications with them, and supports affected employees and those who remain.
Approves the business case and restructuring accruals (ASC 420/712), and tracks cost.

countryAddenda.us: Federal WARN (100+ employees) requires 60 days' notice of plant closings (50+ at a site) or mass layoffs (500+, or 50-499 and 33%), aggregated over 90 days. State mini-WARN laws add more: NY 90 days (50+ employees, 25+ losses; the form asks about AI or automation), NJ 90 days plus mandatory severance of 1 week per year, IL 60 days at 75+ employees, WA 60 days at 50+. OWBPA group releases need 45 days to consider, 7 to revoke and decisional-unit disclosures, and RIF timing must be coordinated with H-1B filings (the Sept 18, 2026 EO weighs layoffs).
countryAddenda.us-ca: Cal-WARN (establishments with 75+ employees) requires 60 days' notice for 50+ layoffs within 30 days regardless of percentage, a relocation of 100+ miles or a termination, sent to employees, EDD, the Local Workforce Development Board and local officials, with the SB 617 content (rapid-response coordination, board contacts, CalFresh). Penalties include up to 60 days' back pay and $500 a day. Releases need a Civil Code 1542 waiver, the Gov Code 12964.5 carve-out and 5 business days to consult an attorney, with no no-rehire clause, and final pay is due immediately. SB 951 (pending) would add disclosures for AI-driven layoffs.
countryAddenda.ca: Ontario mass termination (50+ at an establishment within 4 weeks): 8/12/16 weeks' notice by size, with Form 1 filed with the Director (notice is not effective until received) and posted, plus 3 unpaid job-seeking days (since 27 Nov 2025) and ESA severance. BC group termination (50+ within 2 months): 8/12/16 weeks' notice to employees, any union and the Minister, on top of CLOS. Common-law notice applies to every employee, and releases need consideration beyond ESA amounts (settlements typically land at 60-80% of the realistic common-law range).
countryAddenda.in: Retrenching 'workers' with 1+ year's service requires: 1 month's notice with reasons or pay in lieu; 15 days' average pay per completed year; 15 days' wages to the Worker Re-skilling Fund within 10 days; notice to the appropriate government; last-in-first-out within each category unless reasons are recorded; and a 1-year re-employment preference (IR Code ss.70-72, 83). Chapter X prior permission applies only to factories, mines and plantations with 300+ workers. Market packages are notice pay plus 0.5-1 month's base per year of service, with a floor of 2-3 months.
countryAddenda.tw: Individual redundancy under LSA Art. 11(2)/(4) needs redeployment to be considered, notice, severance within 30 days and the Employment Services Act Art. 33 notification 10 days before separation. Where Mass Redundancy Protection Act thresholds are met within 60 days (e.g., over 1/5 of staff or 80 in a day at sites with 500+), a plan must go to the authority, the union or representatives and employees 60 days in advance, followed by negotiation. The market package is statutory amounts plus 1-3 months' ex gratia, framed as a mutual separation.
countryAddenda.cn: Art. 41 economic layoffs (20+ employees, or 10%+ of the workforce) are limited to statutory circumstances. They need a 30-day explanation to the union or all employees and a labor bureau report (in Shanghai, worker representatives are notified 30 days before filing, from Aug 2026), with priority retention and a 6-month rehire preference. Most MNCs instead run voluntary mutual-termination programs at N+1 to N+3; respect the Art. 42 protected categories and pay untaken leave at 300%.

decisions: US severance formula: service-based, level-based, or both, with what floor and cap?
How long to subsidize COBRA, and whether to pay a pro-rata bonus?
Working notice, pay in lieu or garden leave during WARN and statutory notice periods?
Offer a voluntary separation program before involuntary selection? (It reduces litigation risk and helps morale, but risks losing key talent. It is the default in China.)
Accelerate vesting of equity that would vest within 1-3 months as a program benefit?
Outplacement scope and duration by level?
pitfalls: Missing OWBPA group disclosures, which makes ADEA releases void.
Thinking Cal-WARN needs a percentage threshold. It is triggered by 50+ layoffs within 30 days regardless of percentage.
Giving Ontario mass-termination notice before Form 1 has reached the Director.
Using a China Art. 41 layoff without statutory grounds instead of a voluntary mutual-termination program.
Missing Taiwan's 10-day Art. 33 notification or the Indian Re-skilling Fund payment.
Timing layoffs without considering pending H-1B petitions and LCAs.
policies.training: Managers delivering notifications: a briefing before each RIF. HR, Legal and Finance planners: a RIF playbook review every year.

policies.name: Return of Property & Post-Employment Obligations
policies.owner: HR Operations (Offboarding) with Security and Legal
policies.audience: All departing employees and contractors; managers, IT, Security, Payroll and Legal
policies.purpose: Recover all company property and information, cut off access at the right moment, and remind departing employees of obligations that continue after they leave (confidentiality, IP, export control, national-security and insider-trading rules). All of this must happen without unlawful wage deductions and without relying on restraints that are void where the employee works.
keyProvisions: The offboarding checklist (OF-06) starts when notice is given. All property is returned by the last working day: laptops, phones, badges, security tokens, lab notebooks, evaluation boards, samples, test equipment, documents and any storage media.
Remote employees return property through prepaid tracked shipping or courier pickup arranged by IT within 5 business days of their last day.

Access removal: at the time of the meeting for involuntary terminations; at notice for high-risk departures, with duties adjusted; and by the end of the last working day otherwise. Identity deprovisioning finishes within 1 hour of the trigger.

For high-risk departures (to competitors, foundries, PRC-linked companies, customers, or employees with Restricted or export-controlled access), Security reviews DLP, repository and cloud activity for the previous 30-90 days and may forensically image devices. Findings go to Legal.

Every departing employee signs an exit certification confirming return of property and deletion of company information from personal devices and accounts. Where personal devices hold company data, deletion is supervised or done remotely by container wipe.

Legal sends a reminder of continuing obligations: confidentiality and invention assignment; export-control and TCP duties; the Taiwan National Security Act and travel-approval duties for covered personnel; any lawful non-solicit or compensated non-compete; and insider-trading restrictions until the policy says they end. The reminder never mentions restraints that are void where the employee works.

[Company] never withholds final pay or statutory amounts, and never deducts the value of unreturned property, except where local law expressly allows it with written authorization. It recovers property or its value by demand or legal action.

Trade Compliance is notified of exits by employees with export-license conditions to update records and meet license provisos, and US-person engineers joining PRC fabs are reminded of their personal EAR 744.6 obligations.
China non-compete activation or release, and Taiwan non-compete compensation, are decided and communicated in writing at exit.
Personal items left on site or in devices are returned or made available for collection for 30 days, after which they are disposed of.
Email accounts are disabled with a 30-day auto-reply that directs contacts to the manager. The manager reviews the mailbox only under Legal's rules, and data is kept under POL-49 and any legal hold.
Where a separation agreement includes cooperation or non-disparagement terms, they carry the protected-rights carve-out and local limits.
policies.sampleLanguage: Returning property and your continuing obligations. Before your last day, you must return all [Company] property, including laptops, phones, badges, security tokens, evaluation boards, samples, laboratory notebooks and documents, and any copies of [Company] information in any format. If you work remotely, IT will provide prepaid shipping. You will be asked to sign a certification that you have returned all property and have deleted any [Company] information from personal devices and accounts; if you are unsure how to do this, IT will help. Your obligations to protect [Company]'s confidential information and to assign inventions continue after your employment ends, as do obligations under export-control laws and, where applicable, other laws protecting critical technologies. Legal will send you a written reminder of the obligations that apply to you. [Company] will pay your final wages and statutory amounts on time and will not withhold them because of unreturned property. Nothing in this policy limits your right to communicate with any government agency or to discuss your terms and conditions of employment as permitted by law.

roles.duties: Return all property and information, sign the exit certification, and honor their continuing obligations.
Start offboarding promptly, flag high-risk departures, and collect team-held assets and knowledge.
Remove access on time, manage device returns and container wipes, and preserve data under legal hold.
Run activity reviews and forensics for high-risk exits, and escalate findings to Legal.
Send tailored reminder letters, decide on non-compete activation, and handle recovery actions and misappropriation responses.
Update export-license records and meet license provisos when license-conditioned employees leave.

countryAddenda.us: Rely on NDAs, invention assignment and narrow non-solicits, and do not threaten to enforce void non-competes (MN, ND, OK, WY, CA; WA from 30 Jun 2027, with notices due by 1 Oct 2027). Many states restrict deducting the cost of unreturned equipment from wages (e.g., NY Labor Law 193). Revoke EAR-controlled access, update license records, and remind US-person engineers joining PRC fabs of their personal EAR 744.6 obligations.
countryAddenda.us-ca: Do not withhold final pay or deduct for unreturned property (LC 221; Wage Order 4 section 8); recover by demand or legal action. Remind departing employees of their CUTSA confidentiality duties, but do not enforce non-competes or non-solicits (B&P 16600.5) or seek repayment of costs (AB 692). The exit certification must include the Gov Code 12964.5 carve-out.
countryAddenda.ca: Remind the employee of confidentiality, invention assignment, the moral-rights waiver and any narrow non-solicit; Ontario non-competes are void below the C-suite. Deductions for unreturned property need written authorization and cannot reduce ESA entitlements. Log exits of employees with export-controlled technology under the TCP.
countryAddenda.in: Collect devices and badges, get written confirmation of return, remind the employee of continuing duties and remove access on the last working day. Do not make the full and final settlement (due in 2 working days) conditional on clearance, and keep any recovery within Code on Wages s.18 limits. Rely on garden leave, confidentiality and injunctions, because post-exit non-competes are void, and return original documents.
countryAddenda.tw: Recover devices, remove access, obtain a written return and non-retention certification, and review recent downloads under the disclosed monitoring policy. Remind the employee of Trade Secrets Act and National Security Act exposure and of any continuing travel-approval duty for core key technology personnel. If an Art. 9-1 non-compete is enforced, pay at least 50% of the average monthly wage as compensation, and make no deductions from wages (Art. 26).
countryAddenda.cn: Complete the handover checklist (devices, lab notebooks, confidential data, deletion from personal devices), because economic compensation is due on handover completion (LCL Art. 50). Decide at exit whether to activate the non-compete (monthly compensation and scope notice) or release it; releasing it during the restriction costs 3 extra months' compensation. Update the SAFE Circular 7 registration for departing equity participants.

decisions: Which departures trigger forensic imaging: role-based (e.g., all design engineers with Restricted access) or risk-signal-based?
Remove access at notice for all departures to competitors, or case by case?
Allow departing employees to keep phones or numbers after company data is wiped?
Send notice letters to new employers about continuing obligations? (This can help deter misuse but carries interference and California-specific risk. Legal decides case by case.)
Activate paid non-competes in China and Taiwan only for a named list of critical roles?
pitfalls: Deducting laptop costs from final pay, or delaying final pay until property comes back.
Removing access late for engineers going to competitors or foundries.
Reminder letters that cite non-competes that are void where the employee works.
Missing the China non-compete activation or release decision at exit.
Failing to pay Taiwan non-compete compensation, which voids the restraint.
policies.training: The exit certification is signed at departure. Managers: offboarding responsibilities briefing on appointment. IT and Security: yearly review of the offboarding runbook.

policies.name: References & Employment Verification
policies.audience: All managers and employees; People Ops; former employees and third parties requesting verification
policies.purpose: Answer reference and employment-verification requests consistently, truthfully and lawfully, and issue statutory service or termination certificates on time. This limits defamation, privacy and discrimination risk and treats former employees fairly.
keyProvisions: Only People Ops, or its authorized verification vendor, answers reference and employment-verification requests on behalf of [Company]. All requests are routed to People Ops.

The standard verification is dates of employment and last job title. Salary and other details are disclosed only with the employee's written consent, or where the law requires it (e.g., government or court orders).

Managers may not give references on behalf of [Company]. A personal reference may be given only with People Ops approval, must be clearly marked as personal, must be truthful, and may not refer to protected characteristics, leave, accommodations or complaints.

Statutory documents are issued on time whatever the reason for leaving: service certificates (Taiwan on request; Karnataka within 7 days of request), China termination certificates at termination, Canadian ROEs, US state service letters on request, and relieving and experience letters (India).
Statutory certificates state only the facts the law requires and never include adverse remarks the employee did not ask for.

Where serious misconduct was substantiated (e.g., workplace violence or harassment findings), Legal decides whether and how any disclosure is made. No false or misleading statement is ever given in either direction.
Requests from government agencies, security-clearance investigators, courts or immigration authorities go to Legal or Security.
Rehire eligibility is recorded in Darwinbox (OF-10) and not disclosed outside [Company], except as a yes/no answer where the former employee has consented.
Verification requests are answered within 3 business days. Mortgage, visa and background-check verifications use the approved vendor or template.
Verification vendors are engaged under contracts that cover FCRA or local consumer-reporting obligations, data security and consent.
When [Company] seeks references on candidates, it does so only with the candidate's consent and, for vendor checks, under POL-17.
A log of disclosures (requester, date, information released, consent) is kept for 3 years.
policies.sampleLanguage: References and employment verification. All requests for references or verification of employment about current or former employees must be referred to People Ops at [contact] or to our authorized verification provider. In response to such requests, [Company] will confirm only dates of employment and most recent job title, unless the employee has given written consent to release additional information, such as salary, or the law requires otherwise. Managers and other employees may not provide references on behalf of [Company]. With People Ops' approval, you may provide a personal reference for a former colleague, but it must be clearly identified as your personal view, must be truthful, and must not refer to protected characteristics, leave, accommodations or complaints. [Company] will issue all certificates and letters required by law, such as service or termination certificates, within the required time and regardless of the reason employment ended; these documents will contain only the information the law requires unless the employee requests otherwise. Questions from government agencies or courts must be referred to Legal.

roles.duties: Answers verifications, issues statutory certificates on time, keeps the disclosure log and manages the verification vendor.
Route requests to People Ops, give personal references only when approved, and never discuss protected matters.
Decides on disclosures in misconduct cases and answers government, court and clearance-related requests.
Give written consent for any expanded disclosures they want, and ask for statutory certificates as needed.
The verification provider releases only the authorized data, meets FCRA and data-security duties, and logs releases.

countryAddenda.us: Adopt neutral references (dates and title). Some states require a service letter on request stating the reason for separation (e.g., Minnesota within 10 working days of request; Missouri, Kansas, Nevada; verify). Third-party verification vendors are consumer reporting agencies under the FCRA. Disclose salary only with the employee's written consent.
countryAddenda.us-ca: Truthful, good-faith references to prospective employers are privileged (Civil Code 47(c)), but misrepresentations meant to stop someone getting a job are prohibited (LC 1050-1053). Settlements with employees who filed good-faith claims cannot bar rehire except in limited cases (CCP 1002.5). Former employees may request their personnel file (30 days) and payroll records (21 days).
countryAddenda.ca: There is no statutory service letter, but the Record of Employment must be issued electronically within 5 calendar days after the end of the pay period with the interruption of earnings. References must be accurate to avoid defamation or negligent-misrepresentation claims. BC PIPA and Quebec Law 25 limit disclosure of personal information without notice or consent (verify the BC rules on disclosing references).
countryAddenda.in: In Karnataka, issue a service certificate within 7 days of request (Shops Act amendment, Sep 2026), and do not keep original certificates. Relieving and experience letters are market standard and should not be withheld to force the notice period to be served. Answers to background-verification requests need the former employee's consent (SPDI Rules now; DPDP from May 2027).
countryAddenda.tw: Issue a certificate of service on request (LSA Art. 19) stating dates and position; it may not include adverse remarks the employee did not ask for. For Art. 11/13 terminations and employer-initiated mutual separations, issue the involuntary separation certificate so the employee can claim Employment Insurance.
countryAddenda.cn: Issue a termination certificate at termination stating the contract term, termination date, position and years of service (LCL Art. 50; Implementing Regulations Art. 24), without negative reasons; failing to issue it where this causes loss attracts damages (Art. 89). Answer reference checks only with the former employee's consent (PIPL Art. 13). New employers often ask for the certificate to avoid joint liability (LCL Art. 91).

decisions: Confirm salary on request with consent, or never? (Consent-based confirmation helps former employees with mortgages but adds administration.)
Share rehire eligibility externally (yes/no with consent), or never?
Allow manager personal references, and with what approval?
Use a third-party verification service (e.g., The Work Number) or handle it in-house?
How to respond when a former employee's substantiated serious misconduct could create a safety risk for a new employer? (Legal decides case by case.)
pitfalls: Managers giving informal company references on LinkedIn or by phone.
Withholding service certificates, relieving letters or termination certificates as leverage.
Disclosing the reason for leaving, medical leave or complaints without consent.
Statutory certificates that include negative remarks (Taiwan, China).
Missing the Canadian ROE deadline.
policies.training: Managers: guidance on the reference policy on appointment. People Ops: annual training on statutory certificates and consent requirements.

policies.name: Accessibility & Inclusion
policies.owner: HR (Talent and Inclusion) with People Ops and Facilities
policies.review: Annual; Ontario multi-year accessibility plan reviewed at least every 5 years (verify)
policies.audience: All employees, applicants and managers; HR Technology, Facilities and Procurement
policies.purpose: Build an accessible, inclusive workplace where everyone can compete and contribute on merit. Meet statutory accessibility and disability-employment duties (AODA, ADA, India RPwD, Taiwan and China disability quotas), and keep inclusion programs open to all and consistent with current US anti-discrimination enforcement.
keyProvisions: [Company] provides equal employment opportunity and an accessible workplace. All inclusion programs are open to every employee regardless of race, sex, national origin or any other protected characteristic.

Digital accessibility: the careers site, internal HR systems and learning content meet WCAG 2.1 AA as company standard (Ontario public websites at least WCAG 2.0 AA). Procurement requires accessibility conformance information for new HR technology.
Physical accessibility: new or renovated sites are assessed for accessible entrances, washrooms, lactation and quiet rooms. Lab accessibility adjustments are made with EHS.
Communications and documents are available in accessible formats on request, within 10 business days or sooner where the law requires.
Recruitment: every posting and interview invitation offers accommodation, assessments have accessible alternatives, and AI tools are reviewed for accessibility (POL-50).
Accommodations follow POL-36, including individual accommodation plans and individualized emergency response information where needed.
Employee resource groups, mentoring, sponsorship, fellowships and internships have open eligibility. No compensation metric, hiring target or slate requirement is based on protected characteristics.

Voluntary self-identification data is collected only where lawful. It is stored separately from personnel files and used only in aggregate for statutory reporting (e.g., California pay data, BC pay transparency, US federal contractor duties if applicable) and privileged analysis.

Statutory disability-employment duties are met: Taiwan quota (1% at 67+ employees), China disabled persons' employment security fund or ratio, and the India RPwD equal opportunity policy and liaison officer.
Training: accessibility and inclusive-leadership training for managers, and AODA training for all Ontario staff.
Public statements about workforce inclusion (10-K human capital section, sustainability report, careers site) are checked by Legal against the programs actually operated.
Workforce composition and accessibility metrics are reviewed every year by the CHRO. Analyses of potential disparities are done under privilege.
policies.sampleLanguage: Accessibility and inclusion. [Company] is committed to a workplace in which everyone can compete and contribute on the basis of merit, and in which people with disabilities have equal access to employment, information and facilities. We design our careers site, HR systems and learning content to recognized accessibility standards, and we will provide information in an accessible format on request. Applicants may request accommodation at any stage of the recruitment process, and employees may request workplace adjustments at any time under our Reasonable Accommodation Policy. Our employee resource groups, mentoring and development programs are open to all employees. Any demographic information you choose to provide is voluntary, is stored separately from your personnel file and is used only in aggregate for legally required reporting and to evaluate the fairness of our practices. We meet the disability employment and accessibility requirements that apply in each country where we operate, and we train managers to lead inclusively and to respond appropriately to accommodation requests.

roles.duties: Request accessible formats or accommodations when needed, and take part in inclusive practices and training.
Make sure their teams can take part, respond to accessibility requests, and apply merit-based, consistent decisions.
Owns the policy, the program design (open to all), self-identification data handling and statutory filings (AODA report, quota filings).
Assess and improve physical accessibility of sites and emergency evacuation arrangements.
Reviews programs and public statements against anti-discrimination law and federal contractor duties, and advises on quota compliance.
Produces aggregate and privileged analyses and statutory reports.

countryAddenda.us: ADA Title I applies at 15+ employees. If [Company] is a federal contractor, Section 503 changes effective 21 Sep 2026 remove the CC-305 self-ID form, the 7% utilization goal and disability data collection, and raise the coverage threshold to $20K (verify the remaining 503 duties). Keep ERGs, mentoring and internships open to all: demographic-restricted programs and diversity-linked bonuses create Title VII exposure and, for contractors, False Claims Act exposure (IBM $17M, Apr 2026; EO 14173 certifications).
countryAddenda.us-ca: FEHA (5+ employees) protects disability and requires the interactive process. Translate EEO and harassment policies into any language spoken by 10%+ of a facility's workforce (2 CCR 11023). Store pay-data demographics separately (SB 464) and file the CRD pay data report by the second Wednesday of May (100+ employees).
countryAddenda.ca: AODA (IASR) requires documented accessibility policies and a multi-year plan (50+ employees); training for all staff on the IASR and Human Rights Code; accessible recruitment and accommodation notices; individual accommodation plans and a return-to-work process (50+); individualized emergency response information; and WCAG 2.0 AA public websites (50+). Organizations with 20+ Ontario employees file an accessibility compliance report every 3 years, next due 31 Dec 2026. In BC, employers with 50+ BC employees publish the pay transparency report by 1 Nov 2026.
countryAddenda.in: Under the RPwD Act, publish an equal opportunity policy (s.21), appoint a liaison officer at 20+ employees, and provide reasonable accommodation and accessible facilities. A transgender equal opportunity policy and complaint officer, and an HIV complaints officer at 100+, are also required. Code on Wages s.3 bars gender discrimination, including against transgender persons, in pay and recruitment.
countryAddenda.tw: Private employers with 67+ employees must employ persons with disabilities equal to at least 1% of headcount (minimum 1), or pay the shortfall (the monthly minimum wage for each missing person) into the disability employment fund (People with Disabilities Rights Protection Act Arts. 38, 43). Employment Services Act Art. 5 bars discrimination, with fines of NT$300,000-1,500,000.
countryAddenda.cn: Employers must employ persons with disabilities at a locally set ratio (national floor 1.5%) or pay the Disabled Persons' Employment Security Fund to the local tax bureau (Regulations on the Employment of Persons with Disabilities; verify the Shanghai and Shenzhen ratios and any current fee-reduction policy). The Employment Promotion Law bars discrimination on grounds of gender, ethnicity, religion, disability, carrier status or rural origin.

decisions: Publish workforce demographic data voluntarily after the EEO-1 rescission proposal? (Transparency is valued by some investors, but disclosures must be accurate and legally reviewed.)
Collect voluntary self-ID outside jurisdictions that require it, and for which uses?
Fund ERGs centrally with open-membership rules, or not at all?
Accessibility standard for internal tools: WCAG 2.1 AA or 2.2 AA?
Meet the Taiwan quota through hiring and partnerships, or accept the levy? (Hiring is preferred, and the levy is the backstop.)
Include inclusion or accessibility goals in executive pay? (Avoid demographic targets; process goals such as accessibility conformance are lower risk.)
pitfalls: Demographic-restricted fellowships, internships or ERGs, and diversity-linked bonuses in the US.
Public DEI statements that no longer match the programs actually operated.
Missing the Ontario AODA compliance report (next due 31 Dec 2026).
Ignoring the Taiwan quota levy or the China security fund assessments.
AI assessments and HR tools that are inaccessible to screen-reader users.
policies.training: Managers: inclusive leadership and accessibility training on appointment and every 2 years. Ontario: AODA training for all staff at hire. Acknowledgment at hire.
